第15根K线也是一次外包K线做空入场，针对的是跌破第11根和第13根K线之后的回调。它尤其好，因为有被套的多头买入了那两K线多头反转，以为它是向下跌破第11根和第13根K线双底的突破失败。每当一次跌破双底的突破试图反转向上并失败时，它就是一个楔形失败形态，往往有大约一个等距运动的下跌空间。双底构成向下推进的前两次，跌破双底则是向下的第三次推进。〔译注：原文此句的 Since 从句没有主句与之呼应；译文按文意把结论补出。〕由于从第14根K线起有连续四根空头趋势K线向下，聪明的交易者会想先等到一次更高低点的回调再考虑做多。


> Bar 15 was also an outside bar short entry for the pullback following the breakout below bars 11 and 13. It was especially good because there were trapped longs who had bought the two bar-bull reversal, thinking that it was a failed breakout below the bar 11 and bar 13 double bottom. Whenever a breakout below a double bottom tries to reverse up and fails, it is a failed wedge pattern and often has about a measured move down. The double bottom creates the first two pushes down, and the breakout below the double bottom is the third push down. Since there were four bear trend bars down from bar 14, and smart traders would have wanted a higher low pullback before going long.


第16根K线是跌破昨日第2根K线摆动低点之后的低2回调。


> Bar 16 was a low 2 pullback after the breakout below yesterday's bar 2 swing low.


这些交易中有很多都是很小的剥头皮，不应成为大多数交易者的重点。它们的意义在于展示了一种常见的市场行为。交易者应当把精力集中在更大的转折点上，比如第4、7、9、12根K线。


> Many of these trades were tiny scalps and should not be the focus of the majority of traders. Their significance is that they illustrate a common behavior. Traders should concentrate on trading the bigger turning points, like bars 4, 7, 9, and 12.


![图 5.7](figures/fig-05-07.jpg)


**图 5.7　突破失败**


如图 5.7所示，在 EWZ（iShares MSCI 巴西基金 ETF）这张60分钟图上，有多次来自牛旗和熊旗的突破失败。一旦先有一段趋势，随后出现一面旗形，而它的突破失败并跟着出现反转，那面旗形就是这段趋势的末端旗形。


> As shown in Figure 5.7, there were several failed breakouts from bull and bear flags on this 60 minute chart of EWZ, the iShares MSCI Brazil Fund ETF. Once there is a trend and then a flag that has a breakout that fails and is followed by a reversal, that flag is the final flag of the trend.


一面末端牛旗可以在一个更高的高点之后向下反转，比如第3根和第9根K线处；也可以在更低的高点之后向下反转，比如第5根和第10根K线处。一面末端熊旗可以在一个更低的低点之后向上反转，比如第6、11、13根K线处；也可以在更高的低点之后向上反转，比如第1、8、14根K线处。


> A final bull flag can reverse down after a higher high, like at bars 3 and 9 or after a lower high, like at bars 5 and 10. A final bear flag can reverse up after a lower low, like at bars 6, 11, and 13, or after a higher low, like at bars 1, 8, and 14.


![图 5.8](figures/fig-05-08.jpg)


**图 5.8　末端旗形**


有时末端熊旗也正是下一段多头趋势向上的第一段（见图 5.8）。塔塔汽车（TTM）这家印度车厂的这张120分钟图上，有一面熊旗在第5根K线结束，并成为这波抛售的末端旗形。第6根K线的更高低点带来一波急速上涨到第7根K线，它位于第5根K线更低的高点之上，因此是一个更高的高点，是多头力度的信号。正如第3册中末端旗形那一节所讨论的，从末端熊旗的突破不一定要跌到空头低点之下。


> Sometimes the final bear flag is also the first leg up of the next bull trend (see Figure 5.8). This 120 minute chart of Tata Motors Ltd. (TTM), a carmaker in India, had a bear flag that ended at bar 5 and became the final flag of the sell-off. The bar 6 higher low led to a sharp rally to bar 7, which was above the bar 5 lower high and was therefore a higher high and a sign of bull strength. As discussed in the section on final flags in book 3, the breakout from the final bear flag does not have to fall below the bear low.


![图 5.9](figures/fig-05-09.jpg)


**图 5.9　双底**


如图 5.9所示，5分钟 Emini 小型合约处于强空头趋势中，一路下跌到第1根K线，随后是一面低动能、圆弧状的熊旗，在第2根K线结束。接着是一波急速抛售跌到第3根K线，测试了第1根K线的低点。虽然它高了几个最小报价单位，但那是对空头低点的一次双底测试。事后回看，上涨到第2根K线的行情就是末端熊旗、实际上也是新多头趋势向上的第一段，而跌到第3根K线的抛售则是从那段上涨行情开始的突破回调，也是对熊旗的一次突破失败。从第3根K线起的多头急速行情动能如此之强，它一路冲上第2根K线熊旗之上，中间毫无停顿。这通常意味着后面还有空间，所以交易者不应急着把整个多头仓位全部平掉。第一次回调是第4根K线处的一次高1，位置远在第2根K线高点之上。


> As shown in Figure 5.9, the 5 minute Emini was in a strong bear trend down to bar 1, and this was followed by a low-momentum, rounded bear flag that ended at bar 2. Next came a sharp sell-off to bar 3 that tested the bar 1 low. Although it was a couple of ticks higher, it was a double bottom test of the bear low. The rally to bar 2 in hindsight was the final bear flag and effectively the first leg up of the new bull trend, and the sell-off to bar 3 was a breakout pullback from that rally and a failed breakout of the bear flag. The bull spike up from bar 3 had so much momentum that it soared above the bar 2 bear flag without a pause. This usually indicates that there is more to go, so traders should not be quick to exit their entire long positions. The first pullback was a high 1 at bar 4, well above the bar 2 high.


![图 5.10](figures/fig-05-10.jpg)


**图 5.10　末端旗形的斜率可以预示新趋势的斜率**


有时一段趋势的末端旗形，其斜率与反转之后新趋势的斜率大致相同（见图 5.10）。高盛（GS）的这张60分钟图上，从第1根K线到第2根K线有一面末端牛旗，它的大致斜率与反转之后那段空头趋势的斜率差不多。市场知道这波抛售大约会以多快的速度下跌，但那波抛售被最后一个更高的高点短暂打断，走到第3根K线。从第1根K线到第9根K线的整个形态是一条向下的通道，也就是一面牛旗。上涨到第3根K线的行情是一次向上的假突破。


> Sometimes the slope of the final flag of a trend is about the same as the slope of the new trend after the reversal (see Figure 5.10). This 60 minute chart of GS had a final bull flag from bar 1 to bar 2, and its general slope was about the same as the bear trend that followed the reversal. The market knew the approximate rate of descent that the sell-off would have, but the sell-off was briefly interrupted by one final higher high to bar 3. The entire pattern from bar 1 to bar 9 is a downward channel, which is a bull flag. The move up to bar 3 was a false breakout to the upside.


# 第 6 章　缺口

*6. Gaps*


缺口无非是两个价格之间的空当。在日线图、周线图和月线图上，传统缺口很容易辨认。比如，市场正处在多头趋势中，今天的低点高于昨天的高点，那么今天就是向上跳空。这类传统缺口，出现在趋势起点时叫突破缺口（breakaway gap，与 breakout gap 同义）〔译注：作者把 breakaway gap 与 breakout gap 视为同一概念，本书统译为“突破缺口”〕，出现在趋势中段时叫测量缺口，出现在趋势末端时叫衰竭缺口。如果缺口出现在其他时候，比如趋势的急速行情阶段里、或者交易区间内部，就直接叫缺口。通常，交易者要等到看清市场接下来怎么走之后，才能给一个缺口归类。举例来说，日线图上市场正要从交易区间顶部向上突破，而突破那根K线是一根大实体多头趋势K线、其低点高于前一根K线的高点，交易者就会把这个缺口看成强势信号，认为它可能是一段突破缺口。如果这段新的多头趋势又延续了几十根K线，他们回头再看这个缺口，就会确定地称它为突破缺口。反过来，如果市场在几根K线之内就反转向下、进入空头趋势，他们就会称它为衰竭缺口。


> A gap is simply space between two prices. On daily, weekly, and monthly charts, traditional gaps are easy to spot. For example, if the market is in a bull trend and today's low is above the high of yesterday, then today gapped up. These traditional gaps are called breakaway or breakout gaps when they form at the start of a trend, measuring gaps when they are in the middle of a trend, and exhaustion gaps when they form at the end of a trend. When a gap forms at other times, like within the spike phase of a trend or within a trading range, it is simply called a gap. Traders usually cannot classify a gap until after they see what the market does next. For example, if the market is breaking out of the top of a trading range on the daily chart and the breakout bar is a large bull trend bar with a low above the high of the prior bar, traders will see the gap as a sign of strength and will think of it as a potential breakaway gap. If the new bull trend continues for dozens of bars, they will look back at the gap and definitively call it a breakaway gap. If instead the market reverses down into a bear trend within a few bars, they will call it an exhaustion gap.


如果多头趋势走了5根或10根K线左右之后再次出现缺口，交易者会想，这第二个缺口也许正好落在多头趋势的中段。他们会把它看作一个可能的测量缺口，许多交易者会在市场走完一段向上的等距运动后，找机会对多头仓位止盈。这段等距运动的算法是：从多头趋势的底部到缺口中点量出一段高度，再把这个高度加到缺口中点上。这类缺口通常出现在趋势的急速行情阶段，它让交易者有信心以市价单入场、或者在小幅回调中入场，因为他们相信市场会一路走向等距运动目标位。


> If the bull trend goes for five or 10 bars or so and gaps again, traders will think that this second gap might become the middle of the bull trend. They will see it as a possible measuring gap, and many traders will look to take profits on their longs once the market makes a measured move up. The measured move is based on the height from the bottom of the bull trend to the middle of the gap, and this height is added to the middle of the gap. This type of gap usually is in the spike phase of a trend, and it gives traders confidence to enter at the market or on small pullbacks because they believe that the market will work its way toward a measured move target.


当多头趋势已经走了几十根K线、来到某个阻力区、并且开始露出可能反转的迹象之后，交易者就会留意下一个向上缺口，如果还有的话。一旦真的形成，他们会把它看作潜在的衰竭缺口。如果在市场大幅走高之前，价格就回落到缺口之前那根K线的高点下方，交易者会把这看成弱势信号，认为这个缺口可能代表衰竭，而衰竭是买入高潮的一种。他们往往要等到市场至少修正10根K线、走出两段行情之后，才会再次考虑买入。有时衰竭缺口会出现在趋势反转之前，也正因为如此，每当出现可能的衰竭缺口，交易者都会去看整体的价格行为，判断交易者等式是否支持做空。如果真的反转了，那么制造这次反转的那根趋势K线就是一个突破缺口（一根K线可以起缺口的作用），也可能是反方向趋势的起点。


> After the bull trend has gone on for dozens of bars, reaches a resistance area, and is beginning to show signs of a possible reversal, traders will pay attention to the next gap up, if there is one. If one forms, they will see it as a potential exhaustion gap. If, before going much higher, the market trades back down to below the high of the bar before the gap, traders will see that as a sign of weakness and will think that the gap might represent exhaustion, which is a type of buy climax. They will often not look to buy again until after the market has corrected for at least 10 bars and two legs. Sometimes an exhaustion gap forms before a trend reversal, and because of that, whenever there is a possible exhaustion gap, traders will look at the overall price action to see if the trader's equation warrants a short position. If there is a reversal, the trend bar that creates it is then a breakout gap (a bar can function like a gap) and a possible start of a trend in the opposite direction.


因为所有趋势K线都是缺口，交易者就能在盘中图上看到日线图上那些极为常见的传统缺口的盘中版本。假如一段多头趋势来到阻力区、很可能反转向下（反转在第3册讨论），但在此之前还有最后一次突破，那么这根多头趋势K线就可能变成衰竭缺口。这根K线有时是一根收盘价接近高点的超大实体多头趋势K线，偶尔这次最后的突破会由两根超大实体多头趋势K线构成。这是一个潜在的买入高潮，它提醒敏锐的交易者卖出。多头卖出以落袋为安——他们相信市场很可能会向下走两段行情、大约10根K线，这样他们也许能在低得多的位置再次买入。他们同样清楚可能出现衰竭性买入高潮和趋势反转，不愿冒回吐利润的风险。激进空头也清楚这一点，他们会卖出建立空头仓位。如果接下来几根K线之内出现一根强势空头趋势K线、并且始终入场方向翻转向下，那么那根最后的多头趋势K线就成为得到确认的衰竭缺口，而空头趋势K线则成为突破缺口。多头趋势K线之后紧跟空头趋势K线，就是一次高潮反转，也是一次两根K线的反转。如果两根趋势K线之间还有一根或更多K线，这些K线就构成一个岛形顶。这个岛形顶的底部就是空头突破缺口的顶部，而像所有缺口一样，它可能被回测。如果确实被回测、市场再度转下，这次突破回测就形成一个更低的高点。如果最初的反转向下很强势，那么当市场回测岛形顶、并再度转下时，多头和空头都会卖出，因为双方都更有信心市场将下跌大约10根K线或更久。多头卖出是为了锁定利润或减少亏损——如果他们是在多头突破K线形成的过程中在更高处买入的话。空头卖出则是为了建立空头仓位。等市场向下跌了许多根K线，获利了结者（买回空头仓位的空头）会出现，制造出一段回调或者一个交易区间。如果市场随后又出现一根跌破该交易区间的空头趋势K线，那根K线就可能是测量缺口，交易者会设法留住一部分空头仓位，直到市场接近这个目标。


> Because all trend bars are gaps, traders can see intraday equivalents of the traditional gaps that are so common on daily charts. If there is a bull trend that is at a resistance area and is likely to reverse down (reversals are discussed in book 3), but has one final breakout, that bull trend bar might become an exhaustion gap. The bar is sometimes a very large bull trend bar that closes near its high, and occasionally the final breakout will be made of two very large bull trend bars. This is a potential buy climax, and it alerts astute traders to sell. The bulls sell to grab profits, since they believe that the market will likely trade down for a couple of legs and about 10 bars, possibly allowing them to buy again much lower. They also are aware of the possibility of an exhaustive buy climax and trend reversal, and do not want to risk giving back any of their profits. Aggressive bears are aware of this as well, and they will sell to initiate shorts. If a strong bear trend bar forms within the next few bars and the always-in direction flips to down, that final bull trend bar becomes a confirmed exhaustion gap, and the bear trend bar becomes a breakout gap. The bull trend bar followed by the bear trend bar is a climactic reversal, and a two-bar reversal. If there are one or more bars between the two trend bars, those bars form an island top. The bottom of that island top is the top of the bear breakout gap and, like all gaps, might get tested. If it does and the market turns down again, that breakout test forms a lower high. If the initial reversal down was strong, both bulls and bears will sell as the market tests the island top and as the market turns down again, since both are more confident that the market will fall for about 10 or more bars. The bulls will sell to lock in profits or to minimize losses, if they bought higher as the bull trend breakout bars were forming. The bears will sell to initiate shorts. Once the market trades down for many bars, profit takers (bears buying back their shorts) will come in and create a pullback or a trading range. If the market again has a bear trend bar that breaks below the trading range, that bar is then a possible measuring gap, and traders will try to hold onto part of their shorts until the market approaches that target.


随着市场转下，交易者会去看空头K线的强弱。如果有一两根收盘价接近低点的大实体空头趋势K线，交易者会认为始终入场方向可能要翻转为做空。他们会盯着接下来几根K线，看是否形成一根高1买入信号K线。如果形成了，而且（相对这波抛售）比较弱，比如是一根小实体多头十字星或者一根空头K线，那么想在这根K线高点上方做空的交易者会比想买入的更多。记住，这是一段原本多头趋势中的高1回调，但现在交易者预期的是大约10根K线横盘到下跌，所以更多人会考虑在高1买入信号K线的高点上方做空，而不是买入。如果他们判断正确，这个高1买入信号就会失败，形成一个更低的高点。如果反转向下很强势，交易者还会在这个更低的高点下方、以及高1买入信号K线的下方做空。如果市场进一步横盘到下跌，随后形成一个高2买入建仓形态，空头会假设它同样会失败，并在其高点处以及上方挂限价单做空。另一些空头会在高2买入信号K线下方挂止损单做空，因为那里正是买入高2的多头放置保护性止损的位置。这些多头一旦被止损出局，很可能至少两根K线内都不会再考虑买入；多头缺席、空头在场，就可能引发一次空头突破。如果这次突破很弱，多头也许还能造出一个楔形牛旗（高3买入建仓形态）。如果突破很强势，这波下跌很可能至少走出两小段行情，并达到一个等距运动目标，其基准是交易区间的高度（多头的高点到高2多头信号K线的底部）。这样这根突破K线就变成了测量缺口。如果多头在高3处（一个楔形牛旗）成功把市场拉起来，那么这个空头测量缺口就会关闭，变成衰竭缺口。


> As the market turns down, traders will look at the strength of the bear bars. If there are one or two large bear trend bars closing near their lows, traders will assume that the always-in direction might be flipping to short. They will watch the next few bars to see if a high 1 buy signal bar develops. If one forms and it is weak (relative to the selloff), like a small bull doji or a bear bar, more traders will look to short above its high than to buy. Remember, this is a high 1 pullback in what has been a bull trend, but now traders are looking for about 10 bars sideways to down, so more will look to short above the high 1 buy signal bar than to buy. If they are right, the high 1 buy signal will fail and form a lower high. If the reversal down is strong, traders will also short below the lower high and below the high 1 buy signal bar. If the market goes more sideways to down and then forms a high 2 buy setup, the bears will assume that it, too, will fail, and will place limit orders at and above its high to go short. Other bears will place stop orders to go short below the high 2 buy signal bar, because that is where the bulls who bought the high 2 will have their protective stops. Once these bulls get stopped out, they will likely not look to buy again for at least a couple of bars, and the absence of bulls and the presence of bears can lead to a bear breakout. If it is weak, the bulls might be able to create a wedge bull flag (a high 3 buy setup). If the breakout is strong, the move down will likely go for at least a couple of small legs, and reach a measured move, based on the height of the trading range (the bull high to the bottom of the high 2 bull signal bar). The breakout bar then becomes a measuring gap. If the bulls are successful in turning the market up at the high 3 (a wedge bull flag), then the bear measuring gap will close and become an exhaustion gap.


这个过程在每张图上、每天都发生许多次，交易者始终在问自己：这次突破更可能成功（从而把突破K线变成测量缺口），还是更可能失败（从而把制造突破的那根趋势K线变成衰竭缺口）？这些标签并不重要，重要的是它们的含义。这是交易者要做的最重要的一个判断，而且他们每考虑一笔交易都要做一次：在前一根K线的上方和下方，会有更多买方还是更多卖方？只要他们相信买卖力量存在失衡，他们就握有优势。回到刚才那次多头突破：当终于出现一根针对突破失败的信号K线时，交易者会判断这根K线下方会有更多买方还是更多卖方。如果他们认为突破很强，就会假设买方更多，于是在这根K线下方买入。另一些人会先等一等，看下一根K线是否只下跌几个最小报价单位。如果是，他们就在它上方挂止损单买入，并把它视为一个突破回调买入建仓形态。这个缺口随后很可能变成测量缺口。空头则会把那根突破失败的信号K线看作强烈的卖出信号，在其低点下方做空。如果他们判断正确，市场会抛售、关闭这个多头缺口（把它变成衰竭缺口），并很快跌到多头突破K线的低点之下，他们希望市场继续大幅走低。


> This process happens many times a day on every chart, and traders are always asking themselves whether a breakout will likely succeed (and turn the breakout bar into a measuring gap), or will it more likely fail (and turn the trend bar that formed the breakout into an exhaustion gap). The labels are not important, but the implications are. This is the single most important decision that traders make, and they make it whenever they consider any trade: Will there be more buyers or sellers above and below the prior bar? Whenever they believe that there is an imbalance, they have an edge. In the case of that bull breakout, when there finally is a signal bar for a failed breakout, traders will decide if there will be more buyers or sellers below that bar. If they think that the breakout is strong, they will assume that there will be more buyers, and they will buy below the bar. Others will wait to see if the next bar only falls for a few ticks. If so, they will place stop orders to buy above it, and they will consider it to be a breakout pullback buy setup. The gap will then likely become a measuring gap. The bears will see that signal bar for the failed breakout as a strong sell signal, and they will short below its low. If they are right, the market will sell off, and close the bull gap (turning it into an exhaustion gap), and soon move below the low of the bull breakout bar, and they hope that it will continue much lower.


“所有缺口都会被回补”，这句话你偶尔会听到，但它对交易者的帮助微乎其微。市场总是会回来回测之前的价格，所以更准确的说法应该是“所有之前的价格都会被回测”。不过，留意缺口的交易者足够多，所以缺口确实能起磁力位的作用，尤其是在回调接近缺口的时候。市场离任何磁力位越近，磁场就越强，市场到达该磁力位的可能性也越大（这正是买入价格真空和卖出价格真空的成因）。举例来说，多头趋势中出现一个向上跳空缺口，等到终于出现一次修正或反转时，市场跌到缺口之前那根K线高点之下（也就是回补缺口）的概率，可能只比跌到这段上涨行情中其他某根K线高点之下的概率略高一点。但既然缺口是磁力位，交易者就可以在市场接近缺口时寻找交易机会，就像市场接近任何磁力位时应该做的那样。


> “All gaps will get filled” is a saying that you sometimes hear, but this saying only rarely helps traders. The market is always coming back to test prior prices, so the saying would be more precise if it were “all prior prices get tested.” However, enough traders pay attention to gaps so that they act as magnets, especially when the pullback gets close to them. The closer the market gets to any magnet, the stronger the magnetic field and the more likely the market will reach the magnet (this is the basis for buy and sell vacuums). For example, if there is a gap up in a bull trend, once there is finally a correction or a reversal, the market might be only slightly more likely to go below the high of the bar before the gap (and therefore fill the gap) than it is to go below the high of any other bar in the rally. However, since gaps are magnets, traders can look for trading opportunities as the market approaches them, just as they should as the market approaches any magnet.


一根K线的低点高于前一根K线的高点、或者一根K线的高点低于前一根K线的低点，这种缺口在流动性很高的品种的盘中图上很少见，只有一天的第一根K线是例外——那时它们很常见。不过，如果采用宽泛的定义，5分钟图上每天都有许多其他类型的缺口出现，它们有助于理解市场在做什么，也有助于设置交易。偶尔，5分钟图上某根K线的开盘价会高于前一根K线的收盘价，这往往是微妙的强势信号。比如，连续几根多头趋势K线上出现两三个这样的缺口，多头很可能很强。所有这些缺口在日线图、周线图和月线图上具有同样的意义。


> Gaps where the low of a bar is above the high of the prior bar, or where the high of a bar is below the low of the prior bar, are rare on an intraday chart of a highly liquid instrument, except on the first bar of the day, when they are common. However, if one uses a broad definition, gaps of other types occur many times every day on a 5 minute chart, and they can be useful in understanding what the market is doing and in setting up trades. Occasionally, the open of a bar on a 5 minute chart will be above the close of the prior bar, and this is often a subtle indication of strength. For example, if there are two or three of these gaps on consecutive bull trend bars, the bulls are likely strong. All of these gaps have the same significance on daily, weekly, and monthly charts as well.


因为缺口是价格行为中重要的组成部分，日内交易者应当采用宽泛的缺口定义，并把趋势K线看作它在盘中图上的等价物，因为两者在功能上完全相同。如果成交量足够稀薄，那么每张盘中图上只要出现一串趋势K线，就会留下真实的缺口。记住：所有趋势K线都是急速行情、突破和高潮，而突破是缺口的一种变体。当 Emini 小型合约在当天第一根K线出现大幅向上跳空时，标普500（S&P 500）现货指数上对应的就是一根大实体多头趋势K线。这就是缺口与趋势K线表现同一种行为的一个例子。趋势启动时出现一根大实体趋势K线，它就制造出一个突破缺口。比如，市场正从低点向上反转、或者正突破一个交易区间，那么趋势K线之前那根K线的高点、以及它之后那根K线的低点，就构成了这个突破缺口。你完全可以把整根趋势K线的实体也看作缺口；另外，最近可能还有别的摆动高点，会被一些交易者当作这个缺口的底部。往往不存在唯一的选择，但这并不重要。重要的是确实发生了一次突破，也就意味着存在一个缺口，尽管图上看不到传统意义上的缺口。市场常常会跌到趋势K线之前那根K线的高点下方一两个最小报价单位，而只要回调不跌破这根趋势K线的低点，交易者就仍然认为突破有效。一般来说，如果市场跌破它之前那根K线的高点超过两三个最小报价单位，交易者就会对这次突破失去信心，后续行情可能也不会太多，即便没有出现反转。


> Because gaps are important elements of price action, intraday traders should use a broad definition of a gap and look at trend bars as an intraday equivalents because they are functionally identical. If the volume was thin enough, there would be actual gaps on every intraday chart whenever there was a series of trend bars. Remember, all trend bars are spikes, breakouts, and climaxes, and a breakout is a variant of a gap. When there is a large gap up on the first bar of the day on the Emini, there will be a large bull trend bar on the Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 cash index. That is an example of how a gap and a trend bar represent the same behavior. When there is a large trend bar at the start of a trend, it creates a breakout gap. For example, if the market is reversing up from a low or breaking out of a trading range, the high of the bar before the trend bar and the low of the bar after it create the breakout gap. You can simply think of the entire trend bar's body as the gap as well, and there may be other recent swing highs that some traders will consider as the bottom of the gap. There is often not a single choice, but that does not matter. What does matter is that there is a breakout, which means that there is a gap, even though a traditional gap is not visible on the chart. The market will often dip a tick or two below the high of the bar before the trend bar, and traders will still think that the breakout is in effect as long as the pullback does not fall below the low of the trend bar. In general, if the market falls more than a couple of ticks below the high of the bar before it, traders will lose confidence in the breakout and there might not be much follow-through, even if there is no reversal.


只要出现一根可能构成多头突破的趋势K线，就一定要看它前一根K线的高点和后一根K线的低点。如果两者不重叠，它们之间的空当也许能起测量缺口的作用。如果趋势继续向上，就留意市场在等距运动目标处止盈（该目标以多头行情段的低点到缺口中点来测算）。有时缺口的底部是几根K线之前形成的摆动高点，或者是急速行情内部的一个高点，但位置都在趋势K线之前两根K线处。缺口的低点则可能是突破K线之后许多根K线才形成的摆动低点。空头行情段中向下突破的空头趋势K线也是同样的道理。要始终寻找潜在的测量缺口，最明显的一个就是空头趋势K线之前那根K线的低点、与它之后那根K线的高点之间的那个缺口。


> Whenever there is a trend bar in a potential bull breakout, always look at the high of the bar before it and the low of the bar after it. If they do not overlap, the space between them might function as a measuring gap. If the trend continues up, look for profit taking at the measured move (based on the low of the bull leg to the middle of the gap). Sometimes the bottom of the gap will be a swing high that formed several bars earlier, or a high within the spike, but a couple of bars before the trend bar. The low of the gap might be a swing low that forms many bars after the breakout bar. The same is true of a bear trend bar that is breaking out in a bear leg. Always look for potential measuring gaps, the most obvious one being the one between the low of the bar before the bear trend bar and the high of the bar after it.


如果多头趋势已经走了5到10根甚至更多K线，然后又出现一根多头趋势K线，它可能只是一个平平无奇的缺口，也可能成为测量缺口或衰竭缺口。在看到接下来几根K线之前，交易者无从判断。如果又出现一根强势的多头趋势K线，成为测量缺口的概率就更大，多头会继续买入，预期这波上涨行情大约还能再走一个等距运动，其基准是缺口的中点。


> If the bull trend has been going on for 5 to 10 or more bars and then there is another bull trend bar, it might become just an unremarkable gap, a measuring gap, or an exhaustion gap. Traders will not know until they see the next several bars. If there is another strong bull trend bar, the odds of a measuring gap are greater and bulls will continue to buy with the expectation of the rally continuing up for about a measured move, based on the middle of the gap.


另一种常见的缺口，位于某根K线的高点或低点与均线之间。在趋势中，这类缺口可以构成不错的波段交易机会，去回测趋势的极值点；在交易区间中，它们往往会形成向均线回归的剥头皮机会。举例来说，在一段强势空头趋势中，市场终于上涨到均线上方，这波上涨行情中第一根低点位于均线上方的K线，就是第一根均线缺口K线。交易者会在这根K线低点下方1个最小报价单位处挂卖出止损单做空，目标回测空头市场的低点。如果该止损单没有被触发，他们就把止损位不断上移到刚收盘那根K线低点下方1个最小报价单位处，直到空头仓位成交为止。有时市场涨到信号K线上方，他们会被止损出局；一旦发生这种情况，他们会再试一次，在前一根K线低点下方1个最小报价单位处重新建立空头仓位。一旦成交，这根信号K线就是第二个均线缺口K线的做空信号。


> Another common gap is between the high or low of a bar and the moving average. In trends, these can set up good swing trades that test the extreme of the trend, and in trading ranges, they often set up scalps to the moving average. For example, if there is a strong bear trend and the market finally rallies above the moving average, the first bar in that rally that has a low above the moving average is a first moving average gap bar. Traders will place a sell stop order at one tick below the low of that bar to go short, looking for a test of the bear market low. If the stop is not triggered, they will keep moving the stop up to one tick below the low of the bar that just closed until their short is filled. Sometimes they will get stopped out by the market moving above the signal bar, and if that happens, they will try one more time to reenter their shorts at one tick below the low of the prior bar. Once filled, the signal bar is a second moving average gap bar short signal.


均线缺口每天都会出现许多次，而且大多数时候都出现在没有强趋势的情况下。如果交易者有所选择，许多这类缺口K线都能构成反向做回均线的机会。举例来说，假设当天是一个交易区间日，市场已经在均线上方待了一个小时左右。如果随后抛售跌到均线下方，但紧接着出现一根强势多头反转K线、其高点仍在均线下方，那么只要这根K线的高点与均线之间留有足够空间、够做一次多头方向的剥头皮，交易者往往会在这根K线上方做多。


> Moving average gaps happen many times a day every day, and most of the time they occur in the absence of a strong trend. If traders are selective, many of these gap bars can set up fades to the moving average. For example, assume that the day is a trading range day and that the market has been above the moving average for an hour or so. If it then sells off to below the moving average but is followed by a strong bull reversal bar with a high that is below the moving average, traders will often go long above that bar if there enough room between the high of that bar and the moving average for a long scalp.


所有时间级别上的突破——包括盘中图和日线图——形成的突破缺口和测量缺口，往往与传统版本有所不同。突破点与突破后第一次停顿或回调之间的空当就是缺口；如果它出现在一段可能的强趋势的早期，它就是突破缺口，是强势信号。虽然它会带来一段从行情段起点起算的等距运动，但这个目标通常太近，交易者不值得据此止盈，所以应当忽略这个等距运动目标位。相反，他们应该只把这个缺口看作强势信号，而不是用来推算止盈目标的工具。举例来说，Emini 小型合约的日均区间一直是12点左右，而开盘约一个小时之后，当天区间只有3点，那么一次突破所形成的缺口会指向一个目标，而按该目标算下来当天区间只有6点。如果趋势才刚刚启动，当天区间更可能达到12点左右的均值，而不是只有6点，因此交易者不该在等距运动目标位止盈。


> Breakouts on all time frames, including intraday and daily charts, often form breakout gaps and measuring gaps that are different from the traditional versions. The space between the breakout point and the first pause or pullback after the breakout is a gap, and if it appears early in a possible strong trend, it is a breakaway gap and is a sign of strength. Although it will lead to a measured move from the start of the leg, the target is usually too close for traders to take profits and they should therefore ignore the measured move projection. Instead, they should look at the gap as only a sign of strength and not a tool to use to create a target for taking profits. For example, if the average daily range in the Emini has been about 12 points and after about an hour into the day the range is only three points, the gap formed by a breakout would lead to a target that would result in a range for the day of only six points. If a trend is just beginning, it is more likely that the range will reach about the average of 12 points and not just six points, and therefore traders should not be taking profits at the measured move target.


当行情段起点到突破缺口（breakaway gap）的距离，大约相当于日均区间的三分之一到二分之一时，这个缺口的中点往往能推算出一个等距运动目标位，交易者可能在那里止盈，甚至反手。举例来说，市场处在一个交易区间中，随后形成一根大实体多头趋势K线向上突破该交易区间，区间顶部的那个摆动高点就是突破点。如果下一根K线横盘或上涨，那么这根K线的低点就是第一个可以当作突破回测的价位；它的低点与突破点之间的中点，往往成为多头行情段的中点，而这个缺口就是测量缺口。如果区间大小约为近期日均区间的三分之一到二分之一，就以这段行情段的底部作为等距运动的起点；量出这个低点到测量缺口中点之间相隔多少个最小报价单位，再从该中点向上投射相同的距离。然后观察：如果市场上涨到距离等距运动目标位1个最小报价单位左右的位置，它会怎么表现。如果在突破后的几根K线之内，市场回调进入缺口、随后又上涨，就用那次回调的低点作为突破回测，这时测量缺口就位于该低点与突破点之间。这是强势信号。一旦市场上涨到等距运动目标位，许多交易者会对多头仓位部分或全部止盈。如果这波上涨较弱，有些交易者甚至可能在等距运动目标位挂限价单做空，不过只有经验非常丰富的交易者才该考虑这么做。


> When the distance from the start of the leg to the breakout gap (breakaway gap) is about a third to a half of an average daily range, its middle often leads to a measured move projection where traders might take profits or even reverse their positions. For example, if the market is in a trading range and then the market forms a large bull trend bar that breaks out above the trading range, the swing high at the top of the range is the breakout point. If the market moves sideways or up on the next bar, the low of that bar is the first price to consider as the breakout test; the midpoint between its low and the breakout point often becomes the middle of the bull leg, and the gap is a measuring gap. If the range is about a third to a half of the recent average daily range, use the bottom of the leg as the starting point for the measured move; measure the number of ticks between that low and the middle of the measuring gap, and project that same number of ticks up above that midpoint. Then look to see how the market behaves if it moves up to a tick or so of the measured move. If within a few bars of the breakout the market pulls back into the gap but then rallies, use that pullback low as the breakout test, and then the measuring gap is between that low and the breakout point. This is a sign of strength. Once the market rallies to the measured move projection, many traders will take partial or total profits on their longs. If the move up was weak, some traders might even place limit orders to short at the measured move target, although only very experienced traders should consider this.


艾略特波浪交易者把其中大多数缺口看作一次小的第4浪回调造成的——它没有跌破第1浪的高点，于是他们预期随后会有第5浪。基于艾略特波浪理论成交的量还不够大，不足以让它成为价格行为中的一个重要组成部分；但只要回调没有跌破突破点，所有交易者都会把这看成强势信号，并预期市场会回测趋势高点。这次回调就是一次突破回测。


> Elliott Wave traders see most of these gaps as being formed by a small wave 4 pullback that is staying above the high of wave 1, and expect a wave 5 to follow. Not enough volume is being traded based on Elliott Wave Theory to make this a significant component of the price action, but whenever a pullback does not fall below the breakout point, all traders see this as a sign of strength and expect a test of the trend high. The pullback is a breakout test.


如果回调小幅跌破突破点，这是强势不足的信号。即便回调位于突破点下方，你仍然可以用那个低点与突破点之间的中点。出现这种情况时，我把这类缺口称为负缺口，因为两者相减得到的差是负数。举例来说，在一次多头突破中，用突破回测那根K线的低点减去突破点的高点，结果是负数。负的测量缺口推算出的目标位可靠性较低，但仍然可能相当准确，所以值得留意。顺便说一句，楼梯形态在每一次新的突破之后都会出现负缺口。


> If the pullback falls a little below the breakout point, this is a sign of a lack of strength. You can still use the middle between that low and the breakout point even though the pullback is below the breakout. When that happens, I refer to this type of gap as a negative gap, since the mathematical difference is a negative number. For example, in a bull breakout, if you subtract the high of the breakout point from the low of the breakout test bar, the result is a negative number. Negative measuring gaps lead to projections that are less reliable, but still can be very accurate and therefore are worth watching. Incidentally, stairs patterns have negative gaps after each new breakout.


任何一根趋势K线周围也可能形成小的测量缺口。如果趋势K线的前一根与后一根互不重叠，就出现这种微型测量缺口，而它像任何缺口一样可以引出一段等距运动。如果这根趋势K线当时正在起突破的作用，得到的等距运动通常会更准确。举个例子，看任意一段多头行情段中某根强势多头趋势K线，它正在向上突破、进入一段强势多头行情段。如果它后一根K线的低点等于或高于它前一根K线的高点，两者之间的空当就是缺口，可能成为测量缺口。从行情段起点量到缺口中点，再向上投射，看看若这个缺口位于行情段中点，市场得涨到多高。这就是多头可能止盈的区域。如果上方还有别的理由做空，空头也会在那里做空。当这类微型缺口出现在趋势最初的几根K线里时，市场通常会走得比基于该缺口算出的等距运动远得多。别用这个缺口去找止盈区域，因为市场多半会走得更远，你不想在一段绝佳的波段里过早离场。不过，这类缺口在趋势的早期阶段依然重要，因为它们让顺势交易者对趋势的强度更有信心。


> Small measuring gaps can also form around any trend bar. These micro measuring gaps occur if the bar before and the bar after the trend bar do not overlap and, like any gap, can lead to a measured move. The measured move will usually be more accurate if the trend bar was acting as a breakout. For example, look at any strong bull trend bar in any bull leg where the trend bar is breaking into a strong bull leg. If the low of the bar after it is at or above the high of the bar before it, the space between is a gap and it can be a measuring gap. Measure from the start of the leg to the middle of the gap, and project up to see how high the market would have to go if the gap was in the middle of the leg. This is an area where longs might take profits. If there are other reasons to short up there, bears will short there as well. When these micro gaps occur in the first several bars of a trend, the market will usually extend much further than a measured move based on the gap. Don't use the gap to find an area in which to take profits, because the market will likely go much further and you don't want to exit early in a great swing. However, these gaps are still important in the early stages of a trend because they give trend traders more confidence in the strength of the trend.


突破每天都在发生许多次，但大多数都以失败告终、市场随之反转。不过，突破一旦成功，在可以接受的胜率之下，它能提供的潜在回报可以达到风险的数倍。一旦交易者学会判断一次突破是否可能成功，就应该考虑这类交易。关于测量缺口，第8章讲等距运动时还有别的例子。


> Breakouts occur many times every day, but most of them fail and the market reverses. However, when they succeed, they offer a potential reward that can be several times as large as the risk with an acceptable probability of success. Once a trader learns how to determine if a breakout is likely to be successful, these trades should be considered. There are other examples of measuring gaps in Chapter 8 on measured moves.


采用这种宽泛的缺口定义，交易者能发现许多交易机会。有一种极常见的缺口，出现在任何图上连续三根沿趋势方向推进的K线之中。比如，这三根K线向上推进，而第3根K线的低点等于或高于第1根K线的高点，那么两者之间存在缺口，它可以起测量缺口或突破缺口的作用。第1根K线的高点是突破点，第3根K线的低点对它做了回测，因此成为突破回测。在更小时间级别的图上，你能看到第1根K线顶部的摆动高点，以及第3根K线底部的摆动低点。这种建仓形态很容易被忽略，但如果你研究走势图就会发现，这类缺口往往在之后许多根K线内被回测却没有被回补，因而成为买方强势的证据。


> Using this broad definition of a gap allows traders to discover many trading opportunities. A very common type of gap occurs in any three consecutive trending bars on any chart. For example, if these three bars are trending up and the low of bar 3 is at or above the high of bar 1, there is a gap and it can act as a measuring gap or a breakaway gap. The high of bar 1 is the breakout point and it is tested by the low of bar 3, which becomes the breakout test. On a smaller time frame chart, you can see the swing high at the top of bar 1 and the swing low at the bottom of bar 3. It is easy to overlook this setup, but if you study charts you will see that these gaps often get tested within the next many bars but not filled, and therefore become evidence that the buyers are strong.


另一种相关的缺口，出现在市场已经沿趋势走了许多根K线、如今却突然冒出一根异常大的趋势K线之后。举例来说，市场在过去两个小时里一直在上涨，现在突然形成一根收盘价接近高点的超大实体多头趋势K线，尤其是当这根K线的高点、或者接下来一两根K线中某根的高点延伸到一条趋势通道线上方时，就制造出一个或多个重要缺口，并带有一个或多个突破点和突破回测。偶尔，这根K线是一段更陡峭的新多头趋势的起点，但更常见的是，它代表一段走过头、已经衰竭的多头趋势中的买入高潮，随后几根K线之内就会跟随一段横盘到下跌的修正，可能持续10根K线左右，甚至可能变成趋势反转。经验丰富的交易者就在等这类K线，而他们的等待把卖方从市场里抽走，制造出一个买入价格真空，把市场迅速吸上去。一旦看到这根K线，多头就止盈，空头则在K线收盘时、在K线上方、在接下来一两根K线收盘时（如果他们较弱的话）、或者在那些K线下方挂止损单做空。要去看买入高潮K线之前和之后的K线。第一个要考虑的缺口，是它后面那根K线的低点与它前面那根K线的高点之间的缺口。如果市场继续上涨几根K线，然后回调、再度上涨，此时突破回测就变成了那次回调的低点。如果市场下跌到买入高潮K线之前那根K线的高点之下，这个缺口就被关闭（回补）了。如果市场继续下跌、走出一段大的下跌行情段，这个缺口就变成衰竭缺口。


> A related gap occurs after the market has been trending for many bars but now has an unusually large trend bar. For example, if the market has been going up for the past couple of hours but now suddenly forms a very large bull trend bar with a close near its high, especially if the high of this bar or that of one of the next couple of bars extends above a trend channel line, one or more important gaps with one or more breakout points and breakout tests are created. Rarely, this bar is the start of a new, even steeper bull trend, but much more commonly it represents a buy climax in an overdone, exhausted bull trend and will be followed within a few bars by a sideways to down correction that could last about 10 bars or so, and may even become a trend reversal. Experienced traders wait for these bars, and their waiting removes sellers from the market and creates a buy vacuum that sucks the market up quickly. Once they see it, the bulls take profits and the bears short on the close of the bar, above the bar, on the close of the next bar or two if they are weak, or on a stop below those bars. Look at the bars before and after the buy climax bar. The first gap to consider is that between the low of the bar after it and the high of the bar before it. If the market continues to go up for a few bars and then pulls back and rallies again, the breakout test is now the low of that pullback. If the market trades down below the high of the bar before the buy climax bar, the gap is then closed (filled). If the market continues down into a large leg down, the gap becomes an exhaustion gap.


另外，还要看多头突破之前那些K线，寻找其他可能的突破点。它们通常是摆动高点，可能有好几个值得考虑。比如，几根K线之前可能有一个小摆动高点，而另外两个更高的摆动高点甚至在两个小时之前就已经形成。如果突破那根K线强势地一举越过它们全部，那么它们都是可能的突破点，都可能引出一段向上的等距运动，你或许还得考虑从各个缺口中点向上推演出的目标位。如果其中一个目标位上出现阻力的汇合，比如趋势通道线、更大时间级别的空头趋势线、或者根据其他算法（例如交易区间的高度）算出的另外几个等距运动目标位，那么获利了结者会在该价位进场，同时也会有一些空头。空头里有一部分是做剥头皮的，另一些则在建立波段仓位，并会在更高处加仓。


> Also, look at the bars before the bull breakout for other possible breakout points. These usually are swing highs and there might be several to consider. For example, there might have been a small swing high a few bars earlier but another couple of higher swing highs that formed even a couple of hours earlier. If the breakout bar broke strongly above all of them, they are all possible breakout points that could lead to a measured move up and you might have to consider the projections up from the midpoint of each of these gaps. If there is a confluence of resistance at one of the projections, like a trend channel line, a higher time frame bear trend line, or a couple of other measured move targets based on other calculations, like the height of the trading range, profit takers will come in at that level and there will also be some shorts. Some of the shorts will be scalping, but others will be establishing swings and will add on higher.


有一种流传很广的看法：大多数缺口都会被回补，或者至少突破点都会被回测——这是事实。只要某件事很可能发生，就有交易机会。当出现一段空头急速与通道时，市场常常会向上修正到通道顶部、也就是缺口的底部，并试图形成一个双顶、向下回测。当出现一根向上突破重要摆动高点的买入高潮K线时，通常会有一次回调去回测那个摆动高点，所以交易者应该去找可能促成这次回测的做空建仓形态。不过，别太心急，要确认这个建仓形态说得通，也要有其他证据表明回调可能即将到来。这可能是一个横盘牛旗，它突破后只走了两根K线，接着出现一根强势反转K线，把这个牛旗变成了可能的末端旗形。末端旗形之后通常至少跟着一段两段式修正、去回测旗形的底部；它们往往会从旗形顶部到旗形底部走出一段向下的等距运动，有时还会引出趋势反转。上述所有内容对空头突破同样成立。


> There is a widely held belief that most gaps get filled or at least the breakout point gets tested, and this is true. Whenever something is likely to happen, there is a trading opportunity. When there is a bear spike and channel, the market often corrects back up to the top of the channel, which is the bottom of the gap, and tries to form a double top for a test down. When there is a buy climax bar that breaks out above a significant swing high, there will usually be a pullback that tests that swing high, so traders should look for short setups that could lead to the test. However, do not be too eager, and make sure that the setup makes sense and that there is other evidence that the pullback is likely to be imminent. This might be a sideways bull flag that breaks out and runs for a couple bars and then has a strong reversal bar, turning that bull flag into a possible final flag. Final flags usually are followed by at least a two-legged correction that tests the bottom of the flag; they often drop for a measured move down from the top to the bottom of the flag, and sometimes lead to a trend reversal. All of the preceding is true for bear breakouts as well.


除了趋势起点形成的突破缺口、以及趋势中段形成的测量缺口之外，还有趋势试图反转时形成的衰竭缺口。当缺口出现在趋势后段，随后市场反转并关闭这个缺口，它就变成衰竭缺口；像所有衰竭信号一样（在第3册讲反转的部分讨论），它后面通常跟着一个交易区间，但有时也会引出反转。这类缺口对依据日线图交易的交易者更重要，但日内交易者在跳空开盘之后出现开盘反转时，随时都能见到它们。日内交易者只把它们当作失败的跳空开盘，但它们其实是衰竭缺口的一种。在日线图上，如果一个衰竭缺口之后紧跟一个反方向的突破缺口，而且该缺口在K线收盘之后仍然敞开，就构成岛形反转形态。举例来说，一段多头趋势之后出现一个向上跳空，紧接着在下一根K线、甚至十几根K线之后出现一个向下跳空，两个缺口之间的那些K线就被视为岛形顶。图 18.4（在第18章）给出了日线图上岛形底的一个例子。


> Besides the breakout gaps that form at the start of trends and the measuring gaps that form in the middle, exhaustion gaps form when a trend is trying to reverse. When there is a gap late in a trend and then the market reverses and closes the gap, the gap becomes an exhaustion gap and, like all signs of exhaustion (discussed in book 3 on reversals), it is usually followed by a trading range, but it sometimes leads to a reversal. These are more important to traders who are trading off of daily charts, but day traders see them all the time on gap openings that lead to opening reversals. Day traders think of them as just failed gap openings, but they are a type of exhaustion gap. On the daily chart, if there is an exhaustion gap followed by a breakout gap in the opposite direction and that gap remains open after the bar closes, this creates an island reversal pattern. For example, if there is a bull trend and then there is a gap up that is followed by a gap down on the next bar or even a dozen bars later, the bars between the two gaps are considered to be the island top. Figure 18.4 (in Chapter 18) shows an example of an island bottom on a daily chart.


每当出现一段通道，随后又出现一根收盘价越过前一根K线极值的趋势K线时，交易者就应该留意是否形成缺口。举例来说，如果出现一段多头通道或者一个熊旗，而下一根K线收盘于前一根K线高点之上好几个最小报价单位，这根突破K线就可能成为测量缺口。留意下一根K线的低点是否保持在前一根K线的高点之上。如果是，这根突破K线就可能是测量缺口。如果缺口被关闭，那根趋势K线就可能是衰竭缺口，这波多头急速行情可能导致反转向下。


> Whenever there is a channel and then a trend bar that closes beyond the extreme of the prior bar, traders should watch to see if a gap forms. For example, if there is a bull channel or a bear flag and the next bar closes several ticks above the high of the prior bar, this breakout bar might become a measuring gap. Watch the low of the next bar to see if it stays above the high of the prior bar. If so, the breakout bar might be a measuring gap. If the gap closes, the trend bar might be an exhaustion gap and the bull spike could lead to a reversal down.


关于突破缺口，第1册第23章讲开盘后形成的趋势时有进一步讨论，第3册讲跳空开盘的那一章也有。


> Breakout gaps are discussed further in the first book in Chapter 23 on trends from the open and in the third book in the chapter on gap openings.


![图 6.1](figures/fig-06-01.jpg)


**图 6.1　日线图上多种类型的缺口**


日线图上的传统缺口分为突破缺口（breakaway gap）、测量缺口、衰竭缺口和普通缺口。多数情况下，归类并不重要，一个最初表现为某种类型的缺口，后来可能被看成另一种类型。比如，图 6.1所示 AAPL 日线图上的缺口5，可能曾经是测量缺口，最终却成了衰竭缺口。另外，当市场处在强趋势中时，往往会有一系列缺口，其中任何一个都可能成为测量缺口。交易者需要意识到每一种可能。例如，缺口4、21、25、26、27和45都是潜在的测量缺口。缺口4就是测量缺口，第6根K线的高点几乎构成一段完美的等距运动目标。从这段行情段的底部（第2根K线的低点）到缺口中点，相隔的最小报价单位数与从缺口中点到第6根K线顶部大致相当；获利了结者就是在这个高点进场，新的强势空头也在那里进场。在基于缺口26和缺口45推算的目标位稍下方，出现了止盈盘。


> Traditional gaps on a daily chart are classified as breakout gaps (breakaway gaps), measuring gaps, exhaustion gaps, and just ordinary gaps. For the most part, the classification is not important, and a gap that appears as one type initially can be seen as a different type later on. For example, gap 5 on the daily chart of AAPL shown in Figure 6.1 might have been a measuring gap but ended up as an exhaustion gap. Also, when a market is in a strong trend, it often has a series of gaps and any can become a measuring gap. Traders need to be aware of each possibility. For example, gaps 4, 21, 25, 26, 27, and 45 were potential measuring gaps. Gap 4 was a measuring gap, and the bar 6 high was almost a perfect measured move. The bar 2 bottom of the leg to the middle of the gap had about as many ticks as the middle of the gap to the top of bar 6, where profit takers came in, as did new strong bears. Profit taking came in just below the targets based on gaps 26 and 45.


突破缺口往往会翻转始终入场方向，因而是重要的强势信号。大多数交易者会把下面这些归为突破缺口：缺口3、7、11、15、18、29、32、36、44和47。当突破与缺口同时出现时，要把这个缺口当作强势信号，而不是用来推算等距运动目标位的工具。趋势刚刚启动时，过早止盈是个错误。不要把合理的突破缺口候选者当作测量缺口使用。


> Breakout gaps often flip the always-in direction and therefore are an important sign of strength. Most traders would classify the following as breakout gaps: gaps 3, 7, 11, 15, 18, 29, 32, 36, 44, and 47. When there is a breakout and a gap, look at the gap as a sign of strength and not as a tool to create a measured move target. When a trend is just beginning, it is a mistake to take profits too early. Do not use a reasonable candidate for a breakout gap as a measuring gap.


涨到第22根K线的那波行情向上突破了第6根K线的高点，而回落到第23根和第24根K线的两次回调都是突破回测。第24根K线的低点（市场在那里再次转上）与第6根K线的高点之间的空当，就是突破缺口。这里因为第24根K线的低点位于第6根K线的高点之下，所以这个突破缺口是负的。由于这是从一个大型交易区间向上突破，它同时成为测量缺口的机会很大。


> The rally to bar 22 broke out above the bar 6 high, and the pullbacks to bars 23 and 24 were breakout tests. The space between the bar 24 low, where the market turned up again, and the bar 6 high is the breakout gap. Here, because the bar 24 low was below the bar 6 high, the breakout gap was negative. Since it was a breakout from a large trading range, it had a good chance of also being a measuring gap.


有些经验丰富的交易者会反向操作这次突破、在第22根K线下方做空，目标回测突破点、快速向下做一次剥头皮。多头也在等同样的东西，当回调回测进缺口时，他们随时准备以市价单或限价单积极买入。多头最初是在上涨到第22根K线的那波行情里买入这次突破的，他们乐于在同一价格再次买入，这让新的多头趋势得以恢复，并至少走出某种向上的等距运动（比如，可能依据的是从第22根K线高点回落到第23根K线低点这段高度）。趋势走了一段时间之后，交易者会开始期待更深的回调。缺口常常出现在修正之前，那个缺口就是衰竭缺口，比如缺口5、16、27、33和45。


> Some experienced traders would have faded the breakout and shorted below bar 22, looking for a test of the breakout point and a quick scalp down. The bulls were looking for the same thing and were ready to eagerly buy at the market or on limit orders when the pullback tested into the gap. The bulls originally bought the breakout in the move up to bar 22, and their eagerness to buy again at the same price enabled the new bull trend to resume and go for at least some kind of measured move up (for example, it might have been based on the height of the pullback from the bar 22 high to the bar 23 low). After a trend has gone on for a while, traders will begin to look for a deeper pullback. A gap often appears before the correction, and that gap is an exhaustion gap, like gaps 5, 16, 27, 33, and 45.


如果缺口是急速行情中的一串缺口之一，或者出现在交易区间内部，通常就不给它归类，大多数交易者干脆管它叫缺口，比如缺口19、20、37和38。


> When a gap occurs as part of a series in a spike or within a trading range, it is usually not classified and most traders refer to it simply as a gap, like gaps 19, 20, 37, and 38.


![图 6.2](figures/fig-06-02.jpg)


**图 6.2　趋势K线与缺口是一回事**


盘中图上的传统缺口，通常只有在成交量极度稀疏时才能在5分钟图上看到。图 6.2展示了两只相关联的交易所交易基金（ETF）。左边那只 FAS 当天成交1600万股（16 million shares），右边那只 RKH 只成交了98,000股。RKH 图上所有的缺口，在 FAS 图上都是趋势K线；而 FAS 图上许多大实体趋势K线，在 RKH 图上则是缺口——这说明趋势K线就是缺口的一种变体。


> Traditional gaps on intraday charts can usually be seen on 5 minute charts only if the volume is extremely light. Figure 6.2 shows two related exchange-traded funds (ETFs). The FAS on the left traded 16 million shares today, and the RKH on the right traded only 98,000 shares. All of the gaps on the RKH chart were trend bars on the FAS chart, and many of the large trend bars on the FAS chart were gaps on the RKH chart, demonstrating that a trend bar is a variant of a gap.


![图 6.3](figures/fig-06-03.jpg)


**图 6.3　趋势K线就是缺口**


盘中图也有自己的缺口版本。每一根趋势K线都是急速行情、突破和高潮；而既然每一次突破都是缺口的变体，那么每一根趋势K线都是某种缺口。在大多数5分钟图上，开盘时的缺口很常见。在图 6.3中，第2根K线跳空到昨天最后一根K线的低点下方，形成一个开盘缺口。


> Intraday charts have their own versions of gaps. Every trend bar is a spike, a breakout, and a climax, and since every breakout is a variant of a gap, every trend bar is a type of gap. Gaps on the open are common on most 5 minute charts. In Figure 6.3, bar 2 gapped beneath the low of the final bar of yesterday, creating an opening gap.


市场在第5根K线上反转向上；在反转发生的那一刻，考虑到底部很强势，它成为一段多头趋势起点的概率很高。由于它是一段多头趋势的起点，所以它也是突破缺口。有些交易者把它的实体视为缺口，另一些人则认为缺口是第4根K线的高点与第6根K线的低点之间的空当。


> The market reversed up on bar 5, and at the time of the reversal, the odds of it being the start of a bull trend were good, given the strong bottom. Because it was the start of a bull trend, it was a breakout gap. Some traders saw its body as the gap, and others thought that the gap was the space between the high of bar 4 and the low of bar 6.


第6根K线和第7根K线也是趋势K线，因此也是缺口。趋势在行进过程中出现缺口很常见，它们是强势信号。


> Bar 6 and bar 7 were also trend bars and therefore also gaps. It is common for trends to have gaps along the way and are a sign of strength.


第11根K线既突破了第9根到第10根K线构成的牛旗，也突破了开盘区间。由于开盘区间大约是日均区间的一半，交易者预期当天区间会翻倍，这让第11根K线既可能是突破缺口，也很可能是测量缺口。


> Bar 11 was a breakout of the bull flag from bar 9 to bar 10 and a breakout above the opening range. Since the opening range was about half of the size of an average daily range, traders were looking for a doubling of the range, and that made bar 11 a likely measuring gap as well as a breakout gap.


市场在第12根与第13根K线之间、昨天高点一带犹豫了三根K线，此时已临近收盘。有些交易者把它看作今天开盘区间的顶部。第13根K线是一根空头反转K线；由于市场有可能跌破它，空头把它看作一次突破失败的信号K线（这次突破同时越过了第9根K线的高点和昨天收盘价的高点）。因为这次突破太强势，多得多的交易者都判断这个突破失败卖出信号不会成功，于是挂限价单在其低点处和低点下方买入。这些激进的多头在第14根K线上迅速把市场拉了上去。第14根K线的低点于是构成测量缺口的顶部，而第9根K线的高点是底部。由于第14根K线是一根外包上涨K线，它是一次突破回调买入入场，当市场涨过前一根K线（第13根K线）的高点时触发了买入。这段多头趋势远远走过了等距运动目标位。假如空头成功把市场打下去，第11根K线就会变成衰竭缺口，而不是测量缺口。只要回调跌破第9根K线高点不超过1个最小报价单位左右，交易者仍然会把那个缺口看作测量缺口，并会考虑在等距运动目标位部分止盈（市场涨得太猛，很多人根本不会在目标位离场）。如果市场跌得更深，交易者就不会再相信任何基于第11根K线缺口算出的向上等距运动，而会去寻找其他计算等距运动目标位的方法。到那时，把第11根K线称为测量缺口还是衰竭缺口已经没有意义，交易者也不会再用那种说法去想它了。只要这波抛售没有跌破第10根K线的高点，多头就会认为这次突破是成功的。如果它跌破了第10根K线的高点、或者第10根K线的低点，交易者就会把市场看作处于交易区间中，甚至可能看作空头趋势——如果抛售很强势的话。第14根K线是对第11根K线缺口的一次突破回测。它差了1个最小报价单位没能触及第9根K线的突破点，然后转身向上。不让市场跌破第9根K线的高点或第12根K线的低点，多头就是在展示自己的实力。


> The market hesitated for three bars between bar 12 and bar 13, in the area of yesterday's high, going into the close. Some traders saw this as the top of today's opening range. Bar 13 was a bear reversal bar, and since the market might have traded below it, the bears saw it as a signal bar for a failed breakout (of both the bar 9 high and the high of yesterday's close). Since the breakout was so strong, far more traders assumed that the failed breakout sell signal would not succeed, and therefore placed limit orders to buy at and below its low. Those aggressive bulls were able to turn the market up quickly on bar 14. The low of 14 then formed the top of the measuring gap, and the high of bar 9 was the bottom. Since bar 14 was an outside up bar, it was a breakout pullback buy entry that triggered the buy as the market went above the high of the prior bar (bar 13). The bull trend went far beyond the measured move target. Had the bears succeeded in reversing the market down, bar 11 would have become an exhaustion gap instead of a measuring gap. As long as the pullback did not fall more than a tick or so below the bar 9 high, traders would have still looked at the gap as a measuring gap, and they would have considered taking partial profits at the measured move target (the market raced up so sharply that many would not have exited at the target). If the market fell further, traders would not have trusted any measured move up based on the bar 11 gap, and instead would have looked for other ways to calculate measured move targets. At that point, referring to bar 11 as either a measuring or exhaustion gap would have been meaningless, and traders would no longer have thought of it in those terms. As long as the selloff did not fall below the bar 10 high, the bulls would have considered the breakout to be successful. If it fell below the high of bar 10, or the low of bar 10, traders would have then saw the market as in a trading range, or possibly even a bear trend, if the selloff was strong. Bar 14 was a breakout test of the bar 11 gap. It missed the bar 9 breakout point by a tick and turned back up. By not letting the market fall below the bar 9 high or the bar 12 low, the bulls were showing their strength.


市场在第15根K线上再次突破，这意味着第15根K线是一个突破缺口，也可能是测量缺口。有些交易者会用开盘区间的高度来算等距运动（从第4根K线的低点到第13根K线的高点），另一些人则会用第13根K线突破点与第15根K线回调之间的缺口中点。


> The market broke out again on bar 15, which meant that bar 15 was a breakout gap and a potential measuring gap. Some traders would have used the height of the opening range for the measured move (the bar 4 low to the bar 13 high), and others would have used the middle of the gap between the bar 13 breakout point and the bar 15 pullback.


第15根和第16根K线也是多头趋势中的缺口，因此是强势信号。


> Bars 15 and 16 were also gaps in a bull trend, and therefore signs of strength.


第17根K线是一段已经走了10根或20根K线的趋势中特别大的一根多头趋势K线，因此它很可能起衰竭型趋势K线的作用，也可能是衰竭缺口。买入高潮有时会引出反转，但更常见的是只引出一段修正，持续约10根K线，而且往往是两段行情。


> Bar 17 was an especially large bull trend bar in a trend that had gone on for 10 or 20 bars, and therefore it was likely to function as an exhaustion type of trend bar and a possible exhaustion gap. Buy climaxes sometimes lead to reversals but more often just lead to corrections that last about 10 bars and often have two legs.


第19根K线是另一个可能的突破缺口，因为它向上突破了一个小牛旗；但买入高潮之后，更可能出现的是幅度更大的修正。


> Bar 19 was another potential breakout gap, since it was the breakout above a small bull flag, but after a buy climax, more of a correction was likely.


第20根K线试图成为一个空头突破缺口，但实体太小；这根K线并没有跌破正在形成的交易区间的底部（第19根K线之前那根K线的低点）。


> Bar 20 was an attempt at a bear breakout gap, but the body was too small; the bar did not break below the bottom of the developing trading range (the low of the bar before bar 19).


第22根K线是一个突破缺口，空头希望它会引出一段向下的等距运动（从而变成测量缺口）。它的空头实体很大，跌破了5根K线构成的台阶，也跌破了交易区间的底部。不过，在一段强多头趋势中，它也可能只是回测均线的一部分，或者仅仅来自一次卖出价格真空——强势多头和空头都只是在等价格再低一点点。多头等着买入以建立新的多头仓位，空头则等着对自己的空头仓位止盈。


> Bar 22 was a breakout gap, and the bears hoped that it would lead to a measured move down (and therefore become a measuring gap). It had a large bear body and it broke below a five-bar ledge and the bottom of the trading range. However, in a strong bull trend, it could simply have been part of a test of the moving average, and it might simply have been due to a sell vacuum, with strong bulls and bears just waiting for slightly lower prices. The bulls were waiting to buy to initiate new longs, and the bears were waiting to take profits on their shorts.


第23根K线延伸了这次突破，但后续行情没有跟上，于是像多头趋势中大多数反转尝试和大多数空头突破尝试一样，它失败了。大多数交易者希望再看到一根空头趋势K线，才会认为市场已经翻转为始终做空。这种情况很常见，也正因为如此，激进的多头会买入像第23根K线这类K线的收盘价，认定空头无力把市场翻转为做空。这让那些多头能在修正的最低点附近建立多头仓位。


> Bar 23 extended the breakout, but there was no follow-through, and like most reversal attempts and most bear breakout attempts in bull trends, it failed. Most traders wanted to see one more bear trend bar before they would have considered the market as having flipped to always-in short. This is a common situation, which is why aggressive bulls buy the closes of bars like 23, expecting that the bears would be unable to flip the market to short. This allows those bulls to get long near the very bottom of the correction.


第24根K线是一根多头方向的均线缺口K线，也是第17根K线买入高潮之后两段下跌行情结束的信号K线。虽然第22根K线可以被看作衰竭缺口（因为它是一段小空头趋势的终点），但大多数交易者仍把市场视为始终做多、趋势仍然向上，所以并没有多么重要的空头趋势可供衰竭。这是多头趋势中的一次回调，而不是新的空头趋势。因此，第22根K线只是一次突破失败。


> Bar 24 was a bull moving average gap bar and a signal bar for the end of two legs down from the bar 17 buy climax. Although bar 22 could be considered to be an exhaustion gap, since it was the end of a small bear trend, most traders still saw the market as always-in long and the trend as still up, so there was no significant bear trend to exhaust. This was a pullback in a bull trend and not a new bear trend. Bar 22 was therefore just a failed breakout.


第25根K线又是一次突破，因为市场正从多头趋势的一次回调中反转向上，向上突破了牛旗（第23根K线之后那根多头内包K线是牛旗入场的信号K线）。在向第23根K线的那波空头急速行情之后，第25根K线是潜在的熊旗。等第25根K线收盘明显高于第24根K线的高点，空头大概就放弃了“还会有第二段下跌”这个假设。那次收盘带来了第25根K线成为测量缺口的可能，而在第26根K线经过一根K线的停顿后再次把市场拉起来时，它就真成了测量缺口。这波上涨行情远远超过了等距运动目标位，第25根K线也就变成了突破缺口。


> Bar 25 was another breakout, since the market was reversing up from a pullback in a bull trend and therefore breaking above a bull flag (the bull inside bar after bar 23 was the signal bar for the bull flag entry). Bar 25 was a potential bear flag after the bear spike down to bar 23. Once bar 25 closed well above the bar 24 high, the bears probably gave up on their premise that a second leg down would follow. That close created the possibility that bar 25 was a measuring gap, which it was once bar 26 turned the market up again after a one-bar pause. The rally went well above the measured move target and 25 became a breakaway gap.


有些交易者仍在怀疑是否正在形成一段空头通道；但当第26根K线涨到它前面那根空头趋势K线之上、并越过第22根K线的顶部（即空头突破缺口）时，对大多数交易者来说，空头的说法就站不住脚了。


> Some traders still wondered whether a bear channel might be underway, but when bar 26 went above the bear trend bar before it and above the top of bar 22 (the bear breakout gap), the bear theory was untenable for most traders.


第27、29、32和40根K线也是多头突破缺口。


> Bars 27, 29, 32, and 40 were also bull breakout gaps.


第36根K线是一个突破缺口，但下一根K线就反转向下。于是有些交易者把第36根K线看作衰竭缺口，认为这波上涨行情可能就此结束，接下来要么进入交易区间，要么展开一轮更大的修正。


> Bar 36 was a breakout gap but the next bar reversed down. Some traders then saw bar 36 as an exhaustion gap and a possible end of the rally and the start of either a trading range or a larger correction.


第37、38和39根K线是空头缺口，也是空头实力（卖压）的表现。


> Bars 37, 38, and 39 were bear gaps and signs of strength on the part of the bears (selling pressure).


![图 6.4](figures/fig-06-04.jpg)


**图 6.4　盘中缺口**


这张 Emini 小型合约的5分钟图（图 6.4）展示了不少缺口。唯一的传统缺口出现在开盘时：当天第一根K线的低点跳空到昨天最后一根K线的高点之上。不过，由于第一根K线并没有跳空到昨天的高点之上，日线图上并不存在缺口。


> This 5 minute Emini chart in Figure 6.4 illustrates a number of gaps. The only traditional gap occurred on the open when the low of the first bar of the day gapped above the high of the final bar of yesterday. However, since the first bar did not gap above the high of yesterday, there was no gap on the daily chart.


市场一路下跌到第13根K线，随后上涨到均线上方，突破了空头趋势线。注意第14根K线的低点位于均线上方，而且是两个多小时以来第一根这样的K线。这是一个均线缺口，这类缺口往往引出对空头低点的回测，然后是一段两段式的向上行情，尤其是当向缺口K线的那波上涨像这里一样突破了空头趋势线时。在这里，它引出了第15根K线处的更高低点趋势反转，随后第二段上涨走到第18根K线。


> The market trended down to bar 13 and then rallied above the moving average, breaking the bear trend line. Notice how the low of bar 14 is above the moving average and it is the first such bar in over a couple of hours. This is a moving average gap, and these gaps often lead to a test of the bear low and then a two-legged move up, especially if the move up to the gap bar breaks above the bear trend line as it did here. Here, it led to a higher low trend reversal at bar 15 and then a second leg up to bar 18.


第6根K线向上突破了第1根和第4根K线的高点，这两个高点成了突破点。这些高点与第6根K线的低点之间的空当就是缺口，它在第6根K线之后那根K线上被回补。日内交易者只把它当作一次向上跳空和一次开盘反转向下，但它其实是衰竭缺口的一种形式。


> Bar 6 broke out above the highs of bars 1 and 4, which became breakout points. The space between those highs and the low of bar 6 was a gap, and it was filled on the bar after bar 6. Day traders think of this as simply a gap up and an opening reversal down, but it is a form of an exhaustion gap.


第10根K线之前那根空头趋势K线在高点附近开盘、在低点附近收盘，区间相对较大。由于它出现在市场已经下跌许多根K线之后，所以它是一次卖出高潮：卖方做了最后一次挣扎，此后除非先出现一次回调（往往有两段），否则再没有人愿意卖出。那根突破K线跌破了众多摆动低点（第2、3、5、7和9根K线），第11根K线则成为突破回测。此外，第10根K线的高点与均线之间还有一个大缺口，这个缺口被一段两段式行情回补，而该行情形成了低2做空建仓形态。


> The bear trend bar before bar 10 opened near its high, closed near its low, and had a relatively large range. Since it formed after the market had trended down for many bars, it was a sell climax where there was a last gasp of selling with no one left who would be willing to sell until after a pullback, which often has two legs. That breakout bar broke below many swing lows (bars 2, 3, 5, 7, and 9), and bar 11 became the breakout test. There was also a large gap between the bar 10 high and the moving average, and that gap was filled by a two-legged move that formed a low 2 short setup.


第9根K线突破点与第11根K线突破回测之间的缺口中点，引出了从通道顶部第8根K线向下到第9根K线的等距运动。第10根K线低点下方、向右一根K线处的那个标记，就是从上方两个标记投射下来的目标位。这个缺口成了测量缺口。市场没有像趋势通道线过靶之后通常那样反转向上，而是向下破位，底部正好落在精确到最小报价单位的等距运动目标位上。由于你事先无法知道这些可能的等距运动目标位里哪一个会起作用（如果有的话），最好把你能看到的都画出来，并在任何一个位置上寻找反转。这些都是空头仓位合理的止盈区域。如果还有别的理由建立多头仓位，那么当反转恰好发生在某个等距运动目标位时，这笔反转交易盈利的机会就更大。例如此处，市场跌破了趋势通道线和当天先前的低点，并在一个精确的等距运动目标位反转向上。


> The middle of the gap between the bar 9 breakout point and the bar 11 breakout test led to a measured move down from the bar 8 top of the channel down to bar 9. The hash mark below and one bar to the right of the bar 10 low is the projection down from the two higher hash marks. This gap became a measuring gap. Instead of reversing up, as is common after a reversal up from a trend channel line overshoot, the market broke to the downside and the bottom was at the measured move to the tick. Since you never know in advance which, if any, of the possible measured move targets will work, it is good to draw all that you can see and look for a reversal at any of them. These are reasonable areas to take profits on shorts. If there are other reasons to initiate a long, the chance of a profitable reversal trade increases if it occurs at a measured move. Here, for example, the market broke below a trend channel line and the prior low of the day and reversed up at an exact measured move.


虽然到第11根K线的这波上涨行情已经接近第7根和第9根K线这两个突破点，但缺口并没有被回补。这是空头强势的信号，随后市场创出了新的空头低点。


> Although the rally to bar 11 was close to the bars 7 and 9 breakout points, the gap was not filled. That is a sign that the bears were strong, and it was followed by a new bear low.


第13根K线是一段持续很久的空头趋势之后的又一根大实体空头K线，因此是第二次卖出高潮。下一根K线回补了第10根K线低点下方的缺口。


> Bar 13 was another big bear bar after a protracted bear trend and therefore a second sell climax. The next bar filled the gap below the bar 10 low.


第14根K线是对第7根和第9根K线双底（也就是突破点）的第二次突破回测。然而市场并没有下跌，而是横盘走到第15根K线，形成一个楔形牛旗。这引出一波上涨行情，缺口被关闭，跌破第7根和第9根K线的这次突破失败了。这一天试图变成反转交易日，就像趋势性交易区间日有时会做的那样，但多头趋势没能在当天后段保持控制。


> Bar 14 was a second breakout test of the bars 7 and 9 double bottom, which was the breakout point. However, instead of the market falling, it went sideways to bar 15 and formed a wedge bull flag. This led to a rally and a closure of the gap, and the breakout below bars 7 and 9 failed. The day tried to become a reversal day, as trending trading range days sometimes do, but the bull trend could not maintain control late in the day.


第17根K线是一次突破回调，它回测了第14根K线的突破点高点，并引出一波强势上涨行情，这波行情在第13根K线底部到第11根K线顶部算出的等距运动目标位上方两个最小报价单位处停下。等距运动的标记就在第13根K线的右侧，从最下面那个标记到中间那个标记的距离，向上投射得到最上面那个标记。


> Bar 17 was a breakout pullback that tested the high of the bar 14 breakout point and led to a strong rally that stopped two ticks above the measured move from the bottom of bar 13 to the top of bar 11. The measured move hash marks are just to the right of the bar 13, and the distance from the bottom one to the middle one led to the projection up to the top one.


第18根K线是另一个大均线缺口的例子，这个缺口在两根K线之内就被回补了。


> Bar 18 is another example of a large moving average gap, and the gap was filled within a couple of bars.


此外还有许多小的缺口，比如第6根K线的低点与第8根K线的高点之间的那个。尽管这个高点的价格与第6根K线的低点完全相同，它依然是缺口，而且是对跌破第6根K线那次突破的突破回测。同样，第15根K线那根反转K线的高点，是两根K线之后那根突破回测K线的突破点。


> There are many other minor gaps as well, like between the low of bar 6 and the high bar 8. Even though that high is at the same price as the low of bar 6, it is a gap and it is the breakout test of the breakout below bar 6. Similarly, the bar 15 reversal bar high was the breakout point for the breakout test bar that occurred two bars later.


注意，实体最大的那三根K线——第7根K线、第10根K线之前那根，以及第18根K线之前两根——都引出了反转。记住，大多数突破都走不远，通常会反转，至少会转为一次回调。


> Note that the three bars with the largest bodies, bar 7, the bar before bar 10, and two bars before bar 18, all led to reversals. Remember, most breakouts fail to go very far and usually reverse, at least into a pullback.


当一段趋势已经走了一段时间之后出现一根大实体趋势K线，它通常代表投降或衰竭。例如，第18根K线之前两根形成的那根大实体多头趋势K线，出现在一段非常强势的多头行情段中。空头急于离场，担心市场可能先涨得更高，之后才有回调让他们以更低的价格脱身。其他空仓的交易者则在恐慌，害怕自己错过一波冲进收盘的大趋势，于是以市价单买入，同样担心回调不会出现。这种猛烈的买入来自急不可耐的交易者；他们买完之后，还愿意买入的只剩那些只肯在回调时买入的人。这些高位上再没人愿意买了，市场就只剩下横盘或下跌两条路。


> When a large trend bar occurs after a trend has been going for a while, it usually represents capitulation or exhaustion. For example, that large bull trend bar that formed two bars before bar 18 was in a very strong bull leg. Shorts were desperate to get out and were worried that the market might go much higher before a pullback would come and let them out at a lower price. Other traders who were flat were panicking, afraid that they were missing a huge trend into the close, so they were buying at the market, also afraid that a pullback would not come. This intense buying was caused by traders with tremendous urgency, and after they bought, the only traders left who were willing to buy were traders who would only buy a pullback. With no one left to buy at these high prices, the market could only go sideways or down.


这里有好几个微型测量缺口。例如，第6根K线之后那根空头趋势K线构成一个，第10根K线之后那根多头趋势K线、以及第15根K线之后那根多头趋势K线也同样构成微型测量缺口。这几波行情都走过了等距运动目标位。


> There were several micro measuring gaps. For example, the bear trend bar after bar 6 set up one, as did the bull trend bar after bar 10 and the bull trend bar after bar 15. All of the moves went beyond the measured move targets.


第6根K线之后那根K线的低点与第7根K线之前那根K线的高点构成一个微型测量缺口，而第7根K线的低点正好完成了一段向下的等距运动。中间那根趋势K线是向下突破当天新低的一根强势空头趋势K线，收在低点上。


> The low of the bar after bar 6 and the high of the bar before bar 7 formed a micro measuring gap, and the bar 7 low was an exact measured move down. The trend bar in the middle was a breakout to a new low of the day and a strong bear trend bar, closing on its low.


第15根K线之后那根K线突破了小楔形牛旗。它后面那根K线的低点回测了第15根K线的高点，也就是突破点。这次回测精确到位；只要突破回测的低点跌破突破点不超过1个最小报价单位左右，这次回测就是强势信号。如果突破回测跌得更深，就说明突破不强、更可能失败。突破点与突破回测之间的空当就是微型缺口。由于它是突破缺口，只能用来判断突破的强度，不能作为等距运动的依据。初期突破通常会带来大行情，交易者不该急着止盈。微型缺口常常是负缺口，也就是说突破回测那根K线的低点比突破点那根K线的低点低1、2个最小报价单位。突破K线收盘之后，激进的交易者可以在前一根K线高点上方1个最小报价单位处挂限价单买入，只承担3个最小报价单位左右的风险。成功的概率可能只有40% 左右，但回报是风险的许多倍，所以交易者等式非常有利。


> The bar after bar 15 broke out of a small wedge bull flag. The low of the bar after it tested the high of bar 15, which was the breakout point. The test was exact, and as long as the low of the breakout test does not fall more than a tick or so below the breakout point, the test is a sign of strength. If the breakout test fell more, it would be a sign that the breakout was not strong and was more likely to fail. The space between the breakout point and the breakout test is a micro gap. Since it is a breakout gap, it should be used only as an indication of the strength of the breakout and not as a basis for a measured move. Initial breakouts generally lead to big moves, and traders should not be looking to take profits prematurely. Micro gaps are often negative gaps, meaning that the low of the breakout test bar is a tick or two below the low of the breakout point bar. Once the breakout bar closes, an aggressive trader can place a limit order to buy one tick above the high of the prior bar and risk just three ticks or so. The chance of success might be only about 40 percent, but the reward is many times the risk, so the trader's equation is very favorable.


![图 6.5](figures/fig-06-05.jpg)


**图 6.5　某根K线的开盘价与前一根K线收盘价之间的缺口**


如果某根K线的开盘价高于或低于前一根K线的收盘价，就存在缺口。有时它完全由成交量低迷造成（例如出现很多十字星K线时），但另一些时候它意味着强势。图 6.5中的8个缺口里有7个是多头方向的，只有第2根K线是向下缺口。当同一方向上连续出现两个或更多缺口、并且这些K线实体都沿趋势方向时，那就是强势信号。在那7个多头缺口处，大量交易者在K线收盘时下市价单，而这些单子都在卖价上成交，说明市场必须往上走才能找到足够的卖方来成交。如果卖方只肯在更高处卖、而多头愿意吃卖价，市场很可能会继续上行，至少维持一段时间。


> If the open of the bar is above or below the close of the prior bar, there is a gap. Sometimes it can be entirely due to low volume (for example, when there are many dojis), but other times it can signify strength. Seven of the eight gaps in Figure 6.5 were bullish; only on bar 2 was the gap to the downside. When there are two or more successive gaps in the same direction and the bars have trending bodies, it is a sign of strength. In those seven bull gaps, a large number of traders placed market orders on the close of the bar and the orders got filled at the offer, indicating that the market had to go up to find enough sellers to fill those orders. If sellers are only willing to sell higher and bulls are willing to buy the offer, the market will likely continue up, at least for a while.


第1根K线与它前一根K线的高点、以及它后一根K线的低点构成一个微型测量缺口。上涨到太平洋时间（PST）上午7:35那个摆动高点的行情，正好是从当天第二根K线开盘价起算的一段精确等距运动。等距运动常常以一段急速行情中第一根趋势K线的开盘价为起点。如果市场越过了该目标位，那就改用急速行情的底部，看市场是否会在那个目标位开始修正。


> Bar 1 set up a micro measuring gap with the high of the bar before it and the low of the bar after it. The move up to the 7:35 a.m. PST swing high was an exact measured move from the open of the second bar of the day. Measured moves often begin with the open of the first trend bar of a spike. If the market goes above that target, then use the bottom of the spike to see if the market begins to correct at that target.


那个向下缺口在第二根K线上反转向上，因此它是一个衰竭缺口。日内交易者则只会把它当成一次失败的向下跳空开盘和一次开盘反转向上。


> The downside gap reversed up on the second bar and it was therefore an exhaustion gap. Day traders would instead just think of it as a failed gap down opening and an opening reversal up.


# 第 Ⅱ 部分　磁力位：支撑与阻力

*Part II　Magnets: Support and Resistance*


磁力位有两类：支撑与阻力。磁力位位于市场下方时，它是支撑位，也就是多头建立仓位、空头对自己的空头仓位止盈的区域。磁力位位于市场上方时，它是阻力位，也就是多头对多头仓位止盈、空头建立空头仓位的区域。支撑与阻力都是把市场拉向自己的磁力位。当你意识到某个磁力位离当前价格不远时，在价格到达它之前，只顺着磁力位的方向交易。到达之后，你就得判断：市场看起来是会反转、会横盘，还是干脆无视这个磁力位继续沿趋势走。磁力位告诉你可能的目的地，却不告诉你路径，途中可能有大幅回调。另外，市场可能在几十根K线里都处于交易区间，但距离某个磁力位只有一步之遥。尽管你应该意识到这个磁力位，但在市场决定是否去回测它、以及怎么走到那里的时候，两个方向上都仍然可能存在可靠的交易机会。


> There are two types of magnets: support and resistance. When a magnet is below the market, it is a support level, which means that it is an area where bulls will initiate positions and bears will take profits on their shorts. When a magnet is above the market, it is a resistance level, which means that it is an area where bulls will take profits on their longs and bears will initiate shorts. Support and resistance are magnets that draw the market toward them. When you become aware of a magnet not too far from the current price, trade only in the direction of the magnet until after it is reached. At that point, you will have to decide if it looks like the market will reverse, go sideways, or ignore the magnet and keep trending. Magnets tell you the likely destination, but not the path, and there may be big pullbacks along the way. Also, the market might be in a trading range for dozens of bars, but within striking distance of a magnet. Although you should be aware of the magnet, there still can be reliable trades in both directions as the market decides if it will test the magnet and how it will get there.


交易者时刻都在关注支撑和阻力。市场具有惯性，并且强烈倾向于延续它正在做的事。市场沿趋势运行时，大多数试图反转趋势的尝试都会失败。比如市场正在下跌，大多数支撑位都无法守住、也无法让市场反转。不过，所有多头反转都发生在支撑位上（所有空头反转都发生在阻力位上），所以如果市场开始反转向上，潜在回报往往是风险的许多倍。即便成功的概率常常只有40%，交易者等式仍然是正的，因此这笔反转交易在数学上是站得住的。惯性还意味着：市场处于交易区间时，大多数突破尝试都会失败，市场会反复从区间底部形成的支撑处反转向上、从区间顶部的阻力处反转向下。尽管大多数试图反转趋势的尝试都会失败，但所有趋势反转和所有回调都始于支撑位和阻力位，所以知道它们在哪里，能帮助交易者在最佳位置止盈、并做反转交易。


> Traders are constantly looking at support and resistance. The market has inertia and a strong propensity to continue what it has been doing. When it is trending, most attempts to reverse the trend will fail. For example, if the market is trending down, most support levels will fail to hold or reverse the market. However, all bull reversals happen at support levels (and all bear reversals happen at resistance levels), so if the market begins to reverse up, the potential reward is often many times larger than the risk. Even though the probability of success is often only 40 percent, the trader's equation is still positive and the reversal trade is therefore mathematically sound. Inertia also means that when the market is in a trading range, most attempts to break out will fail, and the market will repeatedly reverse up from the support created by the bottom of the range, and reverse down from the resistance at the top. Even though most attempts to reverse a trend will fail, all trend reversals and all pullbacks begin at support and resistance levels, so knowing where they are can lead traders to take profits and to enter reversal trades at optimal locations.


Emini 小型合约的交易大多由计算机完成，它们的算法基于逻辑和数字。当它们买入正在下跌的市场、或者卖出正在上涨的市场时，是因为它们计算出那个特定价格是它们下单的合理位置。如果有足够多的算法使用相近的价格，市场就可能反转，至少反转一两根K线，而且常常足够做成一笔盈利的交易。虽然有些算法使用的数字并不直接基于 Emini 的价格图（例如，它们可能使用期权市场或其他相关市场的数据），但除非许多程序算出的数字相近，否则不太可能有足够的力量改变市场方向。市场反转时，总是发生在支撑位和阻力位上；通过练习，个人交易者通常能辨认出它们。由于其中一些反转会带来盈利的交易，也由于这些价位是合理的止盈区域，所以知道可能的转折点在哪里很有用。


> Most Emini trading is done by computers, and their algorithms are based on logic and numbers. When they buy a falling market or sell a rally, they are doing so because they calculated that the particular price was a logical location for them to place their trades. If enough algorithms are using similar prices, the market can reverse, at least for a bar or two, and often enough for a profitable trade. Although some algorithms use numbers that are not directly based on the Emini price chart (for example, they might use data based on the options markets or other related markets), unless many programs are coming up with similar numbers, it is unlikely that there will be enough force to change the direction of the market. When the market reverses, it always does so at support and resistance levels; with practice, an individual trader can usually spot them. Because some of these reversals lead to profitable trades, and because these levels are sensible areas to take profits, it is useful to know where possible turning points are.


寻找磁力位的重要理由之一是：它们是部分止盈或全部止盈的合理区域。你止盈的动作，永远应该比寻找反方向入场点更快。也就是说，要在反方向建仓，你需要比止盈更强的建仓形态。如果奔向磁力位的这波行情很弱，而且与更大趋势的方向相反，你也可以考虑建仓反方向、预期反转。市场通常会过靶、至少稍微越过磁力位；如果奔向磁力位的这波行情不是强趋势，市场通常会反转，至少反转一两根K线。如果趋势恢复、越过磁力位更远之后再次反转，这通常是一笔反方向交易的可靠建仓形态，尤其是当出现一根强势反转K线时。


> One of the important reasons to look for magnets is that they are logical areas to take partial or full profits. You should always be faster to take profits on a trade than you should be to look for an entry in the opposite direction. This means that you need a stronger setup to initiate a trade in the opposite direction than you need to take profits. If the move toward the magnet is weak and if it is against the direction of a larger trend, you can also look to initiate a trade in the opposite direction, expecting a reversal. The market will usually overshoot the magnet, at least by a small amount, and if the move toward the magnet is not a strong trend, the market will usually reverse, at least for a bar or two. If the trend resumes and goes even further past the magnet and then reverses a second time, this is usually a reliable setup for a trade in the opposite direction, especially if there is a strong reversal bar.


任何重要的价格行为都可能形成支撑或阻力，常见的例子包括：


> Any significant type of price action can form support or resistance, and common examples include:


- 趋势线。
- 趋势通道线。
- 任何时间级别上任何类型的均线。
- 等距运动目标位。
- 先前的摆动高点或摆动低点。
- 多头入场K线的低点和空头入场K线的高点。
- 多头信号K线的高点和空头信号K线的低点。
- 昨天的高点、低点、开盘价和收盘价。


> • Trend lines. • Trend channel lines. • Any type of moving average on any time frame. • Measured move targets. • Prior swing highs or lows. • Bull entry bar lows and bear entry bar highs. • Bull signal bar highs and bear signal bar lows. • Yesterday's high, low, open, and close.


- 任何一根K线的高点、低点、开盘价或收盘价，尤其是当这根K线是大实体趋势K线时。
- 日线枢轴点。
- 斐波那契回撤位与投射目标。
- 任何类型的带状指标线。支撑和阻力是交易者创造的术语，用来描述某个价格具有足够的数学优势，值得交易者做一笔能赚钱的交易。这些术语是交易者为了帮自己找到交易机会而创造的。任何时间级别上每根K线的高点都处在某个阻力位上，每根K线的低点都处在支撑上，而收盘价之所以停在它所处的位置、不高也不低1个最小报价单位，是因为计算机把它放在那里自有道理。支撑和阻力可能并不显眼，但既然计算机控制着一切、而且它们遵循逻辑，那么一切都必然说得通，哪怕常常难以理解。图上的每个价格都有某种数学优势，但这些优势通常太小，只有高频交易（HFT）程序才做得起来——许多高频程序就是为赚1美分而剥头皮设计的。按定义，一个价格只有在方向概率上存在失衡时，才算是支撑或阻力。举例来说，如果市场跌到某个支撑位，交易者相信至少有大约60% 或更高的概率出现一次至少够做一次剥头皮的反弹，而剥头皮是每个交易者的最小交易单位。如果概率只有52% 或53%，交易者大概不会认为它高到配得上这个称呼，而只会觉得这个价格平平无奇。如果市场处在交易区间的中段，前一根K线的低点从广义上说始终至少算一个最低限度的支撑区域，但这并不意味着预期的反弹大到足以做一笔赚钱的交易。如果预期的反弹只有两个最小报价单位，从交易者的角度看它就不算支撑。如果当前K线还在形成之中、正处在它的低点上、且比前一根K线的低点高1个最小报价单位，那么市场先反弹两个最小报价单位再下跌两个最小报价单位的概率也许是53%。但这个优势太小、价格波动也太小，交易者不会据此下单（尽管高频程序可能会做这笔交易），所以交易者不会称它为支撑。阻力的情况正好相反。


> • The high, low, open, or close of any bar, especially if the bar is a large trend bar. • Daily pivots. • Fibonacci retracement levels and projections. • Any type of band. Support and resistance are terms created by traders to describe any price as having enough of a mathematical edge for a trader to place a profitable trade. These terms were created by traders to help them spot trades. The high of every bar on every time frame is at some resistance level, the low of every bar is at support, and the close is where it is and not one tick higher or lower because computers put it there for a reason. The support and resistance may not be obvious, but since computers control everything and they use logic, everything has to make sense, even if it is often difficult to understand. Every price on the chart has some mathematical edge, but the edges are usually too small to be tradable except by high-frequency trading (HFT) programs, many of which are designed to scalp for a penny of profit. By definition, a price is support or resistance only if it has a directional probability imbalance. For example, if a market falls to a level of support, traders believe that there is about a 60 percent chance or better that there will be at least a bounce big enough for a scalp, which is every trader's minimal trade. If the chance was only 52 or 53 percent, traders would probably not consider that high enough to use the term and instead would just consider the price as unremarkable. If the market is in the middle of a trading range, the low of the prior bar is always at least a minimal area of support in the general sense of the word, but that does not mean the expected bounce is big enough to place a profitable trade. If the expected bounce is only a couple of ticks, it is not support from a trader's perspective. If the current bar is still forming and it is on its low and is one tick above the low of the prior bar, there might be a 53 percent chance of the market bouncing two ticks before it falls two ticks. However, that is too small an edge and too small a price movement for traders to place a trade (although a high-frequency program might make that trade), and therefore traders would not call it support. The opposite is true for resistance.


支撑和阻力之所以存在，是因为市场有记忆。市场一旦回到某个先前的价格，往往会重复它上次在那个位置做过的事。举例来说，市场跌穿一个交易区间的底部、随后又上涨回到区间底部，通常它会再次抛售，因为它上次在这个价位时就是这么做的。那些没能退出多头仓位、硬扛过这段空头行情段的交易者，会急切地希望抓住第二次机会、以更小的亏损离场，他们会一直等到市场涨回来、回测这次突破。届时他们就会卖出多头仓位，从而形成卖压。同时，在抛售底部止盈的那些空头，也会急于在上涨行情中再次做空。空头的卖出与多头的平仓卖出加在一起，会对进一步的上涨形成阻力，通常会把市场压回去。


> Support and resistance exist because the market has memory. Once the market returns to a prior price, it will tend to do the same thing that it did the last time it was there. For example, if the market falls through the bottom of a trading range and then rallies back to the bottom of the range, it will usually sell off again because that's what it did when it was last at that price level. The traders who failed to exit their longs and rode through the bear leg will be eager to get a second chance to exit them with a smaller loss, and they will hold until the market rallies back and tests the breakout. At that point, they will sell out of their longs and this will create selling pressure. Also, the shorts who took profits at the bottom of the sell-off will be eager to short again on the rally. The combined selling by the bears and the liquidating bulls will create resistance to a further rally and usually drive the market back down.


当市场回落到某个价格、多次触及它并且每次都弹开时，市场就是在该价位找到支撑。如果市场上涨到某个价位后不断回落，这个区域就是阻力。任何支撑或阻力区域都像磁力位，把市场吸引到该价格。市场越靠近，就越进入磁场，离得越近，磁力就越强。这提高了市场触及该价格的可能性。这种更强的磁力，一部分来自真空效应。举例来说，市场正沿着一段空头行情上涨、奔向一条空头趋势线但还没碰到它时，卖方往往会先让开、等待这次回测。如果他们相信市场会触及这条线，那么明明马上就能在更高处卖出，在线的稍下方卖出就不合算了。卖盘缺席造成买入失衡，于是产生真空效应，把市场迅速吸上去。结果往往是一根多头趋势K线。接着，做剥头皮的多头获利卖出多头仓位，空头则卖出建立新的空头仓位。由于低点处并没有明确的多头反转，大多数多头都是为剥头皮而买入的，他们只预期一次回调、然后空头趋势重新开始。


> When the market falls back to a price and hits it several times and bounces each time, it is finding support at that price level. If the market rallies to a price level and keeps falling back, the area is resistance. Any area of support or resistance acts as a magnet, drawing the market to the price. As the market approaches, it enters the magnetic field, and the closer it gets, the stronger the magnetic pull is. This increases the odds of the market touching the price. That greater magnetic pull in part is generated by the vacuum effect. For example, if the market is having a bear rally toward a bear trend line but has not yet hit it, the sellers will often step aside and wait for the test. If they believe the market will touch the line, it does not make sense for them to sell just below the line when they can soon sell higher. The absence of selling creates a buy imbalance and therefore a vacuum effect that quickly sucks the market up. The result is often a bull trend bar. Then, the bull scalpers sell out of their longs for a profit and the bears sell to initiate new shorts. Since there was no clear bull reversal at the low, most of the bulls bought for scalps, expecting only a pullback and then a resumption of the bear trend.
