等市场到达目标位，交易者就会认为市场现在更可能下跌到足以做一笔赚钱交易的位置，于是他们不知从哪儿冒出来，凶猛地、不间断地做空，把市场打下去。在那根强势多头趋势K线顶部买入的弱势多头，看到完全没有后续行情时会错愕不已，但他们误解了那根多头趋势K线的含义。他们以为交易者突然确信市场将突破趋势线、并开启一段多头行情段。他们对真空效应浑然不觉，也没想到空头只是在等市场再高一点。那根强势多头趋势K线，是因为空头短暂让开，而不是因为空头买回了自己的空头仓位。持续买入的多头需要找到愿意接下他们交易另一边的空头，而他们只能在更高处找到——空头认为市场会在那里开始反转。市场会继续下跌到某个中性区域，而且通常会越过它，跌到多头重新握有数学优势的位置。这是因为市场在走过头之前，从不知道自己已经走够了。随后市场在中性区域上方上下震荡，而随着多空双方更能界定这个区域，它会变得越来越窄。到了某个时点，双方都认为价值不对了，市场便再次突破，开始新一轮寻找价值的过程。


> Once the market gets to the target, traders think that the market will now more likely go down far enough to place a profitable trade, and they appear out of nowhere and short aggressively and relentlessly, driving the market down. The weak bulls who bought at the top of that strong bull trend bar are stunned that there is no follow-through, but they misunderstood the significance of the bull trend bar. They thought that traders were suddenly convinced that the market was going to break above the trend line and a bull leg would begin. They were oblivious to the vacuum effect and did not consider that the bears were just waiting for the market to get a little higher. The strong bull trend bar was due to the bears briefly stepping aside rather than the bears buying back their shorts. The bulls who kept buying needed to find bears to take the other side of their trades and they could only find them higher, where the bears thought the market would begin to reverse. The market will continue down to an area of neutrality and usually beyond to the point that the bulls now have a mathematical edge. This is because the market never knows that it has gone far enough until it goes too far. Then it trades up and down above the area of neutrality, which becomes tighter and tighter as the bulls and bears are better able to define it. At some point, both perceive that the value is wrong and the market then breaks out again and begins a new search for value.


每一次逆势急速行情，都应该被看作一次真空效应式回调。举例来说，如果5分钟图上出现一段急剧的空头急速行情，随后市场突然反转进入一段多头行情段，那么在低点处一定存在某个支撑区域——不管你是否事先看到了它。多头一直按兵不动，直到市场跌到一个他们认为价值足够可观、而以这样的好价格买入的机会转瞬即逝的位置。他们进场积极买入。聪明的空头意识到了那个磁力位，把它当作对自己空头仓位止盈的机会。结果就是5分钟图上的一个市场底部。这个底部和所有底部一样，出现在某个更大时间级别的支撑位上，比如一条多头趋势线、一条均线，或者一个大型牛旗底部处的空头趋势通道线。要记住：如果5分钟图上的反转很强势，你就会依据那次反转买入，不管你是否在日线图或60分钟图上看到了那里的支撑。同样，即便你看到了更大时间级别的支撑，你也不会在那个低点买入，除非5分钟图上有证据显示正在形成底部。这意味着你不需要翻看一大堆不同的图去找那个支撑位，因为5分钟图上的反转已经告诉你它就在那里。如果你有能力同时跟踪多个时间级别，你就会在市场到达它们之前看到支撑位和阻力位，这能提醒你在市场到达磁力位时去5分钟图上寻找建仓形态。不过，只要你仔细跟踪5分钟图，它就会告诉你所有你需要知道的东西。


> Every countertrend spike should be considered to be a vacuum effect pullback. For example, if there is a sharp bear spike on the 5 minute chart and then the market suddenly reverses into a bull leg, there was an area of support at the low, whether or not you saw it in advance. The bulls stepped aside until the market reached a level where they believed that value was considerable, and the opportunity to buy at this great price would be brief. They came in and bought aggressively. The smart bears were aware of that magnet, and they used it as an opportunity to take profits on their shorts. The result was a market bottom on the 5 minute chart. That bottom, like all bottoms, occurred at some higher time frame support level, like a bull trend line, a moving average, or a bear trend channel line at the bottom of a large bull flag. It is important to remember that if the 5 minute reversal was strong, you would buy based on that reversal, regardless of whether you saw support there on the daily or 60 minute chart. Also, you would not buy at that low, even if you saw the higher time frame support, unless there was evidence on the 5 minute chart that it was forming a bottom. This means that you do not need to be looking at lots of different charts in search of that support level, because the reversal on the 5 minute chart tells you that it is there. If you are able to follow multiple time frames, you will see support and resistance levels before the market reaches them, and this can alert you to look for a setup on the 5 minute chart when the market reaches the magnet. However, if you simply follow the 5 minute chart carefully, it will tell you all that you need to know.


一般来说，如果市场四次、五次回测某个支撑区域，跌穿这个支撑的可能性就会上升，到某个时点，突破的可能性就会大于不突破。如果在这个价位把市场托起来的买方一次又一次失败，他们迟早会放弃，然后被卖方淹没。举例来说，市场横在一条走平的均线上方，交易者会买入每一次触及均线的机会，预期一波上涨行情。但如果市场继续横盘、连一次足以做成一笔赚钱剥头皮的上涨都没有，那么到某个时点他们就会卖出多头仓位，从而制造出卖压。他们也不会再去买均线的每一次触碰。买盘的缺席会提高市场跌穿均线的概率。多头已经认定，均线这个折扣还不足以让他们积极买入，只有在更低的折扣上才会出手。如果跌破均线之后10到20根K线之内找不到这些买家，市场通常会要么沿趋势下跌，要么继续待在交易区间里，只不过现在位于均线下方。交易者会开始做空向均线反弹的上涨行情，这会提高市场开始形成更低的高点、以及均线开始向下倾斜的可能性。市场一旦跌穿支撑，支撑通常就变成阻力；市场一旦向上突破阻力，阻力通常就变成支撑。


> In general, if the market tests an area of support four or five times, the likelihood of breaking through that support increases and, at some point, the breakout becomes more likely than not. If the buyers who lifted the market at this level fail repeatedly to do so again, they will give up at some point and be overwhelmed by sellers. For example, if the market is resting above a flat moving average, traders will buy every touch of the moving average, expecting a rally. If instead the market continues sideways and they don't even get enough of a rally to allow for a profitable scalp, at some point they will sell their longs, thereby creating selling pressure. They will also stop buying touches of the moving average. This absence of buying will increase the probability that the market will fall through the moving average. The bulls have decided that the moving average was not enough of a discount for them to buy aggressively, and they will do so only on a further discount. If it does not find those buyers within 10 to 20 bars after falling below the moving average, the market will usually either trend down or continue in a trading range, but now below the moving average. Traders will begin shorting rallies to the moving average, which will increase the chances that the market will begin to form lower highs and that the moving average will start to trend down. Once the market falls through support, it usually becomes resistance; and once the market breaks above resistance, it usually becomes support.


趋势线或趋势通道线也可能出现同样的情况。举例来说，多头市场四次或更多次回调到一条趋势线，而每次都没有上涨到趋势线上方多远，那么到某个时点，多头就会停止买入趋势线的回测，并开始卖出多头仓位，制造出卖压。这叠加在空头的卖盘之上，而由于多头已经停止买入，市场就会跌穿这条趋势线。不过，有时市场反而会突然向上加速，空头于是不再对每一次小反弹都做空，而是买回自己的空头仓位，把市场推得更高。


> This can also happen with a trend line or a trend channel line. For example, if a bull market pulls back to a trend line four or more times and it does not rally far above the trend line, at some point the bulls will stop buying tests of the trend line and they will begin to sell their longs, creating selling pressure. This is added to the selling of the bears, and since the bulls have stopped buying, the market will fall through the trend line. Sometimes, however, the market will instead suddenly accelerate to the upside and the bears will stop shorting every small bounce and instead will buy back their shorts, driving the market higher.


机构交易由自主决策的交易者和计算机共同完成，计算机程序化交易已经变得越来越重要。机构的交易依据基本面信息或技术面信息，或者两者兼用；这两类交易都由交易员和计算机来做。一般来说，大多数自主决策的交易者主要依据基本面信息做决定，而大多数计算机交易基于技术数据。由于如今大部分成交量由高频交易公司完成，而且大多数交易基于价格行为和其他技术数据，所以大多数程序化交易都是技术驱动的。在二十世纪后期，一家机构运行一个大型程序就能推动市场，这个程序会形成一个微型通道，交易者把它看作程序正在运行的标志。如今，Emini 小型合约大多数交易日都会出现十来个微型通道，其中许多成交量超过100,000份合约。以 Emini 目前1200点左右计算，这相当于6亿美元，比一家机构为一笔小额交易下的单还要大。这意味着单一机构无法把市场推动很远、或者推动很久，图上所有的波动都是许多机构在同一时间朝同一方向交易所致。此外，高频交易计算机会分析每一笔 tick（成交笔数），整天不停地下单。当它们察觉到一个程序在运行时，许多会顺着该程序的方向剥头皮，而且在微型通道（程序）推进期间，它们往往占据大部分成交量。


> Institutional trading is done by discretionary traders and computers, and computer program trading has become increasingly important. Institutions base their trading on fundamental or technical information, or a combination of both, and both types of trading are done by traders and by computers. In general, most of the discretionary traders base their decisions primarily on fundamental information, and most of the computer trades are based on technical data. Since the majority of the volume is now traded by HFT firms, and most of the trades are based on price action and other technical data, most of the program trading is technically based. In the late twentieth century, a single institution running a large program could move the market, and the program would create a micro channel, which traders saw as a sign that a program was running. Now, most days have a dozen or so micro channels in the Emini, and many have over 100,000 contracts traded. With the Emini currently around 1200, that corresponds to $6 billion, and is larger than a single institution would trade for a single small trade. This means that a single institution cannot move the market very far or for very long, and that all movement on the chart is caused by many institutions trading in the same direction at the same time. Also, HFT computers analyze every tick and are constantly placing trades all day long. When they detect a program, many will scalp in the direction of the program, and they will often account for most of the volume while the micro channel (program) is progressing.


主要依据技术信息交易的机构，不可能永远把市场推向一个方向，因为到了某个时点，市场在依据基本面交易的机构眼里就会显得有价值。如果技术派机构把价格推得太高，基本面机构和其他技术派机构就会认为，这是卖出多头仓位、建立空头仓位的大好价格，它们会压倒看多的技术派交易、把市场打下去。当技术派交易造出一段空头趋势，市场到某个时点就会在基本面机构和其他技术派机构眼中显得明显便宜。买家会进场，压倒那些造成抛售的技术派机构，把市场反转向上。


> The institutions that are trading largely on technical information cannot move the market in one direction forever because at some point the market will appear as offering value to the institutions trading on fundamentals. If the technical institutions run the price up too high, fundamental institutions and other technical institutions will see the market as being at a great price to sell out of longs and to initiate shorts, and they will overwhelm the bullish technical trading and drive the market down. When the technical trading creates a bear trend, the market at some point will be clearly cheap in the eyes of fundamental and other technical institutions. The buyers will come in and overwhelm the technical institutions responsible for the selloff and reverse the market up.


所有时间级别上的趋势反转，总是发生在支撑位和阻力位上，因为技术派交易者和程序把它们当作应当停止加注、开始止盈的区域，许多人还会开始做反方向。由于这些位置全都建立在数学之上，计算机算法知道它们在哪里——所有成交量的70%、机构成交量的80% 都来自这些算法。同时，机构的基本面交易者也会关注明显的技术因素。他们把图上的主要支撑和阻力看作价值区域，等市场到达那里时就建立反方向的交易。依据价值交易的程序通常也会在差不多的区域找到价值，因为主要支撑和阻力附近几乎总能用任何衡量方式发现显著的价值。大多数程序依据价格做决定，这中间没有秘密。当某个价格重要时，不管它们用什么逻辑，它们全都看得见。基本面交易者（人和机器）等待价值，一旦发现就重仓出手。他们想在自己认为市场便宜时买入、认为市场昂贵时卖出。举例来说，市场正在下跌，但跌到一个机构觉得开始变便宜的价位，他们就会不知从哪儿冒出来积极买入。这一点在开盘反转时表现得最剧烈、也最常出现（反转可以向上也可以向下，在第3册讲开盘交易的那一节讨论）。空头会买回空头仓位止盈，多头会买入建立新的多头仓位。没有人真的擅长判断市场是否已经走够了，但大多数经验丰富的交易者和程序，通常对自己判断市场何时走过了头的能力相当有信心。


> Trend reversals on all time frames always happen at support and resistance levels, because technical traders and programs look for them as areas where they should stop pressing their bets and begin to take profits, and many will also begin to trade in the opposite direction. Since they are all based on mathematics, computer algorithms, which generate 70 percent of all trading volume and 80 percent of institutional volume, know where they are. Also, institutional fundamental traders pay attention to obvious technical factors. They see major support and resistance on the chart as areas of value and will enter trades in the opposite direction when the market gets there. The programs that trade on value will usually find it around the same areas, because there is almost always significant value by any measure around major support and resistance. Most of the programs make decisions based on price, and there are no secrets. When there is an important price, they all see it, no matter what logic they use. The fundamental traders (people and machines) wait for value and commit heavily when they detect it. They want to buy when they think that the market is cheap and sell when they believe it is expensive. For example, if the market is falling, but it's getting to a price level where the institutions feel like it is getting cheap, they will appear out of nowhere and buy aggressively. This is seen most dramatically and often during opening reversals (the reversals can be up or down and are discussed in the section on trading the open in book 3). The bears will buy back their shorts to take profits and the bulls will buy to establish new longs. No one is good at knowing when the market has gone far enough, but most experienced traders and programs are usually fairly confident in their ability to know when it has gone too far.


因为机构要等到市场明显超卖才肯买入，所以在可能的底部上方区域缺乏买盘，市场得以加速下跌，一直跌到它们确信便宜的区域。有些机构依靠程序判断买入时机，另一些则由人自主决策。一旦足够多的机构买入，市场通常就会向上转折，至少走出两段行情、大约10根或更多K线——要看这件事发生在哪张时间级别的图上。在市场下跌的过程中，机构会一路做空，直到判定已经到达某个可能的目标位、不太可能再跌，此时它们才止盈。市场越超卖，成交量中技术驱动的比例就越大，因为基本面交易者和程序在看到市场便宜、眼看就要被买入时，就不会继续做空。随着市场接近一个主要支撑位，买盘相对缺席，往往使抛售加速冲向支撑，通常会形成一次卖出价格真空，把市场在跌到高潮时吸到支撑下方，此时市场急剧反转向上。大多数支撑位都挡不住空头趋势（大多数阻力位也挡不住多头趋势），但当市场终于反转向上时，它一定发生在某个显而易见的主要支撑位上，比如一条长期趋势线。抛售的底部和反转向上通常伴随着非常巨大的成交量。市场下跌途中会有许多向上冲到阻力位的上涨行情、以及向下砸到支撑位的抛售，每一次反转都发生在足够多的机构判定市场已经走得太远、为反方向交易提供了价值的时候。当足够多的机构在相近的价位一起行动，一次主要反转就发生了。


> Because the institutions are waiting to buy until the market has become clearly oversold, there is an absence of buyers in the area above a possible bottom, and the market is able to accelerate down to the area where they are confident that it is cheap. Some institutions rely on programs to determine when to buy and others are discretionary. Once enough of them buy, the market will usually turn up for at least a couple of legs and about 10 or more bars on whatever time frame chart where this is happening. While it is falling, institutions continue to short all the way down until they determine that it has reached a likely target and it is unlikely to fall any further, at which point they take profits. The more oversold the market becomes, the more of the volume is technically based, because fundamental traders and programs will not continue to short when they think that the market is cheap and should soon be bought. The relative absence of buyers as the market gets close to a major support level often leads to an acceleration of the selling into the support, usually resulting in a sell vacuum that sucks the market below the support in a climactic selloff, at which point the market reverses up sharply. Most support levels will not stop a bear trend (and most resistance levels will not stop a bull trend), but when the market finally reverses up, it will be at an obvious major support level, like a long term trend line. The bottom of the selloff and the reversal up is usually on very heavy volume. As the market is falling, it has many rallies up to resistance levels and selloffs down to support levels along the way, and each reversal takes place when enough institutions determine that it has gone too far and is offering value for a trade in the opposite direction. When enough institutions act around the same level, a major reversal takes place.


判断支撑（以及阻力）有基本面和技术面两种方法。比如，可以用计算来估算，像标普500的市盈率理论上该是多少；但这些计算永远不够精确，无法让足够多的机构达成一致。不过，传统的支撑和阻力区域更容易看出来，因此更容易被众多机构注意到，它们也更清楚地界定了市场应该在哪里反转。在1987年和2008–2009年的两次崩盘中，市场都暴跌到月线趋势线稍下方后反转向上，形成了重要底部。市场会继续上行，伴随许多次向下回测，直到走得太远为止，而那个位置总是某个显著的阻力位。只有到了那时，机构才能确信卖出多头仓位、建立空头仓位有着明确的价值。随后这个过程就会向下反转。


> There are fundamental and technical ways to determine support (and resistance). For example, it can be estimated with calculations, like what the S&P 500 price earnings multiple should theoretically be, but these calculations are never sufficiently precise for enough institutions to agree. However, traditional areas of support and resistance are easier to see and therefore more likely to be noticed by many institutions, and they more clearly define where the market should reverse. In the crashes of both 1987 and 2008–2009, the market collapsed down to slightly below the monthly trend line and then reversed up, creating a major bottom. The market will continue up, with many tests down, until it has gone too far, which is always at a significant resistance level. Only then can the institutions be confident that there is clear value in selling out of longs and selling into shorts. The process then reverses down.


基本面（买或卖的价值）决定整体方向，技术面决定实际的转折点。市场始终在探求价值，而价值就是价格走过头的地方；这种探求也始终发生在支撑位和阻力位上。任何时候的一份报告或一条消息，都可能改变基本面（对价值的感知），足以让市场沿趋势上行或下行几分钟到好几天。持续数月的主要反转基于基本面，其起点和终点都在支撑位和阻力位上。这对每一个市场和每一个时间级别都成立。


> The fundamentals (the value in buying or selling) determine the overall direction, but the technicals determine the actual turning points. The market is always probing for value, which is an excess, and is always at support and resistance levels. Reports and news items at any time can alter the fundamentals (the perception of value) enough to make the market trend up or down for minutes to several days. Major reversals lasting for months are based on fundamentals and begin and end at support and resistance levels. This is true of every market and every time frame.


有一点必须认识到：市场从重要顶部开始转下之后，消息面仍在把基本面报道成看多；市场从重要底部转上之后，消息面仍在把它报道成看空。消息面依然认为市场看多或看空，并不意味着机构也这么看。要交易走势图，而不是交易消息面。价格才是真相，市场总是领先于消息面。事实上，消息面在市场顶部最看多，在市场底部最看空。记者们陷在狂喜或绝望之中，四处寻找专家来解释为什么这个趋势如此强劲、还会持续更久。他们会忽视最聪明的交易者，甚至可能根本不知道那些人是谁。那些交易者感兴趣的是赚钱，不是新闻，也不会主动去找记者。当一位记者打车上班、司机告诉他，自己刚刚卖掉了所有股票、把房子也抵押了，就为了买黄金，记者便兴奋起来，迫不及待要找一个看多的专家上节目，来印证自己对黄金多头市场的深刻洞见。“你想想，市场这么强，连我的出租车司机都在买黄金！所以所有人都会卖掉其他资产、买进更多，市场接下来好几个月只能一路猛涨！”在我看来，当连最弱的交易者终于都进场时，就再也没有人可买了。市场需要一个愿意在更高处接盘的更傻的傻瓜，好让你能带着利润卖出。当再也没有人可买时，市场就只剩一个方向，而它恰好与消息面告诉你的一切相反。电视上那些能言善辩、教授模样的专家没完没了地露面，用博学的论证说明黄金不可能下跌、事实上明年还会再翻一倍，要抗拒他们很难。但你必须认识到，他们出现在那里是为了自我吹嘘和娱乐大众。电视台需要这种娱乐来吸引观众和广告收入。如果你想知道机构究竟在做什么，就去看走势图。机构太大了，藏不住；如果你懂得怎么读图，你就能看到它们在做什么、市场要往哪里走，而这通常与你在电视上看到的任何东西都无关。


> It is important to realize that the news will report the fundamentals as still bullish after the market has begun to turn down from a major top, and still bearish after it has turned up from a major bottom. Just because the news still sees the market as bullish or bearish does not mean that the institutions do. Trade the charts and not the news. Price is truth and the market always leads the news. In fact, the news is always the most bullish at market tops and most bearish at market bottoms. The reporters get caught up in the euphoria or despair and search for pundits who will explain why the trend is so strong and will continue much longer. They will ignore the smartest traders, and probably do not even know who they are. Those traders are interested in making money, not news, and will not seek out the reporters. When a reporter takes a cab to work and the driver tells him that he just sold all of his stocks and mortgaged his house so that he could buy gold, the reporter gets excited and can't wait to find a bullish pundit to put on the air to confirm the reporter's profound insight in the gold bull market. “Just think, the market is so strong that even my cabbie is buying gold! Everyone will therefore sell all of their other assets and buy more, and the market will have to race higher for many more months!” To me, when even the weakest traders finally enter the market, there is no one left to buy. The market needs a greater fool who is willing to buy higher so that you can sell out with a profit. When there is no one left, the market can only go one way, and it is the opposite of what the news is telling you. It is difficult to resist the endless parade of persuasive professorial pundits on television who are giving erudite arguments about how gold cannot go down and in fact will double again over the next year. However, you have to realize that they are there for their own self-aggrandizement and for entertainment. The network needs the entertainment to attract viewers and advertising dollars. If you want to know what the institutions are really doing, just look at the charts. The institutions are too big to hide and if you understand how to read charts, you will see what they are doing and where the market is heading, and it is usually unrelated to anything that you see on television.


大多数重要顶部并非来自由巨量K线和巨量成交构成的高潮——那种情形在重要底部更常见。更常见的是，顶部来自一个交易区间，比如双顶或头肩顶，随后以空头急速行情的形式突破。不过，顶部也可能以高潮的方式出现，底部也可能呈现为交易区间。


> Most major tops do not come from climaxes made of huge bars and volume, which are more common at major bottoms. More often, a top comes from a trading range, like a double top or a head and shoulders top, followed by a breakout in the form of a bear spike. However, tops can be climactic, and bottoms can be trading ranges.


后面讲交易区间的章节、以及第1册讲通道的章节，会说明如何利用支撑和阻力下单。举例来说，交易者会在通道或其他类型交易区间的底部附近买入、在顶部附近做空，然后在回测通道或交易区间的另一侧时止盈并反手。


> The chapters on trading ranges (further on) and channels (in book 1) describe how to use support and resistance to place trades. For example, traders will buy near the bottom of a channel or other type of trading range and short near the top, and then take profits and reverse on the test of the other side of the channel or trading range.


在强趋势中，市场会越过大多数磁力位。举例来说，在一段多头趋势里，新手交易者会发现，这波上涨行情远远越过了他们画出的每一个等距运动目标位和趋势通道线。这些新手会错误地在每一个自以为的阻力位上做空，结果眼睁睁看着亏损一整天不断扩大。他们错误地不断做空那些看起来很棒、实际上很糟的顶部，又拒绝买入那些看起来很差、实际上很好的回调。然而，一旦终于出现回调或反转，它一定发生在某个阻力位上。即便在强趋势中，等距运动目标位也常常精确到最小报价单位。显然，部分原因是计算机能准确地算出它们。计算机控制着市场，它们的止盈必然发生在某个算出来的价位，而那个价位总是某个磁力位。此外，如果一笔交易勉强算“好”——也就是说这个策略是盈利的——那么回报至少要与风险一样大，才能形成正的交易者等式。这通常会导致回报一旦达到风险的大小时就出现一部分止盈盘，因为这是让策略盈利的最低要求。小波段常常精确地结束在等距运动目标位处，而许多强趋势正好结束在某个重要的等距运动目标位处、或者在离它1个最小报价单位之内，因为价格被吸向了磁力位。


> In a strong trend, the market extends beyond most magnets. For example, in a bull trend, beginning traders will discover that the rally continues up far beyond every measured move target and trend channel line that they draw. These beginners will mistakenly be shorting at every perceived resistance level, finding their losses growing all day long. They incorrectly keep shorting tops that look great but are bad, and refuse to buy pullbacks that look bad but are great. However, once there finally is a pullback or a reversal, it will always occur at a resistance level. Even in strong trends, measured move targets often work precisely to the tick. Obviously, this is in part because computers can calculate them accurately. Computers control the market and their profit taking has to be at some calculated level, which is always at some magnet. Additionally, if a trade is minimally “good,” meaning that the strategy is profitable, the reward has to be at least as large as the risk to create a positive trader's equation. This usually results in some profit taking once the reward reaches the size of the risk, because this is the minimum level that the market has to reach to make the strategy profitable. Minor swings often end precisely at measured move projections, and many strong trends end exactly at, or within a tick, of a significant measured move target, as the price gets vacuumed to the magnet.


![图 PII.1](figures/fig-PII-1.jpg)


**图 PII.1　道琼斯工业平均指数月线图**


道琼斯工业平均指数的月线图（图 PII.1）展示了几种类型的支撑和阻力（它们全都是磁力位）。


> The monthly chart of the Dow Jones Industrial Average (Figure PII.1) shows several types of support and resistance (all are magnets).


趋势线和趋势通道线是重要的支撑和阻力区域。2009年崩盘的底部在第18根K线处，它从一条月线趋势线下方反转向上——这条线从1987年崩盘的低点画到1990年10月的回调处。它同时还位于由第8根和第12根K线形成的趋势通道线上（构成决斗线形态，后文会有专门一节讨论）。空头市场中所有重要的向上反转都发生在支撑处，所有顶部都发生在阻力处，但大多数支撑和阻力都挡不住趋势。不过，如果出现一个强势反转形态、并且恰好形成在某个支撑位或阻力位上，机构就会止盈，许多人甚至会建立反方向的仓位。市场底部更常来自卖出高潮，比如1987年和2009年的崩盘。市场顶部更常来自交易区间，比如第9根和第15根K线附近。


> Trend lines and trend channel lines are important support and resistance areas. The bar 18 bottom of the 2009 crash reversed up from below a monthly trend line drawn from the 1987 crash low to the October 1990 pullback. It also was at the trend channel line created by bars 8 and 12 (creating a dueling lines pattern, discussed in a later section). All major reversals up from bear markets occur at support and all tops occur at resistance, but most support and resistance do not stop trends. However, if there is a strong reversal pattern and it forms at a support or resistance level, institutions will take profits and many will even enter in the other direction. Market bottoms more often come from sell climaxes, like the crashes of 1987 and 2009. Market tops more often come from trading ranges, like around bars 9 and 15.


第15根K线的高点接近一个向上等距运动目标位，该目标位依据第12根到第13根K线这波多头急速行情的高度测算。


> The bar 15 high was close to a measured move up based on the height of the bar 12 to bar 13 bull spike.


均线反复起支撑作用，比如在第3、4、6、8、14和20根K线处；也反复起阻力作用，比如在第11和17根K线处。


> The moving average repeatedly acted as support, like at bars 3, 4, 6, 8, 14, and 20, and resistance, like at bars 11 and 17.


交易区间起支撑和阻力的作用。向下突破第9根K线处交易区间的那次突破，成为第11根K线那波上涨行情的阻力；第15根K线处的交易区间则成为第17根K线那波上涨行情的阻力。市场上涨到第15根K线之后，第16根K线在第9根K线处交易区间的顶部找到支撑。摆动高点和低点也起支撑和阻力的作用。第12根K线在第8根K线的低点找到支撑，形成一个双底。第13根K线与第11根K线形成一个双顶，但市场随后横盘，很快向上突破了那道阻力。


> Trading ranges act as support and resistance. The breakout below the bar 9 trading range was resistance to the bar 11 rally, and the bar 15 trading range was resistance to the bar 17 rally. Once the market rallied up to bar 15, bar 16 found support at the top of the bar 9 trading range. Swing highs and lows act as support and resistance. Bar 12 found support at the bar 8 low and formed a double bottom. Bar 13 formed a double top with bar 11, but the market went sideways and soon broke above that resistance.


![图 PII.2](figures/fig-PII-2.jpg)


**图 PII.2　支撑可以变成阻力，阻力也可以变成支撑**


在图 PII.2所示的 Emini 小型合约5分钟图上，支撑变成了阻力，阻力变成了支撑。均线和趋势线都是如此。


> Support became resistance and resistance became support in the 5 minute Emini chart shown in Figure PII.2. This was true for both the moving average and for trend lines.


第1、2、5、6、17、18、19和20根K线在向均线上涨的行情中遇到卖方，第7、8、13、15和16根K线则在向均线的微小回调中遇到买方。


> Bars 1, 2, 5, 6, 17, 18, 19, and 20 found sellers on rallies to the moving average, and bars 7, 8, 13, 15, and 16 found buyers on minor pullbacks to the moving average.


第12、13、15和16根K线是对均线的反复回测；买方得不到回报，很快就不再买入这些回调。市场随后跌破均线，空头开始对向均线上涨的小行情做空，形成一连串更低的高点和更低的低点。


> Bars 12, 13, 15, and 16 were repeated tests of the moving average, and the buyers were not getting rewarded and soon stopped buying the pullbacks. The market then fell below the moving average and the bears began to short small rallies up to the moving average, creating a series of lower highs and lows.


那条多头趋势线是一条最优拟合线，画它的目的是让尽可能多的K线去回测它。买方显然在趋势线一带买入，而它被回测了十几次，却始终没有出现脱离趋势线的急剧上涨行情。这种缺乏加速的状态让多头随时间推移越发谨慎，最终他们不再愿意在趋势线一带买入。市场一旦跌破趋势线，多头就更加犹豫，开始卖出多头仓位，空头则变得更加激进。更低的高点和低点形成，交易者开始画空头趋势线，在上涨行情中做空。


> The bull trend line was a best fit line drawn with the objective of having as many bars as possible test it. Buyers were clearly buying in the area of the trend line, and it was tested more than a dozen times without a sharp rally away from the trend line. This lack of acceleration made the bulls more cautious over time, and eventually they became unwilling to buy in the area of the trend line. Once the market fell below the trend line, bulls became even more hesitant to buy, and began to sell out of their longs, and bears became more aggressive. Lower highs and lows formed and traders began to draw bear trend lines where they shorted rallies.


顺便说一句，任何向上倾斜的通道都应该被看作熊旗，即便它是多头市场的一部分——因为最终总会出现跌破趋势线的动作，而从交易的角度看，市场会表现得像这个通道是一个熊旗一样。同样，任何向下倾斜的通道都应该被看作牛旗，它最终的突破也应当按多头行情段已经在进行的方式来交易。


> Incidentally, any upward-sloping channel should be thought of as a bear flag, even if it is part of a bull market, because eventually there will be a break below the trend line and the market will behave as if the channel was a bear flag for trading purposes. Likewise, any downward-sloping channel should be thought of as a bull flag and its eventual breakout should be traded as if a bull leg is underway.


# 第 7 章　基于第一段行情（急速行情）幅度的等距运动

*7. Measured Moves Based on the Size of the First Leg (the Spike)*


等距运动，指的是一段与先前同方向的某段行情幅度相等的行情。市场第一波走了多远，你就据此估算它第二波会走多远。等距运动为什么成立？因为只要你在寻找等距运动，就说明你相信自己已经看清了始终入场（always in）的方向，而这通常意味着你至少有60% 的把握这一运动会发生。等距运动通常以一段急速行情或一个交易区间的高度为基础测算，初始的保护性止损通常放在第一段行情的起点之外。举例来说，如果出现一波强劲的买入急速行情，那么初始保护性止损就放在这段急速行情最低点下方一个最小报价单位处。如果这段急速行情极其巨大，交易者很少愿意冒那么大的风险，而且他们通常仍能拿到一笔能盈利的交易，但理论上，止损依然放在急速行情之外。另外，这一概率常常高于60%。如果这段急速行情约有4个点高，那么风险就约是4个点。既然你相信等距运动会发生，也相信“在急速行情顶部买入”这个策略站得住脚，那你就是在用4个点的风险去赌一个60% 概率的事件。数学规律决定了：你这个信念（当概率为60% 时该策略会盈利）只有在回报至少与风险一样大时才成立。第25章讨论交易的数学时会讲到这一点。也就是说，这个策略要奏效，你需要有60% 的机会赚到至少4个点，也就是等距运动目标位。换句话说，这个策略唯一能成立的方式，就是等距运动目标位在约60% 的情况下被触及。既然交易趋势是所有交易方式中最可靠的一种，那么假如世上真有管用的策略，这一个必定是其中之一。这就是等距运动成立的原因吗？没有人能确切知道，但它是一个说得通的解释，也是我自己能想象出的最好的解释。


> A measured move is a swing that is equal in size to a prior swing in the same direction. You estimate how far the market will go on its second attempt based on how far it went on its first. Why do measured moves work? If you are looking for a measured move, then you believe that you know the always-in direction, which means that you are probably at least 60 percent certain that the move will occur. The measured move is usually based on the height of a spike or trading range, and the initial protective stop is usually beyond the beginning of the first move. For example, if there is a strong buy spike, then the initial protective stop is one tick below the low of the spike. If the spike is huge, traders will rarely risk that much, and will usually still have a profitable trade, but the theoretical stop is still below the spike. Also, the probability is often more than 60 percent. If the spike is about four points tall, then the risk is about four points. Since you believe that the measured move will occur and that the strategy of buying at the top of the spike is sound, then you are risking four points on a 60 percent bet. Mathematics dictates that your belief (that the strategy will be profitable when the probability is 60 percent) will be true only if the reward is at least as big as the risk. This is discussed in Chapter 25 about the mathematics of trading. This means that for the strategy to work, you need to have a 60 percent chance of making at least four points, which is the measured move target. In other words, the only way that the strategy works is if the measured move target is hit about 60 percent of the time. Since trading a trend is the most reliable form of trading, if there ever are strategies that work, then this has to be one. Is this the reason why measured moves work? No one knows for sure, but it is a plausible explanation, and the best that I have imagined.


大多数等距运动要么以急速行情为基础，要么以交易区间为基础。以急速行情为基础的那种，通常会引出一个交易区间；以交易区间为基础的那种，通常会引出一段急速行情。举个例子，双顶属于一种交易区间，一旦向上或向下的突破抵达等距运动的位置，交易者往往会先止盈一部分。交易者有时会去寻找突破，而突破本身就是急速行情；急速行情一旦走到等距运动区域，他们通常就会预期出现一些止盈。如果这波突破伴随着强劲的急速行情，而且在等距运动目标位处没有出现明显的停顿，那么这段急速行情本身常常会引出一个以急速行情高度为基础测算的等距运动。市场一旦走到那里，交易者往往会开始止盈，结果通常就是一个交易区间。


> Most measured moves are based either on spikes or on trading ranges. When one is based on a spike, it usually leads to a trading range; and when it is based on a trading range, it usually leads to a spike. For example, if there is a double top, which is a type of trading range, traders will often take partial profits once the breakout up or down reaches a measured move. Traders look for a breakout, which is a spike, and they usually expect some profit taking once the spike has reached the measured move area. If the breakout was with a strong spike and there is no significant pause at the measured move target, the spike itself often leads to a measured move based on the height of the spike. Once the market gets there, traders will often begin to take profits and the result will usually be a trading range.


强劲行情出现回调之后，通常还会有同方向的第二段行情，而它的幅度往往与第一段行情大致相当。这个思路就是几项可靠技术的基础，用它们可以推算第二段行情可能在哪里结束。那个等距运动区域，是你为顺势仓位止盈的合理位置；之后你可以等下一次回调，重建仓位。如果出现了强劲的反转建仓形态，也可以考虑做一笔逆势交易。


> Once there is a pullback from a strong move, there is usually a second leg in the same direction, and it is often approximately the same size as the first leg. This concept is the basis for a few reliable techniques to project a possible target for the end of that second leg. That measured move area is a reasonable place to take profits on your trend position, and then you can wait for another pullback to reestablish your position. If there is a strong reversal setup, you can also consider a countertrend trade.


市场急速走出一段行情后回调，接下来很可能有第二段行情，而第二段的幅度常常与第一段大致相等。这就是“第1段行情 = 第2段行情”的走势，但它也被称作 ABC 走势，或 AB = CD。这套字母叫法很容易造成混乱，所以更简单的做法是：把这两段行情直接叫作第1段行情和第2段行情，把第1段行情之后的回调就叫作回调。字母标记之所以让人糊涂，是因为在 AB = CD 结构里，B、C、D 对应的其实是 ABC 走势里的 A、B、C。ABC 走势中的 B 段就是那段回调，它在市场轮廓图（Market Profile，芝商所集团绘制的价格与时间信息图）上会形成一块密集成交区。任何密集成交区的中部，常常都会引出一段等距运动，而这里的目标位与按 AB = CD 测算出的目标位相同。比如，在多头趋势里做 AB = CD 测算：从 A 点出发，加上 AB 段的长度（也就是 B – A），再加到 C 上，就得到 C + (B – A)。就密集成交区来说：你从 A 出发，加上 AB 段的长度（也就是 B – A），再往下回到该密集成交区一半的位置（也就是减去 BC 段的一半），然后加上“B 的高度减去 BC 密集成交区的一半”这个高度，从 BC 密集成交区的中部向上量出等距运动目标位。两个式子都等于 C + (B – A)，因此给出同一个等距运动目标位。这套算法实在太复杂，而且无关紧要，因为你不该仅仅根据斐波那契扩展、等距运动或任何其它磁力位，就用限价单去反向操作这段行情。它们只是提供一个路标：在价格靠近它们之前，让你一直顺势交易；而当价格接近时，你也可以考虑逆势建仓形态。


> When a market makes a sharp move and then has a pullback, it will likely have a second leg and the second leg is frequently approximately the same size as the first. This is a leg 1 = leg 2 move, but it is also called an ABC move or an AB = CD. This alphabetical terminology is confusing, and it is simpler to just refer to the two moves as leg 1 and leg 2, and the pullback after leg 1 as simply the pullback. The confusion with the alphabetical labeling is that in the AB = CD pattern, the B, C, and D correspond to the A, B, and C of the ABC move. The B leg of an ABC is the pullback and it creates a thick area on a Market Profile (CME Group's graph of price and time information). The middle of any thick area often leads to a measured move, and here the target is the same as the one based on AB = CD. For example, for the AB = CD in a bull trend, if you start at point A and add the length of the AB leg (which is B – A), then add that to C, you get C + (B – A). For the thick area, you start at A and then add the length of the AB leg (which is B – A), then move back down to one-half of the thick area (so subtract half of the BC leg), and then add the height of B minus one-half of the BC thick area to get the measured move up from the middle of the BC thick area. Both equations equal C + (B – A) and therefore give the same measured move projection. This is way too complicated, and it is of minor importance because you should not be fading the move with a limit order solely based on Fibonacci extensions or measured moves or any other magnet. They just provide a guide to keep you trading with the trend until they are approached, and at that point you can consider counter-trend setups as well.


除了那些能引出等距运动的清晰回调入场点之外，有时还会出现一种更隐蔽、但同样有效的情形。当市场先走出一段强趋势行情，接着是一段相当强的回调行情段，随后又进入一个交易区间时，交易者可以用这个区间的大致中部，来推算回调的第二段可能走到哪里。随着交易区间逐步展开，你要不断调整那条线，把它放在你估计的中点上；等到行情最终走完第二段之后，它通常会落在回调的中点附近。它只是充当一个路标：提示你应该在哪里预期两段式回调结束，以及市场在哪里搭建交易以恢复趋势。你也可以直接使用“第1段行情 = 第2段行情”的等距运动测量法。比如在一个两段式牛旗里，量出向下的第一段行情的长度，再从回调的顶部减去这个高度，就找到回调第二段向下可能结束的合理位置。


> In addition to clear pullback entries that set up measured moves, sometimes there is a more subtle situation that is equally valid. When a market has a strong trend move and then a fairly strong pullback leg, and then a trading range, traders can use the approximate middle of the range to project where the second leg of the pullback might reach. As the trading range unfolds, keep adjusting the line to where you estimate the midpoint is, and that will usually be around the midpoint of the pullback once the move has finally completed its second leg. This just serves as a guide to where you should be anticipating the two-legged pullback to end and for the market to set up a trade for a resumption of the trend. You can also simply use a leg 1 = leg 2 measurement. For example, in a two-legged bull flag, take the length of the first leg down and subtract that height from the top of the pullback to find a reasonable location for where the second leg down of the pullback might end.


急速与通道类趋势里还有一种变体：通道的高度往往与急速行情的高度大致相同。急速行情很强时尤其如此，比如它由格外大的趋势K线组成，或者由好几根重叠很少、影线很短的强趋势K线组成。出现强劲急速行情时，市场常常会走出一次等距运动，方向上可上可下，但通常是顺着趋势方向，测算的基准是急速行情第一根与最后一根K线的开盘价、收盘价、最高价或最低价的某种组合。比如，如果出现一波巨大的多头急速行情，就量出从急速行情第一根K线开盘价，到最后一根K线收盘价的点数，再把这个点数加到那根最后一根K线的收盘价上。其后的通道通常会在那个区域遇到一些阻力，市场随后往往会向下修正到通道底部。这个等距运动目标位，就是你可以为多头仓位止盈的区域。有时候，市场也可能从急速行情第一根K线的最低点量到最后一根K线的收盘价或最高价，或者从第一根K线的开盘价量到最后一根K线的最高价，所以稳妥的做法是把所有可能性都看一遍。比较少的情况是，市场不会形成多少向上的通道，而是反转向下、跌破急速行情底部，然后走出一次向下的等距运动。


> There is a variation of this in spike and channel trends where the height of the channel is often about the same as the height of the spike. This is especially true when the spike is strong, like one with exceptionally large trend bars or several strong trend bars with little overlap and small tails. When there is a strong spike, the market often makes a measured move in either direction, but usually in the with-trend direction based on some combination of the open, close, high, or low of the first and last bars of the spike. For example, if there is a huge bull spike, take the number of points from the open of the first bar of the spike to the close of the final bar of the spike and add that to the close of that final bar of the spike. The channel that follows usually will find some resistance in that area and the market will often then correct down to the bottom of the channel. This measured move target is an area where you can take profits on your long position. Sometimes the market might make a measured move from the low of the first bar of the spike to the close or high of the final bar of the spike, or from the open of the first bar to the high of the final bar, so it is prudent to look at all the possibilities. Less often, the market will not form much of a channel up and will reverse to below the bottom of the spike, and then make a measured move down.


有一点要牢记：大多数时候，市场都处在某种交易区间之中，因此上下等幅运动（equidistant move）的方向概率是50%。也就是说，市场向上走 X 个点，与向下走同样 X 个点的可能性一样大。当存在趋势时，趋势方向上的胜算更好。出现强劲急速行情时，后续行情出现的概率可能是60%，如果整体图形与一轮强趋势行情相符，有时甚至能达到70%。另外，当市场处在交易区间底部时，概率偏向上涨；当市场处在区间顶部时，概率偏向下跌。这是市场惯性所致——市场倾向于延续它一直在做的事情。如果它在走趋势，胜算偏向趋势延续；如果它在交易区间里，胜算偏向突破尝试会失败。事实上，大约80% 的趋势反转尝试都会失败，所以你应该等它们演变成回调，然后顺着趋势方向入场。同样，有80% 的突破交易区间尝试也会失败，而从数学上看，在交易区间的顶部与底部反向操作，比在区间顶部附近买入大型多头趋势K线、在区间底部附近卖空大型空头趋势K线合理得多。


> It is important to remember that most of the time the market is in some kind of trading range and therefore the directional probability of an equidistant move is 50 percent. This means that the market is as likely to go up X number of points as it is to go down that same number of points. When there is a trend, the odds are better in the trend direction. When there is a strong spike, the odds of follow-through might be 60 percent and sometimes even 70 percent if the overall chart pattern is consistent with a strong trend move. Also, when the market is at the bottom of a trading range, the probability favors a move up; and when it is at the top of the range, the probability favors a move down. This is because of market inertia, which means that the market tends to continue what is has been doing. If it is trending, the odds favor more trending, and if it is in a trading range, the odds favor that breakout attempts will fail. In fact, about 80 percent of trend reversal attempts fail, and that is why you should wait for them to evolve into pullbacks and then enter in the direction of the trend. Also, 80 percent of attempts to break out of a trading range fail, and it makes far more mathematical sense to fade the tops and bottoms of the trading range than it does to buy large bull trend bars near the top and short large bear trend bars near the bottom.


下面这个等距运动的例子用到了几个假设。当时有一波强劲的多头急速行情，由三根多头趋势K线组成，它突破了某个交易区间。紧接着的那一根K线是一根小十字星K线，这个停顿说明急速行情在前一根K线上就结束了——那是连续多头趋势K线里的最后一根。这波突破很强，因为K线之间的重叠非常少，每根K线的开盘价都位于前一根K线收盘价处或更高。所有K线中最长的影线也只有两个最小报价单位，还有几根K线的下方没有影线。第一根K线高3个半点（14个最小报价单位），第二根K线高10个最小报价单位，第三根K线高8个最小报价单位，第四根K线有一个最小报价单位的阳线实体，但下方有3个最小报价单位的影线、上方有2个最小报价单位的影线。那根十字星是第一次失去动能的K线，因此它告诉你急速行情已经在前一根K线结束。第一根K线的开盘价比急速行情中第三根、也就是最后一根多头趋势K线的收盘价低8个点，所以这波急速行情至少应当被视为高8个点。你可以用第一根K线的最低点量到第三根K线的最高点，甚至可以用第四根十字星K线的最高点，但做初步推算时，用较小的那个数字更为保守。如果第二段行情超过了这个目标位，那就去看其它目标位。


> Here is an example of a measured move that uses several assumptions. There was a strong bull spike made of three bull trend bars that broke out of a trading range. The next bar was a small doji bar, and this pause meant that the spike ended on the prior bar, which was the last of the consecutive bull trend bars. The breakout was strong because there was very little overlap between the bars, with the open of each bar at or above the close of the prior bar. The biggest tail on any bar was only two ticks, and a couple of bars had no tail on the bottom. The first bar was three and a half points (14 ticks) tall, the second bar was 10 ticks tall, the third bar was eight ticks tall, and the fourth bar had a one-tick bull body but a three-tick tail on the bottom and a two-tick tail on the top. That doji was the first bar that lacked momentum and it therefore told you that the spike had ended on the previous bar. The open of the first bar was eight points below the close of the third and final bull trend bar in the spike, so the spike should be thought of as being eight points tall, at a minimum. You could use the low of the first bar to the high of the third bar or even the high of the doji fourth bar, but it is more conservative to use the smaller figure for your initial projection. If the second leg surpasses this target, then look at other targets.


在这波急速行情形成的过程中，不管你什么时候买进，这笔交易的止损可能得放在急速行情底部之下。为便于讨论，假设你把风险控制在急速行情第一根K线开盘价下方一个最小报价单位处。如果在急速行情高3个点的时候，你在最高价那个最小报价单位处用市价单买入，那么你就是冒着约3个点的风险去赚至少3个点。那一刻你相信市场会走出一次向上的等距运动，幅度等于急速行情的高度，也就是3个点。你知道自己的止损在哪里；虽然还不知道急速行情的顶部会在哪里，但你知道它至少不会低于你的买入价。既然你相信市场正在走趋势，你就会觉得胜算优于50–50：市场在下跌并触及下方3个点处的止损之前，会先向上走3个点。


> As that spike was forming, if you bought at any point, your stop on your trade might have to be below the bottom of the spike. For argument's sake, assume that you would risk to one tick below the open of the first bar of the spike. If you bought at the market at the highest tick when the spike was three points tall, then you would be risking about three points to make at least three points. At that moment, you believed that the market would have a measured move up equal to the height of the spike, which was three points tall. You knew where your stop was, and you didn't yet know where the top of the spike would be, but you knew that it would be at least as high as where you bought. Since you believed that the market was trending, you felt that the odds were better than 50–50 that the market would go up three points before it fell and hit that stop three points below.


当急速行情继续扩大到7个点之后，你改变了自己的评估。你现在认为，既然市场仍在走趋势，那么胜算至少有50–50：市场在下跌7个点之前，会先再向上走7个点。此时，在这笔你本来只期望赚3个点、并为此冒着3个点风险的交易上，你已经有4个点的浮动盈利。如果你愿意，可以在那时仍在形成的急速行情的最高的那个最小报价单位处加仓，这样你的风险就变成7个点（也许还要多几个最小报价单位，因为你多半会想把风险控制在急速行情第一根K线底部下方一个最小报价单位处），而你的止盈目标也相应提高7个点。不过，就你最初那笔多头仓位而言，你仍然只冒着3个点的风险，但现在赚到总共11个点的机会已超过50%（其中4个点来自你的入场价到当前急速行情顶部，之后再赚7个点）。


> After the spike continued to grow to seven points, you changed your assessment. You now believed that since the market was still trending, the odds were at least 50–50 that the market would go up seven more points before it fell seven points. At the moment, you already had four points of open profit on a trade where you were hoping for three while you risked three. If you wanted, you could have bought more at the high tick of the spike, which was still forming, and then your risk would have been seven points (maybe a few ticks more since you would probably have wanted to risk to one tick below the bottom of the first bar of the spike), and your profit target would be seven points higher. However, on your initial long, you were still risking three points but now had better than a 50 percent chance of making a total of 11 points (the four from your entry to the current top of the spike, and then seven more).


等到第四根K线（也就是那根十字星）形成之后，你就知道这波向上的急速行情已经在前一根K线的收盘价处结束，而这个收盘价比急速行情第一根K线的开盘价高8个点。这时你会得出结论：市场在下跌8个点、跌破急速行情第一根K线的开盘价或底部之前，有超过50% 的机会先向上再走8个点、高于急速行情的收盘价（下跌一侧可能要比8个点再多一两个最小报价单位，因为最安全的止损放在急速行情起点之外）。由于这波急速行情如此强劲，概率很可能超过60%。


> Once that fourth bar formed, which was a doji, you then knew that the spike up had ended at the close of the prior bar, eight points above the open of the first bar of the spike. At that point, you would have concluded that the market had more than a 50 percent chance of going up eight more points above the close of the spike before falling eight points to below the open or bottom of the spike (maybe a tick or two more than eight points on the downside, since the safest stop was beyond the start of the spike). Since the spike was so strong, the probability was likely more than 60 percent.


急速行情一结束，双向交易就开始了，此时不确定性上升。市场以横盘至下跌的方式展开修正，随后向上的通道开始了。尽管市场有可能从这个回调的底部起走出一次“第1段行情 = 第2段行情”的上涨行情——其中急速行情是第1段，通道是第2段——但当急速行情非常强劲时，更可靠的目标位是以急速行情第一根K线开盘价量到最后一根K线收盘价的那个。随着市场上行，价格走高的概率会慢慢被消磨。当多头通道走到距离等距运动目标位大约一半的路程时，上下等幅运动的方向概率又回落到50% 到55% 左右，不确定性再次变得非常高。记住，多头通道之后通常会出现一段回到通道底部的下跌，然后至少有一次反弹，所以这个多头通道其实是一个尚未成形的交易区间的第一段。一旦市场走到等距运动目标区域，那里很可能就是这个初生区间的上沿，胜算偏向下跌。所有交易区间都是如此。这一区域是为多头仓位止盈的绝佳位置；而正因为有那么多交易者在等距运动区域止盈，市场就开始回调。在多头仓位回撤到通道底部附近之前，也就是通常在那里形成一个双底之前，大多数交易者不会再积极买入。这个区域同时也是一处磁力位。多头重新开始买入，而在通道顶部做空的那批空头会止盈离场。由于市场此时处在正在形成的交易区间底部附近，方向概率略微偏向多头。


> As soon as the spike ended, two-sided trading began, and at that point uncertainty increased. The market corrected sideways to down and then the channel up began. Although the market might have made a leg 1 = leg 2 move up from the bottom of this pullback, where the spike was leg 1 and the channel was leg 2, when a spike is very strong, the more reliable target is the one based on the open of the first bar of the spike to the close of the final bar of the spike. As the market rallies, the probability of higher prices slowly erodes. When the bull channel reached about half of the distance to the measured move target, the directional probability of an equidistant move fell back to around 50 to 55 percent and uncertainty once again was very high. Remember, a bull channel is usually followed by a move back down to the bottom of the channel and then at least a bounce, so the bull channel was actually the first leg of a trading range that had not yet formed. Once the market made it to the measured move target area, it was likely the high end of that incipient range, and the odds favored a move down. This is true of all trading ranges. This is an excellent area to take profits on your longs, and because so many traders take profits in the area of the measured move, the market begins to pull back. Most traders will not look to buy aggressively again until the market retraces to around the bottom of the channel, where a double bottom usually forms. This area is also a magnet. The bulls begin to buy again and the bears who shorted at the top of the channel will take profits. Since the market is now around the bottom of the developing trading range, the directional probability slightly favors the bulls.


一旦市场进入交易区间，上下等幅运动的方向概率就又一次变成50–50——只要市场位于该区间的中部附近。如果你的风险是 X 个点，那么你有50% 的机会在止损被触及之前赚到 X 个点，也有50% 的机会在止盈目标达成之前亏掉 X 个点。这是市场相对有效的副产品。大多数时候，市场是有效的，在亏掉 X 个点之前先赚到 X 个点的胜算接近50–50。最佳交易出现在胜算优于50–50的时候，但这种机会常常出现在急速行情期间——急速行情情绪化、变化快，而且很难进场。交易者明白这一点，这正是急速行情能在毫无回调的情况下涨得如此之快的原因。交易者一路加仓，因为他们知道：在急速行情结束之前，赚到的点数不少于所冒风险的胜算优于50–50；只有等到通道明确展开之后，胜算才会回落到大约50–50。在这波急速行情形成的时候，他们并不知道市场走高之前是否会有回调，但他们确信近期它会走高。与其等待一场可能永远不会来的回调、从而错过一波强劲的交易，他们选择用市价单买入，或者在一到四个最小报价单位的回调中买入，并把风险控制在急速行情底部附近。急速行情之所以会形成，靠的就是这种急切；而随之增加的风险，也让许多交易者望而却步。大多数初学者不愿意冒3到7个点的风险。其实他们只需买入一个小仓位——也许是自己常规规模的四分之一——然后接受这个风险，因为机构正是这么做的。机构懂数学，所以不怕做这笔交易。


> Once the market enters the trading range, the directional probability of an equidistant move is again 50–50 whenever the market is near the middle of that range. If your risk is X points, you have a 50 percent chance of making X points before your stop is hit, and a 50 percent chance of losing X points before your profit target is reached. This is a by-product of the markets being relatively efficient. Most of the time, they are efficient and the odds of making X points before losing X points are close to 50–50. The best trading occurs when the odds are better than 50–50, but this often occurs during spikes, which are emotional, fast moving, and difficult to enter. Traders understand this and that is why the spike grows so quickly without any pullbacks. Traders keep adding to their positions all the way up because they know that until the spike ends, the odds of making as much as they are risking are better than 50–50, and the odds fall to about 50–50 only once the channel is well underway. When that spike is forming, they do not know if there will be a pullback before the market goes higher, but they are confident that it will go higher in the near term. Rather than waiting for a pullback that may never come and therefore missing out on a strong trade, they buy at the market or on oneto four-tick pullbacks and risk to around the bottom of the spike. This urgency is behind the formation of spikes, and the increased risk keeps many traders away. Most beginners are unwilling to risk the three to seven points. Instead, they should simply buy a small position, maybe one-quarter of their normal size, and take the risk, because that is what the institutions are doing. They understand the math and therefore are not afraid to take the trade.


这种向50–50市场靠拢的过程，是所有等距运动交易的基础。胜算处于失衡状态，而向等距运动目标位上行的过程，就是一次试图恢复不确定性的过程。市场总会过靶，然后不得不折返，去重新逼近一个50–50的市场。等距运动区域是胜算的一次过靶，跨过之后胜算就短暂地偏向空头。等市场回撤到通道底部时，胜算又一次过靶，只不过这次偏向多头。当市场反弹回升、回到正在形成的交易区间中部时，胜算又重新回到50–50附近，市场也就恢复了平衡状态。


> This move toward a 50–50 market is the basis of all measured move trades. The odds are out of balance, and the rally to the measured move is an attempt to restore uncertainty. The market invariably overshoots and has to backtrack to home in on a 50–50 market. The measured move area is an overshoot of the odds, and they then briefly favor the bears. Once the market retraces to the bottom of the channel, the odds again overshoot, but this time in favor of the bulls. When the market bounces back up toward the middle of the developing trading range, the odds are once again around 50–50 and the market is in balance.


![图 7.1](figures/fig-07-01.jpg)


**图 7.1　第1段行情 = 第2段行情**


在图 7.1所示的日线图上，埃克森美孚（Exxon Mobil，XOM）从K线A到K线B走出了强劲的第一段上涨行情，于是交易者在K线C的更高的低点买入，搏一次可能的“第1段行情 = 第2段行情”上涨。K线D略微未及靶位（虚线顶部）。价格一旦进入目标区域，许多交易者就认为，在跌到K线A的那波抛售之后，这可能是他们眼中的一段两段式空头反弹。如果你用 ABC 标记，K线B就是 A 点，K线C就是 B 点，K线D就是 C 点；正因为这套标记容易造成混乱，更好的做法是直接把涨到K线B的那段行情叫作第1段行情，把跌到K线C的抛售叫作回调，把涨到K线D的上涨行情叫作第2段行情。


> Exxon Mobil (XOM) had a strong first leg up from bar A to bar B on the daily chart shown in Figure 7.1, so traders bought the bar C higher low for a possible leg 1 = leg 2 rally. Bar D slightly undershot the target (the top of the dashed line). Once in the area of the target, many traders saw what they thought might be two-legged bear rally after the sell-off to bar A. If you were to use ABC labeling, bar B is point A, bar C is point B, and bar D is point C, and because of this confusion, it is better to simply refer to the move up to bar B as leg 1, the sell-off down to C as the pullback, and the rally up to D as leg 2.


在K线E出现更高的低点、且上涨行情突破K线D之后，你可以把 AD 看作包含了两个更小行情段（AB 和 CD）的第一段行情，然后一直持有多头，直到走出一次向上的等距运动（AD = EF，目标位是实线的顶部）。


> Once there was a higher low at bar E and the rally broke above bar D, a trader could look at AD as a first leg that contains two smaller legs (AB and CD), and then stay long until there was a measured move up (AD = EF, and the target is the top of the solid line).


斐波那契交易者也会把其它扩展位（138%、150%、162% 等）视为寻找反转的有效区域，但这不但复杂，而且粗略。一旦市场明显表现出双向行为，想要找强烈信号就逢低买入、逢高卖出，可靠性并不比它差。


> Fibonacci traders also look to other extensions (138 percent, 150 percent, 162 percent, etc.) as valid areas in which to look for reversals, but this is too complicated and approximate. Once the market has clearly two-sided behavior, it is just as reliable to look to buy low and sell high whenever there is a strong signal.


![图 7.2](figures/fig-07-02.jpg)


**图 7.2　第1段行情 = 第2段行情的变体**


有时“第1段行情 = 第2段行情”的等距运动中，第1段行情并不是最初那波下跌的绝对低点。第一段下跌之后的向上修正，通常是一段两段式行情或一个楔形熊旗，但无论从哪一种形态出发，随后的回调常常会跌破修正段行情的起点，就像图 7.2中第6根K线那样。等到第9根K线形成、看起来像是第一段下跌之后回调的结束时，敏锐的交易者会接受这样一种可能：涨到第9根K线的这波修正，起点是第4根K线而不是第6根K线；因此他们认为第二段下跌可能等于“第1根K线到第4根K线”这第一段下跌，而不是“第1根K线到第6根K线”那一段。第12根K线的底部，正是以第4根K线作为第一段终点的“第1段行情 = 第2段行情”等距运动，精确到最小报价单位。如果市场反而继续下跌，那么交易者也会观察：当价格跌到以第6根K线作为第1段终点的“第1段行情 = 第2段行情”区域时，会发生什么。


> Sometimes a leg 1 = leg 2 measured move has a leg 1 that is not the absolute low of the initial sell-off. The correction up from the first leg down is usually a two-legged move or a wedge bear flag, but the pullback from either often falls below the beginning of the corrective leg, as it did in Figure 7.2 at bar 6. By the time bar 9 formed what appeared to be the end of the pullback from the first leg down, astute traders were open to the possibility that the correction up to bar 9 began at bar 4 and not bar 6, and therefore thought that the second leg down might be equal to the bar 1 to bar 4 first leg down instead of the bar 1 to bar 6 first leg down. The bottom of bar 12 was a perfect leg 1 = leg 2 measured move to the tick based on the bar 4 end of the first leg. If the market instead continued down, then traders would have watched to see what happened once it fell to the area of the leg 1 = leg 2 based on a leg 1 ending at bar 6.


为什么把第1段行情的终点考虑在第4根K线是合理的？因为交易者预期在第二段下跌开始之前会先出现一次向上的两段式回调，而从第6根K线到第9根K线的上涨处在一条通道之中，因此很可能只是一段行情。艾略特波浪交易者知道，向上的修正可以包含一段跌破最初下跌底部的回调，他们把这种横盘式的修正叫作平台形（flat）。这里的平台形就是涨到第5根K线的行情、跌到第6根K线的行情，以及涨到第9根K线的行情。另外，涨到第5根K线的那段行情是一波相当强劲的多头急速行情，因此它有可能就是这轮修正的起点。从那波急速行情回调到第6根K线，是一次更低低点回调，而更低低点回调很常见。所以，当这轮修正展开时，这种解释并不会让交易者感到困扰。


> Why did it make sense to consider the possibility that leg 1 ended at bar 4? Traders were looking for a two-legged pullback up before the second leg down began, and the move up from bar 6 to bar 9 was in a channel and therefore likely just one leg. Elliott Wave traders know that upward corrections can include a pullback that goes below the bottom of the initial move down, and they call this sideways type of correction a flat. The flat here would be the move up to bar 5, the move down to bar 6, and the move up to bar 9. Also, the move up to bar 5 was a reasonably strong bull spike and therefore it was a possible start of the correction. The pullback to bar 6 from that spike up was a lower low pullback, and lower low pullbacks are common. Therefore, as the correction was unfolding, traders were not troubled by this interpretation.


第5根和第8根K线构成了一个潜在的双顶熊旗，但向上突破到第9根K线排除了这种可能。不过，只要价格向上突破一个双顶，交易者就会盯着看它会不会失败。如果失败，这实际上就是一个楔形顶。三次向上推进包括：第5根和第8根K线组成的双顶，以及其后突破到第9根K线的突破失败。


> Bars 5 and 8 formed a potential double top bear flag, but the breakout to bar 9 eliminated that possibility. However, whenever there is a breakout above a double top, traders watch to see if it fails. If so, this effectively is a wedge top. The three pushes up are the bar 5 and bar 8 double top followed by the failed breakout to bar 9.


突破失败之后，市场向下急跌到第10根K线，交易者便认为从第1根K线高点开始的第二段下跌已经展开。


> Once the market spiked down to bar 10 after the failed breakout, traders believed that the second leg down from the bar 1 high had begun.


这张图上还有一些值得一提的特征。第12根K线是一个扩张三角形底部，其中第4根、第6根和第12根K线就是三次向下推进。


> There were some other noteworthy features on this chart. Bar 12 was an expanding triangle bottom with bars 4, 6, and 12 being the three pushes down.


当天开盘后先是急速上涨到第3根K线，随后又急速抛售下跌到第6根K线，它跌破开盘价的幅度，大致与第3根K线高于开盘价的幅度相同。尽管当天的振幅不大，但它与近几天大致相当（12月末常常出现振幅很小的交易日）。只要有哪一天的振幅处于平均水平、而开盘价又位于振幅中部，市场往往就会试图在开盘价附近收盘。交易者明白这一点，所以第7根K线之后那个窄幅交易区间，很有可能出现一次回测当天开盘价的突破。当天收盘价比开盘价高一个最小报价单位，这在日线图上形成了一根几乎完美的十字星蜡烛线。


> The first day opened with a sharp rally up to bar 3 and then a sharp sell-off down to bar 6 that extended about as far below the open as bar 3 did above it. Even though the range was small, it was about average for the recent days (the end of December often has small days). Whenever a day has an average range and the open is in the middle of the range, the market often tries to close around the open. Traders know this, and that is why the tight trading range that followed bar 7 had a good chance of having a breakout that tested the open of the day. The day closed at one tick above the open, and this formed an almost perfect doji candle on the daily chart.


涨到第9根K线的那波上涨，是对跌破第3根K线的那波抛售的突破回测。跌到第23根K线的那波抛售，则是对涨过第13根K线的那波上涨的突破回测，它比保本止损高出一个最小报价单位，没有触发这些止损。它同时也是对当天开盘价的一次精确回测。


> The rally to bar 9 was a breakout test of the sell-off below bar 3. The sell-off to bar 23 was a breakout test of the rally above bar 13, and it missed the breakeven stops by one tick. It was also an exact test of the open of the day.


![图 7.3](figures/fig-07-03.jpg)


**图 7.3　以交易区间中部为基础测算的等距运动**


在图 7.3中，Research in Motion（RIMM）自昨日低点下方形成开盘反转之后，急速上涨到第2根K线，随后回调到第3根K线。


> In Figure 7.3, Research in Motion (RIMM) had a sharp move up to bar 2 after an opening reversal from below yesterday's low, and then a pullback to bar 3.


由于在一波强劲的三根K线多头急速行情之后，很可能有第二段上涨行情，所以如果交易者想知道这段行情可能在哪里结束，他们可以不断调整 B 线，让它位于正在形成的区间的中部。一旦市场向上突破，他们就可以作一条平行线，把它从 A 线等距向上平移，得到一次等距运动，并预期在那里止盈。尽管市场当时处在交易区间之中，但存在略微偏向向上突破的倾向，因为进入交易区间之前的那段行情是上涨，而且区间内大多数K线都是多头趋势K线，代表着买压。


> Since a second leg up was likely after a strong three-bar bull spike, if traders were interested in knowing where it might end, they could keep adjusting line B to be in the middle of the developing range. Once the market breaks out, they could make a parallel and drag it equidistantly up from line A for a measured move, where they could expect to take profits. Even though the market was in a trading range, there was a slight bias toward an upside breakout because the move before the trading range was up and most of the bars in the trading range were bull trend bars, representing buying pressure.


在市场向上突破第6根K线、脱离三角形之前，交易者可以两个方向都做，就像在任何交易区间里一样。既然交易区间是多空双方都认可存在价值的区域，那么大多数离开中部的试探都会失败，市场会被拉回区间之内。最终，市场会挣脱这片磁力场，在另一个价位上找到价值。


> Until the market broke out of the triangle by going above bar 6, traders could have traded in both directions, as they can in any trading range. Since a trading range is an area where both the bulls and the bears have agreed that there is value, most probes away from the middle fail and the market will get drawn back into the range. Eventually, the market will break away from the magnetic field and find value at a different price.


![图 7.4](figures/fig-07-04.jpg)


**图 7.4　以空头急速行情为基础测算的等距运动**


当一条消息催生出一段急速行情时，这段急速行情常常会引出一个等距运动，交易者可以在那里考虑止盈。在图 7.4中，市场在第1根K线处因一则关于总统提议新银行监管规定的公告而大感意外，由此走出两根大型空头趋势K线。一旦出现一根停顿K线——比如一根十字星、一根下方影线很长的K线，或者一根带阳线实体的K线——你就知道急速行情已经在前一根K线结束。在这里，急速行情持续了两根K线，交易者便从急速行情最后一根K线的收盘价起向下寻找等距运动。他们预期它所对应的最小报价单位数量，大约等于从急速行情第一根K线开盘价到最后一根K线收盘价之间所包含的数量。有时候，从第一根K线的最高价到最后一根K线的最低价会成为等距运动的高度，但交易者总是先看最近的那个可能性，只有当第一个目标位没能拦住市场时，才会去看更大的运动。这个目标位很适合作为波段空头的最后一次止盈点，然后等回调再去做空。如果在这个回测区域出现强烈的反转信号，就可以考虑做一笔逆势交易。


> When there is a news release that creates a spike, the spike often leads to a measured move where traders can look to take profits. In Figure 7.4, at bar 1 the market was surprised by an announcement about the president proposing new banking regulations, and this led to two large bear trend bars. Once there is a pause bar like a doji, a bar with a large tail on the bottom, or a bar with a bull body, then you know that the spike had ended on the prior bar. Here, the spike lasted two bars and traders looked for a measured move down from the close of the final bar of the spike. They expected it to be about the same number of ticks as there were from the open of the first bar of the spike down to the close of the final bar of the spike. Sometimes the high of the first bar to the low of the final bar of the spike becomes the height of the measured move, but traders will always look at the nearest possibility first and look for bigger moves only if the first target failed to contain the market. This target is a good place to take your final profit on a swing short and then look for a pullback to short again. If there is a strong reversal signal at that test area, a counter-trend trade can be considered.


![图 7.5](figures/fig-07-05.jpg)


**图 7.5　急速行情可以引出向上或向下的等距运动**


急速行情之后，可以接着走出向上或向下的等距运动。在图 7.5中，开盘后出现了一波强劲的六根K线上涨行情，但在这个大幅跳空低开的日子里，市场在均线处受阻失败，最终完成了一次向下的等距运动。这次运动是以急速行情第一根K线的开盘价量到最后一根K线的收盘价为基础测算的。尽管大多数急速行情只要出现任何一根停顿K线就会结束，但如果停顿之后行情继续上行，你就应该考虑这样一种可能：它会像急速行情一样发挥作用——在更高的时间级别图表上，它很可能就是一段急速行情。


> A spike can be followed by a measured move in either direction. In Figure 7.5, there was a strong six-bar rally on the open, but the market failed at the moving average on this large gap down day and ultimately reached a measured move to the downside. The move was based on the open of the first bar of the spike to the close of the final bar of the spike. Although most spikes end as soon as there is any pause bar, if the move continues up after the pause, you should consider the possibility that it will function like a spike, which it probably is on a higher time frame chart.


# 第 8 章　基于缺口与交易区间的等距运动

*8. Measured Moves Based on Gaps and Trading Ranges*


在日线图上，缺口很常见：一根K线的低点高于前一根K线的高点，或者一根K线的高点低于前一根K线的低点。如果市场对方向有坚定的信念，缺口的中点往往就成为趋势的中点。当市场接近等距运动目标位时，交易者会仔细盯住那个精确的目标位，往往会在这个区域部分止盈或全部止盈，有些交易者还会开始建立反方向的仓位。这往往会导致停顿、回调，甚至反转。


> Gaps are common on daily charts where the low of one bar is above the high of the prior bar or the high of a bar is below the low of the prior bar. If there is conviction about the direction of the market, the middle of the gap often becomes the middle of the trend. As the market gets near the measured move target, traders will look carefully at the exact target and often take partial or total profits in that area, and some traders will begin to take positions in the opposite direction. This often leads to a pause, a pullback, or even a reversal.


在日内图上出现突破时，这种缺口极少出现。不过，往往有一样东西同样可靠，那就是突破点与第一次停顿或回调之间的缺口。举例来说，如果市场向上突破一个摆动高点，突破K线是一根相对较大的多头趋势K线，而下一根K线的低点位于突破点之上，那么这个低点与突破点之间就有一个缺口，它往往会成为测量缺口。如果突破之后的那根K线也是一根大的多头趋势K线，那就等第一根小的多头趋势K线、空头趋势K线或十字星K线出现。它的低点就是该缺口的顶部。如果突破点或突破回调不清晰，市场往往就直接拿突破K线的中点当缺口的中点。这种情况下，等距运动以这轮上涨行情的起点为基准，量到突破K线的中点，然后预期市场会在该价位之上再走出差不多相同数量的最小报价单位。


> When a breakout occurs on an intraday chart, only rarely will this kind of gap appear. However, there is often something just as reliable, which is a gap between the breakout point and the first pause or pullback. For example, if the market breaks out above a swing high and the breakout bar is a relatively large bull trend bar and the low of the next bar is above the breakout point, then there is a gap between that low and the breakout point and that often becomes a measuring gap. If the bar after the breakout is also a large bull trend bar, then wait for the first small bull trend bar, bear trend bar, or doji bar. Its low is then the top of the gap. If the breakout point or the breakout pullback is unclear, the market will often just use the middle of the breakout bar as the middle of the gap. In this case, the measured move is based on the start of the rally to the middle of the breakout bar. The market would then be expected to rally for about the same number of ticks above that level.


如果市场在突破后的几根K线之内就回调，而回调的低点落在缺口之中，那么这个缺口现在变小了，但它的中点仍然可以用来寻找等距运动目标位。如果市场回调得更深，甚至略微跌破缺口，那么突破点与这次回调之间的中点仍然可以用来做测算。由于这时突破回调与突破点之差是一个负数，我把它称为负缺口（negative gap）。基于负缺口的等距运动目标位，可靠性要低一些。


> If the market pulls back within a few bars of breaking out and the low of the pullback is in the gap, then the gap is now smaller but its midpoint still can be used to find a measured move target. If the market pulls back further, even to a little below the gap, the midpoint between the breakout point and that pullback can still be used for the projection. Since the difference between the breakout pullback and the breakout point is then a negative number, I call this a negative gap. Measured move projections are less reliable when they are based on a negative gap.


在市场轮廓图（Market Profile）上，这些市场快速运动所形成的日内测量缺口，就是两个分布区之间的稀薄区，代表市场处于单边成交状态的价位。分布区则是“厚实”的区域，其实就是正在进行双边成交的交易区间。交易区间是多空双方对价格达成共识的区域，它的中点，就是多空双方都认为公允的那个区间的中点。缺口同样是一个共识区域：它是多空双方一致认同“这里不该有成交”的区域，它的中点就是该区域的中点。这两种情况下，从最简单的层面看，如果这些价位是多空共识的中点，那么它们就能大致指示出包含它们的那段行情段的中点。它们一旦形成，就把你顺势入场的一部分或全部仓位做波段持有。当目标位逐渐临近时，如果有好的建仓形态，可以考虑逆势入场。大多数交易者用前一个交易区间的高度来做测算，这没有问题，因为不管你用什么办法，那个精确距离都只是近似值（除非你是斐波那契或艾略特波浪交易者，并且有那种离奇的本事，能说服自己市场几乎总能走出完美的形态——尽管压倒性的证据恰恰相反）。关键在于只做顺势；不过一旦市场进入等距运动区域，你就可以开始寻找逆势入场。然而，最好的逆势交易只出现在此前一段强到足以突破趋势线的逆势行情之后。


> On a Market Profile, these intraday measuring gaps where the market moves quickly are thin areas between two distributions, and represent prices where the market is one-sided. The distributions are “fat” areas and are simply trading ranges where there is two-sided trading taking place. A trading range is an area of agreement on price, and its middle is the middle of what bulls and bears think is fair. A gap is also an area of agreement. It is an area where the bulls and bears agree that no trading should take place, and its middle is the midpoint of that area. In both cases, on a simplistic level, if those prices are a midpoint of agreement between bulls and bears, then they are a rough guide to the midpoint of the leg that contains them. Once they form, swing part or all of your with-trend entries. As the target is approached, consider countertrend entries if there is a good setup. Most traders use the height of the prior trading range for measuring, which is fine because the exact distance is only approximate no matter how you do it (unless you are a Fibonacci or Elliott Wave trader and have the uncanny ability to convince yourself that the market almost always creates perfect patterns, despite the overwhelming evidence to the contrary). The key is to trade only with the trend, but once the market is in the area of the measured move, you can begin to look for countertrend entries. However, the best counter-trend trades only follow an earlier countertrend move that was strong enough to break the trend line.


如果市场在触及等距运动目标位之后出现停顿，那两段强劲的趋势行情可能只是更大时间级别一轮修正的尾声；如果看起来确实如此，那就把任何逆势入场的一部分仓位做波段持有。两段行情往往就完成一轮运动，而这轮运动之后通常至少跟着一段拉长的逆势行情，这段逆势行情至少包含两段行情，有时还会演变成一个方向相反的新趋势。这段逆势行情往往会一路回测到突破点。


> If the market pauses after the measured move is reached, the two strong trend legs might be simply the end of a higher time frame correction, and if that appears to be the case, then swing part of any counter-trend entry. Two legs often complete a move, and the move is usually followed by at least a protracted coun-tertrend move that has at least two legs, and it sometimes becomes a new, opposite trend. The counter-trend move will often test all the way back to the breakout point.


有时这些测算精确到最小报价单位，但大多数时候市场会未及靶位或过靶。这个方法只是一条指导原则，让你始终待在市场的正确一侧。


> Sometimes the projections are exact to the tick, but most of the time the market undershoots or overshoots the target. This approach is only a guideline to keep you trading on the correct side of the market.


![图 8.1](figures/fig-08-01.jpg)


**图 8.1　测量缺口**


缺口的中点往往引出一段等距运动。在图 8.1中，Emini 小型合约在第3根K线处向上跳空，位于前一日的第2根K线高点之上，而这个缺口的中点有可能就是这轮上涨行情的中点。交易者从这轮上涨行情的起点——第1根K线的底部——量到缺口的中点，然后把同样数量的点数向上投射出去。第4根K线距离该投射位只有两三个最小报价单位之遥，但很多交易者认为，Emini 的目标位只有等到市场走到距其一个最小报价单位之内，才算被充分测试过。这让交易者有信心在次日开盘急跌到第5根K线时买入。当日最高点比等距运动目标位高出两个最小报价单位。第二天市场抛售到第7根K线，但再次上涨，在略低于目标位的位置做了一次测试。接下来的一天，多头放弃了，市场大幅向下跳空，随后一路抛售。当然，确实有一些消息发布，电视上的评论员就用它们来解释这里的每一个走势；但实际情况是，这些走势建立在数学之上。消息只是给市场的一个借口，让它去做它本来就要做的事。


> The middle of a gap often leads to a measured move. In Figure 8.1, the Emini had a gap up at bar 3, above the bar 2 high of the previous day, and the middle of that gap was a possible middle of the move up. Traders measured from the bar 1 bottom of the rally to the middle of the gap and then projected that same number of points upward. Bar 4 came within a couple of ticks of the projection, but many traders believe that a target in the Emini has not been adequately tested unless the market comes to within one tick of it. This gave traders confidence to buy the sharp sell-off on the open of the next day down to bar 5. The high of the day was two ticks above the measured move projection. The market sold off on the next day down to bar 7 but rallied again to test just below the target. On the following day, the bulls gave up and there was a large gap down and then a sell-off. There were certainly news announcements that the television pundits used to explain all of the moves, but the reality was that the moves were based on math. The news was just the excuse for the market to do what it was already going to do.


![图 8.2](figures/fig-08-02.jpg)


**图 8.2　测量缺口**


图 8.2展示的两个交易日，其等距运动都以稀薄区为依据。稀薄区是一种突破区域，那里K线之间重叠极少。


> Figure 8.2 shows two days that have measured moves based on thin areas. A thin area is a breakout area where there is very little overlap of the bars.


太平洋标准时间上午11:15，联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）报告发布之际，市场从第3根K线起急速上涨，并向上突破了当日的第2根K线高点。第4根K线处的旗形用一段两段式横向修正回测了这次突破，而第2根K线顶部与第4根K线突破回测底部之间，存在一个小小的负缺口。如果你用第4根K线回调的低点减去第2根K线突破点的高点，得到的缺口高度就是一个负数。负缺口的中点有时能给出完美的等距运动，但更常见的是：等距运动的终点等于突破点的顶部（这里是第2根K线高点）减去初始交易区间的底部（这里是第1根K线低点）。你也可以用第3根K线的低点来计算等距运动，但永远更好的做法是先看最近的那个目标位，只有当市场穿过较低的目标位之后，才去考虑更远的目标。市场在当日最后一根K线处，精准触及了从 A 线（第1根K线）到 B 线的等距运动所给出的 C 线目标位；次日开盘，又用第3根K线到 B 线的投射位向上刺穿了 D 线目标位。尽管第1根K线高于第3根K线，它仍然可以被视为这段等距运动的底部——只要把跌到第3根K线的那波抛售看成只是对这段行情第1根K线真实低点的一次过靶。


> The market had a sharp move up from bar 3 on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) report at 11:15 a.m. PST, and broke above the bar 2 high of the day. The flag at bar 4 tested the breakout with a two-legged sideways correction, and there was a small negative gap between the top of bar 2 and the bottom of the bar 4 breakout test. If you subtract the high of the bar 2 breakout point from the low of the bar 4 pullback, you get a negative number for the height of the gap. Although the middle of a negative gap sometimes yields a perfect measured move, more commonly the end of the measured move will be equal to the top of the breakout point, here the bar 2 high, minus the bottom of the initial trading range, here the bar 1 low. You could also use the low of bar 3 to calculate the measured move, but it is always better to look at the nearest target first and to consider further targets only if the market trades through the lower ones. The market reached the line C target from the line A (bar 1) to line B measured move exactly on the last bar of the day, and poked above the line D target using the bar 3 to line B projection on the open of the next day. Even though bar 1 is higher than bar 3, it can still be considered the bottom of the measured move by thinking of the sell-off to bar 3 as just an overshoot of the bar 1 actual low of the leg.


第二个交易日，在第7根K线下方、第8根K线上方出现了一个缺口，收盘前不久价格越过了 F 线目标位。


> On the second day, there was a gap below bar 7 and above bar 8, and the line F target was exceeded just before the close.


顺带一提，第8根K线与第9根K线处还形成了一个双顶熊旗。


> Incidentally, there was also a double top bear flag at bars 8 and 9.


![图 8.3](figures/fig-08-03.jpg)


**图 8.3　在等距运动目标位止盈**


在图 8.3所示的月线图上，苹果（AAPL）处于强劲的多头趋势之中。只要存在趋势，交易者就会寻找合乎逻辑的价位，以便能够部分止盈或全部止盈。他们通常会求助于等距运动。第13根K线就位于以第4根K线到第5根K线那段强劲上涨行情为基础的等距运动目标位略上方。


> Apple (AAPL) was in a strong bull trend on the monthly chart shown in Figure 8.3. Whenever there is a trend, traders look for logical levels where they can take partial or full profits. They usually turn to measured moves. Bar 13 was just above the measured move based on the strong rally from bar 4 to bar 5.


第10根K线是一根多头趋势K线，它向上突破了第9根K线处的回调——那是对“突破第5根K线的尝试”所做的回调。每一根趋势K线都是突破K线，也都是缺口K线；在这里，第10根K线同时充当了突破缺口和测量缺口。虽然第11根K线向下急速扎到第10根K线下方，但作为一根突破失败的K线，这波下跌不太可能有太多后续行情，因为那根信号K线是连续第三根强劲的多头趋势K线。动量太大，做空并不可靠。市场在第12根K线处再次向上测试第9根K线上方的那个缺口，这次回调给了交易者一个潜在的测量缺口。市场在第13根K线处转向下跌，比目标位低了大约3%；该目标位是按第8根K线低点到这个缺口中点的上涨幅度测算出来的。它可能正在形成两根K线反转，而这可能导致一轮更深的修正：修正可能包含两段行情，并持续10根K线或更久。由于第13根K线是连续第六根多头趋势K线，向上的动量依然强劲。在长时间的上涨趋势之后出现这么大的力度，有时代表趋势进入高潮式衰竭，随后会跟着一轮大幅修正。这里是对多头部分止盈或全部止盈的合理区域，但还不足以构成一个强到能让交易者根据这张月线图开始做空的建仓形态。不过，由于目前还没有出现明确的顶部，市场也可能再向上推一次，去触及以第10根K线缺口为基础的等距运动目标位。


> Bar 10 was a bull trend bar that broke out above the bar 9 pullback from the attempted breakout above bar 5. Every trend bar is a breakout bar and a gap bar, and here bar 10 functioned as a breakout gap and a measuring gap. Although bar 11 spiked below bar 10, the move down was unlikely to have much follow-through as a failed breakout bar, because the signal bar was the third consecutive strong bull trend bar. This was too much momentum to be a reliable short. The market tested into the gap above bar 9 again at bar 12, and this pullback gave traders a potential measuring gap. The market turned down at bar 13, about 3 percent below the target based on the move up from the bar 8 low to the middle of that gap. It might be in the process of forming a two-bar reversal, which could lead to a deeper correction that could have a couple of legs and last for 10 or more bars. Since bar 13 was the sixth consecutive bull trend bar, the momentum up was still strong. When this much strength occurs after a protracted bull trend, it sometimes represents a climactic exhaustion of the trend and is followed by a large correction. This is a reasonable area to take partial or full profits on longs, but not yet a strong enough setup for traders to be initiating shorts based on this monthly chart. However, since there is not yet a clear top, the market might have another push up to the measured move target based on the bar 10 gap.


虽然现在下结论还为时过早，但交易者可能正在用第8根K线低点到第9根K线高点来构建一个等距运动目标位。那个目标位虽然图上没有画出，但它只是略低于以第4根K线到第9根K线的多头急速行情所测算出的目标位。而市场已经越过了那个目标位。交易者需要看到更多K线，才能知道最高点是否已经出现，还是说市场会去触及以第10根K线缺口为基础的目标位。如果市场真的去了那里，可能有、也可能没有止盈盘和做空者；但既然它是一个清晰的等距运动磁力位，这里就是双方都有理由出现的区域。


> Although it is too early to tell, traders might be using the bar 8 low to the bar 9 high to create a measured move target. Although not shown, that target is just slightly below the target based on the bar 4 to bar 9 bull spike, which the market already exceeded. Traders need to see more bars before they know whether the high is in or it will reach the target based on the bar 10 gap. If it does, it may or may not find profit takers and shorts, but since it is a clear measured move magnet, it is a logical area for both to be present.


![图 8.4](figures/fig-08-04.jpg)


**图 8.4　等距运动**


如图 8.4所示，跌向第3根K线附近那个突破回调熊旗的走势很陡峭，而一个合理的向下等距运动目标位，是从这段行情段的顶部（第2根K线）量到旗形的近似中点（C 线）。据此投射出的目标位就是 D 线；该目标位被过靶，并引发了一次对移动平均线的测试。你也可以用第1根K线的高点来做测量，但一般来说，算第一个目标位时应该看当前这段行情段的起点。D 线目标位被触及后不久，以第1根K线为起点测算的 E 线目标位也被打到了。注意，从第2根K线跌到第4根K线的这一波是强劲的空头趋势，其间没有明显的趋势线突破，所以最好还是坚持做顺势的建仓形态。


> As shown in Figure 8.4, the move down to the breakout pullback bear flag around bar 3 was steep, and a reasonable target for a measured move down is from the top of the leg (bar 2) to the approximate middle of the flag (line C). This projected to line D, which was overshot and led to a moving average test. You could also have used the bar 1 high for a measurement, but you should generally look at the start of the current leg for your first target. After the line D target was reached, the line E target based on the bar 1 starting point was hit soon afterward. Note that the move down to bar 4 from bar 2 was a strong bear trend with no significant trend line break, so it was best to stick to with-trend setups.


第4根K线附近那个小楔形熊旗大体上是横向的，因此它可能是一面空头末端旗形；但由于此时还没有出现过一波急速上涨（比如一根位于指数移动平均线上方的均线缺口K线），逆势交易只能做剥头皮（如果你真要做的话）。只有当你水平足够高、能在顺势机会一出现时就立刻切换过去做顺势，才应该做这种逆势操作。如果你做不到，你就不该做逆势，而应该努力去做顺势入场。仅仅处在等距运动区域内，还不足以构成逆势入场的理由。你需要此前已经出现过一些逆势的强势表现。


> The small wedge bear flag around bar 4 was mostly horizontal and therefore a possible final bear flag, but since there had yet to be a sharp rally (like a gap bar above the exponential moving average), countertrend trades had to be scalps (if you took them at all). You should take them only if you are a good enough trader to then switch to with-trend trades as soon as one developed. If you are not, you should not be trading countertrend and instead you should be working hard to take with-trend entries. Just being in the area of a measured move is not enough reason for a counter-trend entry. You need some earlier countertrend strength.


第二个交易日，在向上突破第8根K线之后，第10根K线附近出现了一面旗形。这次对双底牛旗的向上突破，向上投射到 H 线。第一个底部，是自第7根K线起那波急速上涨行情中一次只有一根K线的回调。如果你改用当日第7根K线的低点来测算，那么目标位在次日跳空高开之后不久就会被触及。


> On the second day, there was a flag around bar 10, after the breakout above bar 8. This breakout above the double bottom bull flag projected up to line H. The first bottom was the one-bar pullback in the spike up from bar 7. If instead you used the bar 7 low of the day, the target would have been reached shortly after the gap up on the following day.


一旦出现突破后的旗形，明智的做法是把你顺势交易的一部分仓位做波段持有，直到等距运动目标位被触及。到了那时，如果有好的建仓形态，就可以考虑做一笔逆势交易。


> Once there is a breakout flag, it is wise to swing part of your with-trend trade until the measured move is reached. At that point, consider a countertrend trade if there is a good setup.


![图 8.5](figures/fig-08-05.jpg)


**图 8.5　测量缺口**


如图 8.5所示，B 线是突破点（第2根K线的高点）与第一次回调的低点（第5根K线的低点）之间那片稀薄区的中点。等距运动目标位在第8根K线处被精准命中，一个最小报价单位都不差。


> As shown in Figure 8.5, line B is the midpoint of the thin area in between the breakout (the high of bar 2) and the low of the first pullback (the low of bar 5). The measured move was hit to the exact tick at bar 8.


E 线是一处稀薄区的中点，市场大幅过靶了它投射出的 F 线目标位。从第12根K线熊旗展开的这次突破，到第13根K线之间形成了一大片稀薄区，但当时时间已经太晚，从其中点测算的等距运动目标位不太可能被触及。不过到那个时候，当天已经明确是空头趋势日，交易者只应该做空，除非出现清晰而强劲的多头剥头皮机会（尾盘确实有过两次）。跌到第13根K线的五根K线急速行情引出了一段向下的等距运动，而当日最低点距离该目标位只差一个最小报价单位。


> Line E was the midpoint of a thin area and the market greatly overshot its line F projection. The breakout from the bar 12 bear flag had a huge thin area down to bar 13, but it was so late in the day that a measured move from its midpoint was unlikely to be reached. However, at that point the day was clearly a bear trend day and traders should only be shorting unless there was a clear and strong long scalp (there were a couple in the final hour). The five-bar spike down to bar 13 led to a measured move down, and the low of the day missed it by a tick.


顺带一提，走到第7根K线的那段行情突破了一条趋势线，说明空头正在变强；走到第9根K线的那段行情突破了一条主要趋势线，由此构建出第10根K线处的更低的高点，去测试趋势极值（第8根K线），随后的空头趋势也就此展开。


> Incidentally, the move to bar 7 broke a trend line, indicating that the bears were getting stronger, and the move to bar 9 broke a major trend line, setting up the bar 10 lower high test of the trend extreme (bar 8), and the subsequent bear trend that followed.


# 第 9 章　反转往往在此前失败反转的信号K线处结束

*9. Reversals Often End at Signal Bars from Prior Failed Reversals*


一次早期反转失败时的入场价，往往是之后某次成功反转的磁力位。举例来说，如果市场正处于空头趋势，期间有几次做多入场都随着市场继续抛售而失败，那么一旦向上的反转终于成功，这些入场价中的每一个，以及每一根信号K线的高点，都会成为目标位。市场常常会一路涨到最高的那根信号K线的高点，之后才会出现一次显著回调。很可能的情形是：一些在那些更高的信号处入场的交易者，在市场一路与他们作对时做了分批建仓，随后把最初的那笔入场价当作自己最后的止盈目标——在最糟的那一笔入场上保本离场，而在所有更低的入场仓位上止盈。也可能只是这样：聪明的交易者相信事实就是如此，于是会在这些目标位把手里的多头全部抛掉；又或者，它不过是所有优秀交易者都心知肚明的众多秘密暗号之一——他们在那里离场，仅仅是因为他们知道，回调结束在先前的入场点附近，是一种可靠且反复出现的形态。对交易者来说，这也可能是个带着点“谢天谢地，我再也不干这种事了！”意味的价位。他们没有把亏损的那笔交易平掉，亏损不断扩大，而他们一直盼着市场回到自己的入场价。当市场终于回来时，他们离场，并发誓再也不犯这种错误。


> The entry price of an early reversal that failed is often a magnet for a later, successful reversal. For example, if there is a bear trend and there have been several bull entries that failed as the market continued to sell off, each of these entry prices and the highs of every signal bar will be targets once a reversal up finally succeeds. The market will often rally all the way to the highest signal bar's high before having a significant pullback. It is likely that some traders who entered on those higher signals scaled in as the market went against them and they then used their initial entry as their final profit target, exiting breakeven on their worst entry and taking profits on all of the lower entries. It might just be that smart traders believe this to be the case and will dump their longs at those targets, or it might simply be one of the many secret handshakes that all great traders know, and they exit there simply because they know that it is a reliable recurring pattern for pullbacks to end near earlier entry points. It can also be something of a “Thank you, God, I will never do this again!” price for traders.
