They did not exit a losing trade, and their loss kept growing while they kept hoping for the market to come back to their entry. When it finally does, they exit and swear that they will never make that mistake again.


交易中发生的几乎每一件事，都有其数学依据，尤其是因为成交量里有如此大的一部分，是由建立在统计分析之上的软件算法产生的。在前面那个反转向上的空头趋势的例子中，最早的那个买入信号常常位于一段空头通道的起点。当一段空头通道开始时，一段上下等幅运动（equidistant move）的方向概率至少是60%。也就是说，市场先下跌10个最小报价单位、随后再上涨10个最小报价单位的概率约为60%。这个距离可以是任何幅度，只要基于近期波段、处在合理可及的范围之内；但关键在于市场存在下行偏向。随着市场下跌、动量放缓，当这波下跌走完大约一半时，方向概率会降到50% 上下，但这个中性区域的价位，通常要等到市场形成交易区间之后才能知道。当市场继续跌向某个重要的磁力位时，方向概率会越过中性值，实际上转为有利于多头。在交易区间的中部，存在不确定性；而一旦市场触及底部，就会形成共识：市场走得太远了。此时，方向概率有利于多头。随后市场会上涨，并开始形成一段交易区间。在交易区间的底部，方向概率总是有利于多头，而这个底部会落在某个关键的技术价位上。市场下跌的过程中，可供选择的技术价位有很多，而其中大多数都不会引出一个清晰的买入建仓形态。有些公司会依据一个或多个技术支撑位来编写程序，另一些公司则会用别的支撑位。当足够多的关键技术区域密集出现在相近的位置上时，押注反转的成交量就会大到足以改变方向。到那时，数学期望就站在你这一边，因为你买入的价位，将会是某个交易区间的底部。反转点从来不是事先就能确定的，但它发生时总会伴随某种反转形态；当市场处在关键技术位时——比如等距运动目标位、趋势线，乃至更大时间级别的移动平均线和趋势线——留意这些形态非常重要。这一点在第3册讲反转的那一章里有进一步讨论。通常没有必要翻看一大堆图表去找建仓形态，因为只要你有耐心、保持警觉、并且认得这些形态，每一张图上都会有一个合理的建仓形态。


> There is a mathematical basis for just about everything that happens in trading, especially since so much of the volume is generated by software algorithms that are based on statistical analysis. In the example of that bear trend that reversed up, that earliest buy signal is often at the start of a bear channel. When a bear channel begins, the directional probability of an equidistant move is at least 60 percent. That means that the market had about a 60 percent chance of falling 10 ticks before rallying 10 ticks. It can be any size move that is within reasonable reach based on the recent swings, but the key point is that the market has a downside bias. As the market falls and the momentum slows, the directional probability falls to around 50 percent when the move down is about half over, but the price of this neutral area is usually not knowable until after the market forms a trading range. As it continues to fall down to some significant magnet, the directional probability overshoots neutrality and actually shifts in favor of the bulls. In the middle of the trading range, there is uncertainty; but once the market hits the bottom, there is agreement that the market went too far. At this point, the directional probability favors the bulls. It will then rally and begin to form a trading range. The directional probability always favors the bulls at the bottom of a trading range, and that bottom will be at some key technical price. There are many to choose from as the market is falling, and most do not lead to a clear buy setup. Some firms will write programs based on one or more technical support levels, and other firms will use others. When enough key technical areas occur in close proximity, there will be enough volume betting on a reversal to change the direction. At that point, the math is on your side because you are buying at what will be the bottom of a trading range. The reversal point is never known with certainty in advance, but it will happen with some kind of reversal pattern; it is important to watch for these patterns when the market is at key technical levels, like at measured move targets, trend lines, and even higher time frame moving averages and trend lines. This is discussed further in the chapter on reversals in book 3. It is usually not necessary to look at lots of charts in search of setups because there will be a reasonable setup on every chart if you are patient, vigilant, and aware of the patterns.


市场一旦转向上，通常就会试图形成一段交易区间；而这个初生交易区间的顶部，最先的几种可能，就是那些更早的做多入场价。市场会试图上涨到那些多头信号K线的顶部。在市场上涨的过程中，方向概率会回落到50%，并且随着市场接近区间顶部而继续下降。由于这个顶部从来不是事先就能知道的，方向概率处于中性的那个交易区间中部，也从来不是事先就能知道的，所以市场会过靶，直到触及某个交易者认为明显过头的技术位。这个位置常常就在那些更早的买入信号所在的价位上。记住，上一次价格在那里的时候，方向概率是有利于空头的；当价格再一次到那里时，通常又会再次有利于空头——这就是市场往往在那里再次转向下跌的原因。那是一个卖方取得控制权的价位。这轮上涨常常会与先前某根入场K线构成双顶，随后在交易区间演变的过程中转向下跌，至少是短暂地下跌。市场在寻找不确定性——也就是方向概率中性、等于50% 的状态——的过程中，常常会上下往复。到了某个时点，市场会认定这个区域对多空双方都不再代表价值，而且对其中一方来说是个糟糕的价位。随后市场会再次走出趋势，直到找到一个多空双方都视为好价位、愿意在那里进场建仓的价格。


> Once the market turns up, it will usually try to form a trading range, and the first possibilities for the top of the incipient trading range are those earlier long entry prices. The market will try to rally to the top of those bull signal bars. As it is going up, the directional probability falls back to 50 percent, and it continues to fall further as the market gets near the top of the range. Since that top is never known in advance and the middle of the trading range where the directional probability is neutral is never known in advance, the market overshoots until it hits some technical level where traders believe it is clearly overdone. This is often at the level of those earlier buy signals. Remember, the directional probability favored the bears when the price was last there, and when it gets there another time it usually favors the bears once more; that is why the market typically turns down there again. It is a price where the sellers took control. The rally often forms a double top with one of those earlier entry bars and then turns down, at least briefly, as the trading range evolves. The market will often go up and down as it searches for uncertainty, which means a neutral directional probability of 50 percent. At some point, the market will decide that this area no longer represents value for both the bulls and the bears and that it is a bad price for one side. The market will then trend again until it finds a price that both the bulls and the bears see as a good price at which to initiate positions.


![图 9.1](figures/fig-09-01.jpg)


**图 9.1　此前的入场点是回调的目标位**


SPY（也就是与 Emini 小型合约相当的交易所交易基金（ETF））的月线图上，有一段强劲的多头趋势在2000年结束；但在市场持续上涨的过程中，出现过几次试图反转为空头趋势的尝试（见图 9.1）。每一根空头信号K线的低点（第1、2、3根K线），都是下跌途中任何一轮回调的目标位。


> The monthly chart of the SPY (an exchange-traded fund that is comparable to the Emini) had a strong bull trend that ended in 2000, but there were several attempts to reverse into a bear trend as the market continued up (see Figure 9.1). Each of the bear signal bar lows (bars 1, 2, and 3) was a target for any correction on the way down.


同样，2003年结束的那段空头趋势，途中也有过几次失败的多头反转尝试（第4、5、6根K线），而每一根多头信号K线的高点，都是之后任何一轮上涨的目标位。


> Likewise, the bear trend that ended in 2003 had several failed bull reversal attempts along the way (bars 4, 5, and 6) and the high of each bull signal bar was a target for any subsequent rally.


另外，从2003年起的那轮上涨行情中有过几次失败的空头尝试（第7、8、9、10根K线），每一次都是2009年初结束的那段空头趋势中的目标位。那波抛售中有过几次筑底尝试，而那些买入信号K线中每一根的高点（第11、12、13根K线），都是当前这轮上涨行情的目标位。最后，涨到第17根K线的那轮上涨行情中有过几次做顶的尝试（第14、15、16根K线），而每一根卖出信号K线的低点，都是任何一次抛售中的磁力位。


> Also, the rally from 2003 had several failed bear attempts (bars 7, 8, 9, and 10), and each one was a target in the bear trend that ended in early 2009. That sell-off had several bottom attempts, and the high of each of those buy signal bars (bars 11, 12, and 13) is a target for the current rally. Finally, the rally up to bar 17 had several attempts at a top (bars 14, 15, and 16), and the bottom of each of those sell signal bars is a magnet on any sell-off.


这些目标位从来都不是必须触及的，但每一个都是强磁力位，经常把市场拉回到它的价位上。


> None of the targets ever has to be reached, but each is a strong magnet that frequently draws the market back to its level.


# 第 10 章　其他磁力位

*10. Other Magnets*


还有许多其他价格磁力位，往往会吸引市场靠近它们、去做一次测试。下面列出其中一些。这些磁力位中有很多在本书的其他地方讨论过。当市场正朝着某个磁力位走趋势时，明智的做法是顺势交易，直到该磁力位被测试、而且最好是过靶之后再说。不要在磁力位处逆势交易，除非此前已经出现过某种逆势的强势信号，比如一次趋势线突破，或者除非这波行情是更大时间级别趋势中的一次回调。


> There are many other price magnets that will tend to draw the market toward them for a test. Here is a list of some. Many of these are discussed elsewhere in the books. When a market is trending toward a magnet, it is prudent to trade with the trend until the magnet is tested and preferably overshot. Do not trade counter-trend at the magnet unless there has been some prior countertrend strength like a trend line break, or unless the move is a pullback in a higher time frame trend.


- 趋势线。
- 趋势通道线。
- 任何等距运动目标位，包括第1段行情 = 第2段行情（leg 1 = leg 2）的投射位。
- 急速与通道：通道的起点通常在不久之后就会被测试。
- 昨天的高点、低点、开盘价和收盘价。


> • Trend lines. • Trend channel lines. • Any measured move target including a leg 1 = leg 2 projection. • Spike and channel: the start of the channel is usually tested before long. • High, low, open, and close of yesterday.


- 过去几根K线、甚至过去几天的摆动高点和摆动低点，它们往往会形成双底牛旗和双顶熊旗。
- 突破点。
- 任何类型的缺口，包括均线缺口。
- 每一种回调之后趋势的极值点（关于第一次回调序列，见第11章）。
- 当天早些时候或此前几天形成的交易区间，包括窄幅交易区间和铁丝网：它们的极值和中部往往都会被测试。
- 交易区间日上该区间的大致中点，尤其是在那个区域还存在一个日内交易区间时（也就是一片“厚实”区域）。
- 末端旗形：市场从旗形突破之后，会回到该旗形处，通常再从另一侧突破出去。
- 铁丝网。
- 入场K线和信号K线的保护性止损。
- 入场价（突破回测）。
- 巨大趋势K线反向的那一端极值（一根巨大多头趋势K线的低点，一根巨大空头趋势K线的高点）。


> • Swing highs and lows of the past few bars or even days, often setting up double bottom bull flags and double top bear flags. • Breakout points. • Gaps of any kind, including moving average gaps. • The extreme of a trend after every type of pullback (see Chapter 11 on the first pullback sequence). • Trading ranges from earlier in the day or prior days, including tight trading ranges and barbwire: the extremes and the middle often get tested. • The approximate middle of the range on a trading range day, especially if there is an intraday trading range in that area (a fat area). • Final flags: after the breakout from the flag, the market comes back to the flag and usually breaks out of the other side. • Barbwire. • Entry bar and signal bar protective stops. • Entry price (breakout test). • Huge trend bar opposite extreme (the low of a huge bull trend bar and the high of a huge bear trend bar).


- 剥头皮和波段仓位的常见止盈目标：在苹果（AAPL）上是50美分和1美元；在5分钟 Emini 小型合约上，一笔4个最小报价单位的剥头皮对应五到六个最小报价单位，一笔波段交易则对应3、4和10个点。
- 一段相当于所需保护性止损规模的行情：如果一笔 Emini 交易要求你用12个最小报价单位的保护性止损来避免被打掉，那就预期这波行情最终会朝你有利的方向走到12个最小报价单位。
- 日线、周线和月线上的摆动高点和低点、K线的高点和低点、均线、缺口、斐波那契回撤位与投射位，以及趋势线。
- 整数价位，比如股票上的整百（例如苹果在 $300）和道琼斯工业平均指数上的整千（道指12,000）。如果一只股票快速从 $50涨到 $88，它很可能会去测试 $100，并且通常在回调之前会走到 $105或 $110。


> • Common profit targets for scalp and swing positions: in AAPL, 50 cents and a dollar; in the 5 minute Emini, five to six ticks for a four-tick scalp, and three, four, and 10 points for a swing. • A move equal to the size of the required protective stop: if an Emini trade required you to use a 12-tick protective stop to avoid getting stopped out, expect the move to ultimately reach 12 ticks in your favor. • Daily, weekly, and monthly swing highs and lows, bar highs and lows, moving averages, gaps, Fibonacci retracements and extensions, and trend lines. • Round numbers like hundreds in stocks (e.g., AAPL at $300) and thousands in the Dow Jones Industrial Average (Dow 12,000). If a stock quickly moves from $50 to $88, it will likely try to test $100 and usually go to $105 or $110 before pulling back.


![图 10.1](figures/fig-10-01.jpg)


**图 10.1　大趋势K线的极值都是磁力位**


当出现一根带小影线的巨大趋势K线时，在这根K线上、或紧随其后入场的交易者，往往会把保护性止损放在这根K线之外。市场慢慢走到这些止损位，然后再沿着这根趋势K线的方向反转回去，是相当常见的情况。


> When there is a huge trend bar with small tails, traders who enter on the bar or soon afterward will often put their protective stops beyond the bar. It is fairly common for the market to work its way to those stops and then reverse back in the direction of the trend bar.


图 10.1中的第1根K线是一根底部光秃的巨大多头趋势K线。市场在随后那根空头内包K线处反转向下，形成了一个更高的低点，但在此之前，它先打掉了这根趋势K线低点下方的保护性止损。聪明的交易者会做空那根内包K线，但他们也准备好在那根打掉止损、随后又把市场翻转向上的第2根多头反转K线之上做多。


> Bar 1 in Figure 10.1 is a huge bull trend bar with a shaved bottom. The market reversed down off the bear inside bar that followed and formed a higher low, but not before running the protective stops below the low of the trend bar. Smart traders would have shorted the inside bar, but they were ready to go long above the bar 2 bull reversal bar that hit the stops and then turned the market back up.


第3根和第4根K线也都是带小影线的巨大趋势K线，但两者后面都没有立刻出现一波打掉止损的回调。


> Bars 3 and 4 were also huge trend bars with small tails, but neither was followed by an immediate pullback that ran stops.


# 第 Ⅲ 部分　回调：趋势向交易区间转化

*Part III　Pullbacks: Trends Converting to Trading Ranges*


即使一张图处在强趋势中，它也会出现双边成交的时段；但只要交易者相信趋势会恢复，这些时段就只是回调。这些交易区间小到足以让交易者把它们看作趋势中的短暂停顿，而不是这张图的主要特征。所有回调，在你正在看的那张图上，都是小型交易区间；所有交易区间，在更大时间级别的图上，都是回调。不过，在你面前这张图上，大多数试图突破交易区间的尝试都会失败，而大多数试图突破回调的尝试都会成功。在更大时间级别的图上，交易区间就是一次简单的回调；如果你在那个图上交易，就可以像对待任何其他回调一样对待它。


> Even when a chart is in a strong trend, it will have periods of two-sided trading, but as long as traders believe that the trend will resume, these are only pullbacks. These trading ranges are small enough for traders to view them as just brief pauses in the trend, rather than the dominant feature of the chart. All pullbacks are small trading ranges on the chart that you are viewing, and all trading ranges are pullbacks on higher time frame charts. However, on the chart in front of you, most attempts to break out of a trading range fail, but most attempts to break out of a pullback succeed. On higher time frame charts, the trading range is a simple pullback, and if you are trading on that chart, you can trade it like any other pullback.


由于更大时间级别图上的K线更大，你的风险也更大，因此你必须降低仓位规模。大多数交易者更愿意只用单一时间级别交易，而不是来回切换，并随不同的时间级别建立不同规模的仓位、使用不同大小的止损和止盈目标。


> Since the bars are larger on a higher time frame chart, your risk is greater, and you have to reduce your position size. Most traders prefer to trade off a single time frame and not switch back and forth taking different-sized positions and using different-sized stops and profit targets depending on the time frame.


如果市场处在强趋势中，而且人人都预期趋势会延续，那怎么还会出现回调？要理解原因，不妨以多头趋势为例。反转向下形成回调，是多头止盈造成的，此外还有程度较小的空头剥头皮。多头会在某个时点止盈，因为他们知道这在数学上是最优的做法。如果他们永远持有，市场几乎总会回到他们的入场价，最终还会远远跌到其下方，造成巨大亏损。他们从来无从确知最佳的止盈位置在哪里，于是把阻力位当作自己最好的估计。这些价位对你来说不一定明显，但因为它们给交易者提供了机会，所以持续寻找它们很重要。趋势剥头皮交易者、波段交易者，以及逆势剥头皮交易者，都预期会有这次回调，并据此交易。当市场到达某个目标位、足够多的多头认为应该在此止盈时，缺乏新的买盘加上他们卖出自己的多头仓位，就会让市场停顿下来。这个目标位可以是任何阻力位（在本书第二部关于支撑与阻力的几章中讨论过），也可以是某根重要信号K线上方的一定数量最小报价单位（比如 Emini 上的6、10或18个）。那根K线可能有一个比前一根K线多头实体更小的多头实体，可能带有一条上影线，或者下一根K线可能是一根带空头实体的小K线。这些都是信号：多头在摆动高点处买入的意愿下降，一些多头正在止盈，空头开始为剥头皮而做空。如果足够多的多头和空头卖出，回调就会变得更大，当前这根K线可能跌破前一根K线的低点。在一段强劲的多头急速行情中，交易者会预期多头趋势立刻恢复，所以多头和空头都会在前一根K线低点附近买入。这就形成一个高1买入信号，而且通常后面跟着一个新高。随着多头趋势成熟、转弱，更多的双边成交会出现，多头和空头都会预期回调的幅度更大、持续的K线更多。市场可能形成一个高2买入信号、一个三角形，或者一个楔形牛旗（bull flag）。这就形成了一小段下跌趋势；当它到达某个数学目标位时，多头会重新开始买入，空头会止盈并买回自己的空头仓位。在市场上再次上涨到足以让这个过程重演之前，双方都不会再卖出。


> If the market is in a strong trend and everyone expects the trend to continue, why would a pullback ever happen? To understand why, consider the example of a bull trend. The reversal down into the pullback is due to profit taking by the bulls and, to a lesser extent, scalping by the bears. Bulls will take profits at some point because they know that it is the mathematically optimal thing to do. If they hold forever, the market will almost always work back down to their entry price and will eventually go far below, creating a large loss. They never know for certain where the optimum place is to take profits, and they use resistance levels as their best estimate. These levels may or may not be obvious to you, but because they offer opportunities to traders, it is important to look for them constantly. Trend scalpers and swing traders, as well as counter-trend scalpers, expect the pullback and trade accordingly. When the market reaches a target where enough bulls think that they should take profits, their lack of new buying and their selling out of their longs will cause the market to pause. The target can be any resistance level (discussed in the chapters on support and resistance in Part II of this book), or a certain number of ticks above an important signal bar (like six, 10, or 18 in the Emini). The bar might have a bull body that is smaller than the bull body of the prior bar, it might have a tail on the top, or the next bar might be a small bar with a bear body. These are all signs that the bulls are less willing to buy at the top of the swing, that some bulls are taking profits, and that bears are beginning to short for scalps. If enough bulls and bears sell, the pullback will become larger and the current bar might fall below the low of the prior bar. In a strong bull spike, traders will expect that the bull trend will immediately resume, so both the bulls and bears will buy around the low of the prior bar. This creates a high 1 buy signal and is usually followed by a new high. As a bull trend matures and weakens, more two-sided trading will develop, and both the bulls and the bears will expect a pullback to fall for more ticks and last for more bars. The market might form a high 2 buy signal, a triangle, or a wedge bull flag. This creates a small downtrend, and when it reaches some mathematical target, the bulls will begin to buy again, and the bears will take profits and buy back their shorts. Neither will sell again until the market rallies far enough for the process to repeat.


部分买盘也开始枯竭：多头不再愿意只在一到三个最小报价单位的浅跌处买入。他们变得谨慎，怀疑一轮更大的回调即将到来。因为他们相信自己能在高点下方6到10个最小报价单位甚至更低的位置买到，所以高位买入对他们没有吸引力。同时，他们也有动力部分止盈或全部止盈，因为他们相信市场很快会走低，在那里他们可以再次买入，并在市场上涨去测试最近那个高点时赚到更多利润。动能程序察觉到动能消失，也会止盈，在任一方向的动能恢复之前不再入场。空头同样看到了趋势转弱，开始在K线的高点上方、摆动高点上方卖出以剥头皮，而且会在更高的位置分批建仓。一旦看到更多卖压，他们也会在K线低点下方做空，预期出现更深的回调。


> Some of the buying also begins to dry up as bulls become unwilling to continue buying only oneto three-tick dips. They grow cautious and suspect that a larger pullback is imminent. Because they believe that they will be able to buy six to 10 ticks or more below the high, there is no incentive for them to buy any higher. Also, there is an incentive for them to take partial or full profits because they believe that the market will soon be lower, where they can buy again and make additional profits as the market rallies to test the most recent high. Momentum programs sense the loss of momentum and will also take profits and not enter again until momentum in either direction returns. Bears also see the weakening of the trend and begin to sell above the highs of bars and above swing highs for scalps, and they scale in higher. Once they see more selling pressure, they will also short below the lows of bars, expecting a deeper pullback.


大多数多头离场所依据的卖出信号，比他们建立空头仓位所需的信号更弱。他们最初是在强势中寻找止盈机会，比如在摆动高点上方、前一根K线高点上方，或者在某一根大多头趋势K线的收盘价处。在强势中止盈之后，他们会把剩余仓位在弱势中止盈，开始在空头反转K线下方卖出自己的多头仓位；他们怀疑回调会变得更大。大多数人不会加入空头一起去卖，因为大多数交易者都做不到持续稳定地反手做交易。他们一直在想市场在上涨，通常需要先平掉多头、等上几分钟，才能说服自己去做一笔反方向的交易。如果他们相信市场只是在回调、并不是反转，那么一旦认为回调结束，他们就会转而买回自己的多头仓位。既然大多数人做不到、或者不愿意反手，他们在想买入的时候就不愿意手里有空头。如果他们去做了这笔做空剥头皮，多半就再也做不到反手做多，结果会因为想做一笔小小的空头剥头皮，而发现自己被关在一轮多头波段行情之外。为了在一笔低概率的空头上赚1个点，却错过一笔高概率多头的2到4个点，这在数学上说不通。


> Most bulls will exit their longs on a weaker sell signal than they would need to take short positions. They initially look to take profits on strength, like above a swing high or the high of the prior bar or on the close of a large bull trend bar. After taking profits on strength, they will then look to take profits on the remainder of their positions on weakness, and begin to sell out of their longs below bear reversal bars; they suspect that the pullbacks will become larger. Most will not join the bears in shorting, because most traders are unable to reverse a trade consistently well. They have been thinking that the market was going up, and usually need to get out of their longs for several minutes before they can convince themselves that they should take a trade in the opposite direction. If they believe that the market is only pulling back and not reversing, they will instead look to buy back their longs once they think that the pullback has ended. Since most cannot or will not reverse, they don't want to be short when they are looking to buy. If they took the short scalp, they would most likely not be able to reverse back to long, and they would find themselves trapped out of a bull swing because they tried to make a small bear scalp. It does not make mathematical sense to try to make one point on a low-probability short and end up missing two to four points on a high-probability long.


在多头趋势中，会出现一连串更高的高点与更高的低点。趋势强劲时，多头会为了任何理由买入，很多人还会移动自己的保护性止损。如果市场创出新高，他们就会把止损上移到最近那个更高的低点下方。如果足够多的空头做空、足够多的多头止盈，反转可能比交易者起初预期的更强。这往往发生在趋势的后期，也就是此前已经有过好几次回调、而每次之后都创出新的多头高点之后。不过，多头和空头都相信市场会在最近这个摆动低点上方重新掉头向上，所以双方通常都会在该低点处或上方买入。结果要么是一个双底牛旗，要么是另一个更高的低点。这波抛售可能很急，但只要足够多的交易者相信多头趋势仍然完好，他们就会买入，市场就会去测试之前的高点；在那里多头会部分止盈或全部止盈，空头会再次做空。


> In a bull trend, there is a series of higher highs and higher lows. When the trend is strong, bulls will buy for any reason, and many will trail their protective stops. If the market makes a new high, they will raise their stops to below the most recent higher low. If enough bears short and enough bulls take profits, the reversal can be stronger than what traders initially expected. This often happens later in a trend, after several prior pullbacks were followed by new bull highs. However, both the bulls and the bears believe that the market will turn back up above the most recent swing low, and both will usually buy at or above that low. This results in either a double bottom bull flag or another higher low. The sell-off can be sharp, but as long as enough traders believe that the bull trend is intact, traders will buy and the market will test the old high, where bulls will take partial or full profits, and the bears will short again.


随着多头趋势成熟，交易者只会想买入更深的修正，并且预期市场会走出两段式修正，也就是第二段跌破第一段的低点。价格行为会告诉交易者这种更深的修正何时可能出现；一旦他们相信它要出现，就不再把自己的保护性止损挂在最近那个摆动低点下方。他们会转而在更高的位置止盈，比如在最近的摆动高点上方止盈，然后再在那个低点附近买回、重建自己的多头仓位。一旦他们相信市场很可能走出一段两段式修正、因而会跌破最近那个更高的低点，那么继续依赖该低点下方的止损就说不通了。他们会在这一切发生之前平掉大部分或全部仓位，但依然看多。这时多头趋势已经不再创出更高的高点和更高的低点。不过，在更大时间级别的图上，这个更低的低点通常仍位于最近那个更高的低点之上，所以更大级别的多头趋势依然完好。这次两段式回调是一个大型高2买入建仓形态；随着趋势成熟，这些回调会变得更大，内部还会再分小段。如果趋势真的已经反转，就会出现一连串更低的高点和更低的低点；但通常总会有一次清晰的反转（反转在第3册中讨论）。在没有清晰反转的情况下，一段两段式下跌只是一类牛旗，通常后面还会跟着一个新的多头高点。举例来说，第一段下跌可能是一小段空头急速行情，第二段下跌是一小段空头通道。如果这波下跌很强，即便它处在一段紧凑复杂的通道里、并不是空头急速行情，交易者也会预期它至少是两段下跌中的第一段。买在回调处的多头会在趋势高点下方止盈，而空头会在旧高点下方开始激进做空，预期出现一个更低的高点和第二段下跌。


> As the bull trend matures, traders will only look to buy a deeper correction, and they expect the market to make two-legged corrections, where the second leg falls below the low of the first. The price action tells traders when a deeper correction like this is likely, and when they believe that it is, they will no longer trail their protective stops below the most recent swing low. They will look to take profits higher, like above the most recent swing high, and then look to buy again around that low, reestablishing their longs. It does not make sense for them to rely on a stop below the most recent higher low once they believe that the market is likely to have a two-legged correction and, therefore, fall below that low. They will exit most or all of their position before that happens, but still remain bullish. The bull trend is no longer forming higher highs and higher lows. However, this lower low is usually still above the most recent higher low on a higher time frame chart, so the larger bull trend is still intact. This two-legged pullback is a large high 2 buy setup, and as the trend matures, these pullbacks get larger and have subdivisions. If the trend has truly reversed, there will be a series of lower highs and lows, but there is usually a clear reversal (reversals are discussed in book 3). In the absence of a clear reversal, a two-legged down move is just a type of bull flag and is usually followed by a new bull high. For example, the first leg down might be a small bear spike and the second leg down is a small bear channel. If the move down is strong, even if it is in a tight, complex channel and is not a bear spike, traders will expect it to be the first of at least two legs down. Bulls who bought the pullback will take profits below the trend high, and bears will begin to short aggressively below the old high, expecting a lower high and second leg down.


一旦市场开始形成更低的高点，多头通常只会想买入更深的回调，而他们买盘的缺失，又反过来促成了这些更深的回调。空头看到的是同样的价格行为，于是转向持有自己的空头仓位以博取更大利润，预期抛售的规模会变大。市场反复在旧高点附近（略上方、正好在、或略下方）抛售，却又不断从旧低点附近上涨。向上和向下的突破尝试都失败，市场失去方向，造成近期的不确定性。这正是交易区间的标志。多头会反复尝试恢复趋势，空头会反复尝试反转趋势，而两者中有80% 都会失败。由于多头趋势中的交易区间在更大时间级别的图上只是一面牛旗，概率偏向向上突破。总会有某种形态，被多头和空头共同认可为多头趋势即将恢复的信号。当一个可信的形态出现时，愿意在上涨行情中做空剥头皮的空头变少，多头则开始继续朝着区间顶部买入。愿意做空的空头变少、愿意卖出多头仓位的多头变少，上涨行情就会向上突破这个交易区间。如果突破很强，那些原本在建立波段仓位、预期出现更大修正或反转的空头，会买回自己的空头仓位，并且在至少接下来的好几根K线里都不再考虑做空。剥头皮的、做波段的空头都不再做空，多头也不止盈，市场通常就会向上走出一段等距运动，幅度大约等于这个交易区间的高度。之后多头开始止盈，空头再次做空。如果抛售很强，就会出现一次回调、一个交易区间，甚至反转向下。


> Once the market begins to make lower highs, the bulls will usually only look to buy deeper pullbacks, and their absence of buying helps to create those deeper pullbacks. The bears see the same price action, and transition to holding on to their shorts for larger profits, expecting the sell-offs to become larger. The market repeatedly sells off around (slightly above, at, or below) the old high, but continues to rally from around the old low. Upside and downside breakout attempts fail, and the market loses its direction, creating near-term uncertainty. This is the hallmark of a trading range. There will be repeated attempts by the bulls to resume the trend and by the bears to reverse the trend, and 80 percent of both fail. Since a trading range in a bull trend is just a bull flag on a higher time frame chart, the odds favor an upside breakout. There will always be some pattern that the bulls and bears will recognize as a sign that the bull trend is about to resume. When a credible one appears, fewer bears will be willing to scalp shorts on the rally, and the bulls will begin to continue to buy toward the top of the range. With fewer bears willing to short and fewer bulls willing to sell out of their longs, the rally will break above the trading range. If the breakout is strong, the bears who were building a swing position, expecting a larger correction or a reversal, will buy back their shorts and not look to short again for at least several more bars. With neither the scalping nor the swinging bears now shorting and the bulls not taking profits, the market usually runs for about a measured move up, equal to about the height of the trading range. Bulls will then begin to take profits and bears will again short. If the selling is strong, there will be a pullback, a trading range, or even a reversal down.


空头趋势中的情形正好相反。回调最初源于空头在新低处止盈，但总会有一些激进的多头买入，他们认为市场会上涨到足以赚一笔剥头皮的程度。一旦市场上涨到某个阻力位——通常形成的是低2或低3形态——多头就会在止盈的同时卖出自己的多头仓位，空头则再次做空。空头希望市场继续创出更低的高点和更低的低点。每当看到一波急剧的上涨行情，只要它接近最近那个更低的高点，他们就会激进做空。有时他们要到市场触及最近的摆动高点时才大举做空，这就是双顶熊旗如此常见的原因。只要市场继续创出更低的高点，他们就知道大多数交易者会认为空头趋势仍然完好，因而很可能跟随出现又一个更低的低点，在那里他们可以对空头仓位部分止盈或全部止盈。最终，一次回调会演变成交易区间，并出现一些涨破最近那些更低的高点的行情。在更大时间级别的图上，仍然会是更低的高点和更低的低点；但对你正在交易的那张图而言，这个更高的高点是一个信号：空头趋势已经失去了一部分强度。随着空头趋势成熟、转弱，它们常常走出两段式上涨，其中同时出现一个更高的低点和一个更高的高点，但空头趋势依然完好。这就是低2做空建仓形态的基础，它其实就是一次两段式上涨行情。区间内会出现某种形态，让多头和空头都看出空头趋势很可能恢复，而这个形态总是出现在某个阻力位，比如一段等距运动的目标位或一条趋势线。这会让多头不愿意在区间底部附近买入，让空头更愿意一路卖到区间底部。随后市场向下突破，多头剥头皮交易者停止买入，多头波段交易者卖出自己的多头仓位。市场接着下跌大约一段等距运动，此时空头开始止盈，激进的多头再次开始买入。如果多头和空头的买盘都足够强，就会有一次回调、一个交易区间，或者一次向上的趋势反转。


> The opposite happens in a bear trend. The pullbacks are initially due to bears taking profits on new lows, but there is always some buying by aggressive bulls who think that the market will rally far enough for them to make a profitable scalp. Once the market has rallied to some resistance level, usually in a low 2 or low 3 pattern, the bulls will sell out of their longs as they take profits, and the bears will short again. The bears want the market to continue to make lower highs and lows. Whenever they see a sharp rally, they will aggressively short when it approaches the most recent lower high. They sometimes don't short heavily until the market reaches the most recent swing high, which is why double top bear flags are so common. As long as the market continues to make lower highs, they know that most traders will see the bear trend as being intact, and therefore likely to be followed by another lower low, where they can take partial or full profits on their shorts. Eventually a pullback will evolve into a trading range, and there will be some rallies above the most recent lower highs. On a higher time frame chart, there will still be lower highs and lows, but on the chart that you are trading, this higher high is a sign that the bear trend has lost some of its strength. As bear trends mature and weaken, they often form two-legged rallies where there is both a higher low and a higher high, but the bear trend is still intact. This is the basis for a low 2 short setup, which is simply a two-legged rally. There will be some pattern within the range that will tell both bulls and bears that the bear trend is likely to resume, and it will always be at a resistance level, like a measured move or a trend line. This will make bulls less willing to buy near the bottom of the range and bears more willing to continue to sell all the way to the bottom. The market then breaks to the downside, the bull scalpers stop buying, and the bull swing traders sell out of their longs. The market then falls for about a measured move, where the bears will begin to take profits and the aggressive bulls will once again begin to buy. If the buying by the bulls and the bears is strong enough, there will be a pullback, a trading range, or a trend reversal up.


回调的最后一段行情，往往是逆着趋势的一段微型通道（牛旗末端的一段空头微型通道，或者熊旗末端的一段多头微型通道）。微型通道的突破通常只走一两根K线，随后就会出现回调，尤其当这条微型通道有四根或更多K线时。如果趋势很强，往往根本没有回调，因此在这条微型通道突破时入场是一笔合理的交易。当趋势不是很强时，微型通道的突破通常在一两根K线之内就会有一次失败的尝试。和所有突破一样，交易者必须把这次突破的强弱，与针对这次突破失败所出现的信号K线的强弱放在一起比较。如果突破明显更强——尤其是在底层趋势也强的时候——这次反转尝试很可能失败，并引出一个突破回调建仓形态，给交易者第二次顺着突破方向入场的机会。如果突破相对较弱，比如是一根带大影线的小趋势K线，而反转K线很强，尤其是在背景很可能导致反转的情况下（比如一面正好位于交易区间顶部下方的牛旗），那么这次反转尝试多半会成功，交易者就应当做这笔反转入场。如果突破与反转强弱大致相当，而且没有强势的底层趋势，交易者就会去评估下一根K线的强弱。举例来说，如果交易区间中部出现一面牛旗，而突破该旗形的那根多头趋势K线后面跟着一根同样强的空头反转K线，并且市场又跌破那根空头反转K线的低点，交易者就会去评估这根空头入场K线的形态。如果它变成一根多头反转K线，他们就会认定市场只是在从牛旗的突破处形成回调，于是会在这根K线的高点上方买入。如果它反而是一根强势的空头趋势K线，尤其是在它收于自己的低点、并且收在多头突破K线的低点下方时，交易者就会把这个形态看成一次空头突破，并寻找做空机会——前提是他们还没有在那根空头反转K线下方做空。


> The final leg of a pullback is often a micro channel against the trend (a bear micro channel at the end of a bull flag or a bull micro channel at the end of a bear flag). The breakout of a micro channel usually only goes for a bar or two before there is a pullback, especially if the micro channel has four or more bars. If the trend is strong, there is often no pullback and therefore entering on the breakout of the micro channel is a reasonable trade. When the trend is not very strong, the breakout from the micro channel usually has a failure attempt within a bar or two. As is the case with all breakouts, traders have to assess the strength of the breakout compared to the strength of the signal bar for the failed breakout. If the breakout is significantly stronger, especially if the underlying trend is strong, the reversal attempt will likely fail and lead to a breakout pullback setup that will give traders a second chance to enter in the direction of the breakout. If the breakout is relatively weak, like a small trend bar with big tails, and the reversal bar is strong, especially if the context is likely to lead to a reversal (like a bull flag just below the top of a trading range), the reversal attempt will probably succeed and traders should take the reversal entry. If the breakout and reversal are about equally strong, and there is no strong underlying trend, traders will assess the strength of the next bar. For example, if there is a bull flag in the middle of a trading range, and the bull trend bar that breaks out of the flag is followed by an equally strong bear reversal bar, and the market trades below the low of that bar, traders will evaluate the appearance of that bear entry bar. If it becomes a bull reversal bar, they will assume that the market is just forming a pullback from the breakout of the bull flag, and will buy above the high of the bar. If instead it is a strong bear trend bar, especially if it closes on its low and below the low of the bull breakout bar, traders will see the pattern as a bear breakout and look to get short, if they did not already short below the bear reversal bar.


严格来说，回调就是一根逆着趋势走得足以打掉前一根K线极值的K线。在多头趋势中，回调是指某根K线至少向下延伸到前一根K线低点之下1个最小报价单位。不过，更宽泛的定义更有用：趋势动能中的任何停顿（包括内包K线、反方向的趋势K线或十字星K线）都应该被视为回调，即使那可能只是横盘、并没有真正往回走。哪怕是最强的趋势，随着它推进，也会在某个时点开始给出“这次回调会有多深”的证据。最常见的情况是，那会是一片双边成交的区域。举例来说，在一段急速与通道式多头趋势中，急速行情之后市场出现停顿或回调，形成通道的起点。当这段趋势通道结束、抛售（回调）开始时，市场通常会向下测试到通道底部。那里正是空头开始卖出的位置；随着多头通道涨到他们的做空入场价之上，他们开始担心。随着多头趋势推进，他们和其他空头卖出得更多；但一旦趋势掉头向下、进入回调，这些空头会非常乐意在自己最早、最低的那笔做空入场价——也就是通道的起点——把全部仓位都平掉。一旦他们回到空仓，就不会再考虑在那个区域卖出，因为他们已经看到自己先前那笔做空之后市场涨了多远。不过，如果他们仍然看空，就会在一轮上涨行情中再次做空。如果这轮上涨行情在先前高点之下结束，就会形成一个更低的高点，并且通常会引出第二段下跌。如果空头特别强，这个更低的高点就可能是一段新空头趋势的起点，而不只是一个刚成形交易区间里的第二次回调。


> In the strictest sense, a pullback is a bar that moves against the trend enough to take out the prior bar's extreme. In a bull trend, a pullback is a move where a bar extends at least one tick below the low of the prior bar. However, a broader definition is more useful, and any pause (including an inside bar, an opposite trend bar, or a doji bar) in a trend's momentum should be considered to be a pullback, even though there may be only sideways action and not an actual move backward. As even the strongest trend progresses, it at some point begins to give evidence of how deep a pullback will be. Most commonly, it will be an area of two-sided trading. For example, after the spike in a spike and channel bull trend, the market has a pause or pullback that creates the start of the channel. Once the trend channel ends and a sell-off (pullback) begins, it will usually test down to the bottom of the channel. That is where bears started selling, and as the bull channel goes above their short entry price, they begin to worry. They and other bears sell more as the bull trend advances, but once the trend turns down into a pullback, those bears will be very happy to exit all of their entries at their earliest and lowest short entry price, which was the start of the channel. Once they are flat, they will not look to sell in that area, because they saw how far the market rallied after their earlier short trade. However, if they are still bearish, they will short again on a rally. If the rally ends below the prior high, it will create a lower high and usually leads to a second leg down. If the bears are particularly strong, that lower high could be the start of a new bear trend and not just a second pullback in an incipient trading range.


趋势末端的楔形也是如此。如果空头趋势形成一个向下倾斜的楔形，市场会试图向上修正到楔形顶部，也就是最早那批多头开始买入的位置。如果市场能够到达他们最早那笔入场价，他们就能把那笔交易保本平掉，同时在所有更低位置的仓位上获利；而在市场再次下跌之前，他们多半不愿再买入。他们从第一笔交易中学到：自己买的价格太高了；他们不喜欢在市场持续下跌时一直扛着多头仓位的浮动亏损，也不想再经历一次。这一次，他们会等待回调，希望市场形成一个更高的低点，甚至是更低的低点。他们预期楔形最初的那个低点会在随后任何一次回调中充当支撑位，而在该价位附近、把止损放在略低于该价的位置买入，能让他们得到一笔风险明确且有限的入场，这一点他们喜欢。


> The same is true for a wedge at the end of a trend. If a bear trend forms a downward-sloping wedge, the market will try to correct to the top of the wedge where the earliest bulls began to buy. If the market can reach their earliest entry price, then they can exit that trade at breakeven and with a profit on all of their lower entries, and they will likely not want to buy until the market falls again. They learned from their first trade that they bought at too high a price; they did not like riding through the open losses of their long positions as the market continued to fall and do not want to experience that again. This time, they will wait for a pullback and hope the market forms a higher low or even a lower low. They expect that the original low of the wedge will be support on any subsequent pullback and that buying near that level with a stop a little below that price gives them an entry with a defined and limited risk, and they like that.


市场在趋势中倾向于回测最早出现双边成交的区域，这一点让有洞察力的交易者能够预判回调可能何时形成、以及它大致会走多远。他们不会在双边成交刚出现时就逆势入场，但双边成交告诉他们：逆势交易者正在开始建仓，用不了多久，市场很可能就会回调到那个价位。当趋势通道、楔形或楼梯形态开始出现反转的迹象之后（见第3册中讲趋势反转的那一章），他们就会去做逆势交易，并指望在双边成交开始的区域（通道的起点）获利离场。


> The tendency of the market in a trend to test the earliest area of two-sided trading allows perceptive traders to anticipate when a pullback might form and how far it will likely extend. They won't want to enter countertrend at the first sign of two-sided trading, but that two-sided trading tells them that countertrend traders are beginning to take positions and at some point before too long the market will likely pull back to that price level. After the trend channel or wedge or stairs pattern begins to develop signs of a reversal (see the chapter on trend reversals in book 3), they will take countertrend trades and look to exit with a profit in the area where the two-sided trading began (the start of the channel).


因为回调本身就是一段趋势，尽管它相对于它所回调的那个更大趋势通常很小，但和所有趋势一样，它通常至少包含两段行情。单段行情和三段行情的回调也很常见，小型通道和三角形同样常见；不过所有回调都相对短暂，交易者会预期趋势很快恢复。有时这些行情段只有在小一个时间级别的图上才看得见，另一些时候它们很大，每一段又细分出更小的行情段，而每一小段同样包含两段。由于交易者预期主趋势很快恢复，他们会在回调中反向操作突破。举例来说，如果有一段强空头趋势，最终出现了一次包含两段上涨的回调，那么当市场向上突破第一段上涨的高点时，空头的数量通常会远远多于多头。尽管市场向上突破的只是一个多头趋势中的摆动高点，买入这次突破的多头通常也会被做空的空头所压倒，因为他们预期这次突破会失败、空头趋势很快就会恢复。他们会在摆动高点处及其上方用限价单和市价单做空。他们把这次突破看成在高价位重新建立空头仓位的短暂机会。由于反转趋势的尝试中有80% 会失败，概率强烈偏向空头。对于强趋势中的第一次两段式回调，这一点尤其成立。


> Since a pullback is a trend, even though it is usually small compared to the larger trend from which it is pulling back, like all trends it will commonly have at least two legs. One-legged and three-legged pullbacks are also common, as are small channels and triangles, but all pullbacks are relatively brief, and traders will expect the trend to resume soon. Sometimes the legs are visible only on a smaller time frame chart, and other times they are large and each leg breaks down into smaller legs, each of which also has two legs. Because traders expect the major trend to resume soon, they will fade breakouts in a pullback. For example, if there is a strong bear trend that finally has a pullback with two legs up, there will usually be far more bears than bulls as the market breaks out above the high of the first leg up. Even though the market is breaking out above a swing high in a bull trend, the bulls buying the breakout will usually be overwhelmed by bears who will short it, because they expect the breakout to fail and for the bear trend to resume very soon. They will short on limit and market orders at and above the swing high. They see this breakout as a brief opportunity to reestablish shorts at a high price. Since 80 percent of attempts to reverse a trend will fail, the odds strongly favor the bears. This is especially true for the first two-legged pullback in a strong trend.


任何包含两段的行情，都应该当作回调来交易，即便它是顺势的。有时趋势中的最后一段行情就是一段顺势的两段式运动，在多头趋势中走向一个更高或更低的高点，在空头趋势中走向一个更低或更高的低点。举例来说，如果一段多头趋势出现一波抛售，跌穿了多头趋势线，而这次趋势线突破之后跟着一次两段式回调，那么这次回调只不过回测了先前的极值，甚至可能超过旧极值。这意味着，这次趋势线突破之后的回调，既可能形成一个更低的高点，也可能形成更高的高点，而它仍然属于向新空头趋势过渡的一部分。严格来说，空头趋势要到最终那个高点之后才开始；但那个最终高点，往往只是跌破多头趋势线的那次突破之后的一次更高的高点回调。


> Any move that has two legs should be traded as if it is a pullback, even if it is with the trend. Sometimes the final leg in a trend is a two-legged, with-trend move to a higher or lower high in a bull trend or a lower or higher low in a bear trend. For example, if there is a bull trend that has a sell-off that falls through the bull trend line and this trend line breakout is followed by a two-legged pullback, that pullback simply tests the prior extreme and can even exceed the old extreme. This means that the pullback from that trend line breakout can result in either a lower high or even a higher high and still be part of a transition into a new bear trend. Strictly speaking, the bear trend does not begin until after the final high, but that final high is often just a higher high pullback from the breakout below the bull trend line.


什么才算两段？你可以按收盘价画一张线图，往往能清楚地看到一段两段式行情。如果你用的是K线图或蜡烛图，最容易辨认的两段式行情是这样：先有一段逆势行情，接着一段较小的顺势行情，然后再来第二段逆势行情（教科书式的 ABC 回调）。那么，为什么行情常常在第二段之后反转？以多头趋势中的一次两段式回调为例。多头会在新低处买入（也就是 C 段），认为第二段下跌就是趋势的终点。同时，那些一直在等两段式修正的空头剥头皮交易者，会买回自己的空头仓位。最后，那些买在第一段下跌低点（也就是 A 段）的激进多头，会在市场走向更低低点的过程中加仓自己的多头仓位。如果所有这些买盘压倒了那些在跌破第一段下跌时做空的新空头，就会引发一轮上涨行情，而它通常至少会去回测此前的高点。


> What qualifies as two legs? You can create a line chart based on closes and often clearly see a two-legged move. If you are using bar or candle charts, the easiest two-legged move to see is one in which there is a countertrend move, then a smaller with-trend move, and then a second countertrend move (a textbook ABC pullback). So why does the move often reverse after the second leg? Look at a two-legged pullback in a bull trend as an example. Bulls will buy the new low (the C leg), thinking that the second leg down will be the end of the trend. Also, short scalpers who were looking for a two-legged correction will be buying back their shorts. Finally, aggressive bulls who bought the low of the first leg down (the A leg) will now be adding to their long positions on the move to a lower low. If all of these buyers overwhelm the new bears who shorted on the breakout below the first leg down, a rally will ensue and it will usually test the old high at a minimum.


不过，很多时候这两段行情只有在小一个时间级别的图上才清晰可见，在你正在看的那张图上只能靠推断。由于用一张图做交易，比整天来回查看多张图要容易，所以如果交易者能在面前这张图上看出这两段行情——哪怕只是推断出来的——他们就占优势。


> However, oftentimes the two legs are clearly visible only on a smaller time frame chart and have to be inferred on the chart that you are viewing. Since it is easier to use a single chart for trading than to be checking multiple charts all day long, traders have an advantage if they can see the two legs on the chart in front of them, if only by inference.


在多头市场中，当出现一连串多头趋势K线时，一根空头趋势K线就可以被认定为回调的第一段行情（A 段），即便这根K线的低点位于前一根K线低点之上。如果你去看小一个时间级别的图，那段逆势行情很可能清晰可见。如果下一根K线顺势收盘，但高点低于那根终结多头波段行情的K线的高点，那么它就是 B 段。如果接下来出现一根空头K线，或者一根低点低于前一根K线低点的K线，就会形成第二段下跌（C 段）。


> In a bull market, when there is a series of bull trend bars, a bear trend bar can be assumed to be the first leg of a pullback (the A leg) even if the low of the bar is above the low of the prior bar. If you examined a smaller time frame chart, a countertrend leg would likely be evident. If the next bar has a with-trend close but a high below that of the bar that ended the bull swing, then this is the B leg. If there is then a bear bar or a bar with a low below the low of the prior bar, this will create the second leg down (the C leg).


需要推断的成分越多，这个形态就越不可靠，因为能看到它、或对它抱有信心的人会更少。交易者投入的资金多半会更少，离场也会更快。


> The more that has to be inferred, the less reliable is the pattern, since fewer traders will see it or have confidence in it. Traders will likely commit less capital and be quicker to exit.


这里有一个显而易见的要点。如果这轮正在回调的趋势是以一波高潮、或任何重要的趋势反转形态结束的，那么趋势已经改变，你就不该再去寻找旧趋势中的回调来入场。它结束了——至少在这10根K线左右里结束了，也许当天剩下的时间都结束了。所以在一次强劲的上涨行情之后，如果出现了楔形顶，或者在跌破多头趋势线之后出现了一个更低的低点，你现在应该寻找的是做空的建仓形态，而不是旧多头趋势中可以买入的回调。当是否已经发生了一次可能的趋势反转还不清楚时，两个方向的建仓形态都很有可能奏效，至少做剥头皮是如此。发生了趋势反转的可能性越大，避开旧方向上的交易就越重要，因为此时新方向上很可能至少会走出两段行情。另外，这波行情持续的时间和点数，通常与反转的清晰程度大致成正比。当你遇到一个极好的反转建仓形态时，应当把一部分仓位做波段持有，极少情况下甚至可以把全部仓位做波段持有。


> There is an obvious point here. If the trend that is now pulling back ended in a climax or any significant trend reversal pattern, the trend has changed and you should not be looking to enter pullbacks in the old trend. It is over, at least for maybe 10 bars or so and maybe for the rest of the day. So after a strong rally, if there is a wedge top or a lower low after a break of the bull trend line, you should now be looking for setups to short and not pullbacks in the old bull trend to buy. When it is not clear that there was a probable trend reversal, setups in both directions are likely to work, at least for scalps. The more likely it is that a trend reversal has taken place, the more important it becomes to avoid trades in the old direction, since it is now likely that there will be at least two legs in the new direction. Also, the amount of time and number of points in this move will usually be roughly proportional to the clarity of the reversal. When you have a great reversal setup, you should swing part or, rarely, even all of your position.


所有回调都始于某种反转形态。这种反转通常强到足以诱使逆势交易者逆着趋势建仓，但还不够强、不足以构成一个可靠的逆势建仓形态。由于这个建仓形态和这次回调都不足以改变始终入场交易的方向，交易者就不该去寻找逆势交易。相反，他们应该去寻找一个意味着回调可能结束的建仓形态，然后顺着趋势方向入场。不过，由于回调始于一次反转，很多交易者会过度谨慎，把一笔极好的交易给自己劝退了。对任何一笔交易，你都不会有100% 的把握；但当你相当有把握地认为一笔交易看起来不错时，你就必须相信数学期望、做这笔交易，并且坦然接受“有时你确实会亏”这一现实。这就是这一行的本质；只有愿意接受亏损，你才谈得上靠交易谋生。记住，一个失败率高达70% 的美国职业棒球大联盟击球手，会被视为超级明星，并靠那另外的30% 赚到数百万美元。


> All pullbacks begin with a reversal pattern of some type. It is usually strong enough to entice counter-trend traders into taking a position against the trend, but not strong enough to be a reliable countertrend setup. Since the setup and the pullback are not strong enough to change the direction of the always-in trade, traders should not be looking for a countertrend trade. Instead, they should be looking for a setup that signifies a possible end of the pullback and then enter in the direction of the trend. However, since the pullback began with a reversal, many traders would be overly cautious and talk themselves out of a great trade. You are never going to be 100 percent certain of any trade, but when you are reasonably confident that a trade looks good, you have to trust the math, take the trade, and simply accept the reality that you will lose some of the time. That is just the nature of the business, and you cannot make a living as a trader unless you are willing to take losses. Remember, a major league baseball hitter who fails 70 percent of the time is considered to be a superstar and makes millions off that other 30 percent.


当市场处在弱趋势中，或者处在从交易区间向趋势过渡的早期阶段，它有时会是这样的：先有一面旗形，接着是一次旗形突破，然后是一次回调，而这次回调又变成另一面旗形。有时市场会这样反复好几次，最后才出现一次强势突破。


> When the market is in a weak trend, or in the early stages of transitioning from a trading range into a trend, it will sometimes have a flag, and then a flag breakout, and then a pullback, and that pullback becomes another flag. The market will sometimes do this several times before a strong breakout materializes.


一根K线和两根K线的停顿，比那些持续许多根K线、并且真正从极值往回走的回调更难交易。举例来说，如果有一段强劲的多头行情，其中最后一根K线是一根小K线，它的高点只比前一根K线的高点低一两个最小报价单位，而前一根K线是一根大多头趋势K线、前面还跟着一两根大多头趋势K线；这时如果你在这根小K线的高点上方1个最小报价单位处买入，你就是在当日高点买入。由于很多机构会对每一个新高都反向操作，因此存在一个不小的风险：这波行情可能反转并打掉你的止损，而你的止盈目标还没被触及。不过，如果趋势非常强，这仍是一笔重要的、值得做的交易。这笔交易之所以这么难，部分原因是你几乎没有时间去分析趋势的强弱、去检查有没有可能出现趋势通道线过靶，或者寻找其他可能导致这笔交易失败的理由。


> One-and two-bar pauses are more difficult to trade than pullbacks that last many bars and actually pull back from the extreme. For example, if there is a strong bull move in which the last bar was a small bar with a high just a tick or two below the prior bar's high and that bar was a large bull trend bar and followed one or two other large bull trend bars, if you buy one tick above this bar, you are buying at the high of the day. Since lots of institutions fade every new high, there is a substantial risk that the move might reverse and hit your stop before your profit target is reached. However, if the trend is very strong, this is an important trade to take. Part of what makes this trade so difficult is that you have very little time to analyze the strength of the trend and to look for possible trend channel line overshoots or other reasons why the trade might fail.


另一种更难处理的停顿，是一根小十字星，它的高点比此前那根强多头趋势K线的高点高出1个最小报价单位。在这根十字星的高点上方买入，有时是一笔好交易；但对大多数交易者来说，要足够快地评估风险太难了，不如等一个更清晰的建仓形态。不买停顿K线突破的一个理由是：如果最后一两根趋势K线带有相当大的影线，那就说明逆势交易者已经能够施加一些影响。另外，如果此前那次顺势入场是在一次更大的回调之后（比如一个高2），你就应该犹豫，因为每一次回调通常都会变得更深，而不是更浅。不过，如果市场刚刚完成突破，并且出现了三根收盘价接近各自高点的多头趋势K线，那么在这些K线之后的那根停顿K线高点上方买入时，剥头皮成功的可能性是不错的。一般来说，强多头趋势早期出现的这类高1做多（或在空头趋势中对应的低1做空），是大多数交易者唯一应该考虑的停顿K线入场。还要记住：一根K线突破之后的停顿K线，同样可能是一笔反方向入场的信号，因为一根K线的突破常常失败，尤其是当它逆势时。


> An even more difficult pause is a small doji with a high one tick above the high of the prior strong bull trend bar. Buying above the high of the doji is sometimes a good trade, but for most traders, it is too difficult to assess risk quickly enough and it is better to wait for a clearer setup. A reason against buying a pause bar breakout is if the last trend bar or two had fairly large tails, which indicates that countertrend traders were able to assert some influence. Also, if the prior with-trend entry followed a larger pullback, like a high 2, you should be hesitant since each pullback usually gets deeper, not shallower. However, if the market just broke out and had three bull trend bars with closes near their highs, then the chance of a successful scalp when you buy above the pause bar that follows these bars is good. In general, these high 1 longs (or low 1 shorts in bear trends) in the early stages of a strong bull trend are the only pause bars entries that most traders should consider. Also, remember that a pause bar after a one-bar breakout is just as likely to be an entry in the opposite direction, since one-bar breakouts often fail, especially if they are countertrend.


如果一次回调相对于趋势很小，那么它一结束就入场通常是安全的。如果它大到足以成为一段可交易的、强劲的逆势行情，那最好等到第二个信号形成。举例来说，如果强多头趋势中出现了一段持续很久的空头通道，与其在它第一次反转向上时买入，不如等到这次突破之后出现一次回调，然后买入这个突破回调，这样更安全。


> If a pullback is small compared to the trend, it is usually safe to enter as soon as it ends. If it is large enough to be a tradable, strong countertrend move, it is better to wait until a second signal sets up. For example, if there is a protracted bear channel in a strong bull trend, rather than buying the first reversal back up, it is safer to wait for a pullback from that breakout and buy the breakout pullback.


所有多头趋势中的回调，结束都有其原因，而这个原因永远是：市场已经到达某种支撑。有时它们结束得很平静，另一些时候则会出现逆着主趋势的强趋势K线，几乎要把趋势反转掉。大型回调如此，小型旗形突破之后的一两根K线回调也是如此。就连1987年和2009年的股市崩盘，也都结束在月线图的多头趋势线上，因此它们只是多头趋势中的回调。大多数回调结束在一组聚集的支撑位处，尽管很多交易者可能看不到其中的一部分、甚至全都看不到。有些交易者会买入多头趋势中的回调，是因为他们只盯着某一个支撑位——无论那是一条多头趋势线、一条沿牛旗底部的通道线、一个此前的最高价或最低价、某条均线，还是其他任何类型的支撑；另一些交易者买入，则是因为他们在同一区域看到了另一个不同的支撑位。一旦有足够多的买盘涌入、压倒了空头，趋势就会恢复。空头趋势中的回调也是如此。它们总是结束在一组聚集的阻力位处，尽管市场所看到的那个阻力，往往很容易被人忽略。一旦市场接近关键价格，价格真空效应往往就占据主导。举例来说，如果买家相信市场正在接近一个重要的支撑位，他们常常会退到一边，等这个价位被触及。这可能导致一段非常强的空头急速行情；但支撑一旦被触及，多头就会进场，坚决而猛烈地买入。制造了这次回调的空头也是一样。他们同样看到了这个支撑位，市场越接近它，他们就越确信市场会走到那里。结果是：在市场到达该价位之前，他们一直激进而不停地卖出；到达之后，他们突然停止卖出，迅速买回自己的空头仓位。这次回调可能以一根大的空头趋势K线收尾，看上去像是要把始终入场交易翻转为做空，但接下来几根K线里并没有出现后续行情。相反，多头趋势恢复了，有时一开始还很缓慢。由于多头和空头都在买入，反转可能很急、也可能走得很远。价格真空效应始终存在，即使在最戏剧性的反转中也是如此，比如1987年和2009年的股市崩盘。这两次市场中都在自由落体式下跌，但当市场跌破月线趋势线一小段之后，都强劲反转向上。这两次崩盘尽管声势惊人，却只是价格真空效应发挥作用时的例证。


> All bull pullbacks end for a reason, and that reason always is that the market has reached some kind of support. Sometimes they end quietly and other times with strong trend bars against the main trend and come close to reversing the trend. This is true of large pullbacks, and one-or two-bar pullbacks from breakouts of small flags. Even the 1987 and 2009 stock market crashes ended at the monthly bull trend line, and were therefore just pullbacks in a bull trend. Most end at a cluster of support levels, even though many traders may not see some or all of them. Some traders will buy a pullback in a bull trend because they are focused on one support level, whether it is a bull trend line, a channel line along the bottom of the bull flag, a prior high or low, some moving average, or any other type of support, and others will buy because they see a different support level in the same area. Once there are enough buyers coming in to overwhelm the bears, the trend will resume. The same is true of bear pullbacks. They always end at a cluster of resistance levels, although it is often easy to not see the resistance that the market is seeing. Once the market gets close to the key price, the vacuum effect often dominates. For example, if buyers believe that the market is getting close to an important support level, they will often step aside and wait for that level to be hit. This can result in a very strong bear spike, but once the support is hit, the bulls come in and buy aggressively and relentlessly. The same is true for the bears who created the pullback. They, too, see the support level, and the closer the market gets to it, the more confident they are that the market will get there. The result is that they sell aggressively and relentlessly until the level is reached, and then they suddenly stop selling and quickly buy back their shorts. The pullback can end with a large bear trend bar that looks like it might flip the always-in trade to short, but the follow-through selling over the next bars does not develop. Instead, the bull trend resumes, sometimes slowly at first. With both the bulls and the bears buying, the reversal can be sharp and go a long way. The vacuum effect is always present, even during the most dramatic reversals, like the 1987 and the 2009 stock market crashes. In both instances, the market was in a free fall, but strongly reversed up once the market fell a little below the monthly trend line. As dramatic as both crashes were, they were just examples of the vacuum effect at work.


旗形突破之后出现的一两根K线回调，也会出现完全相同的行为。举例来说，如果一段强空头趋势中，均线处出现一个低2熊旗并触发了做空，那么入场K线后面可能跟着一根多头趋势K线。这代表一次突破失败，它可能是一段多头趋势或一波更大级别空头上涨行情的开端。不过，这种情形通常都会失败；而当一次失败又失败时，它就变成了更大趋势中的一次回调。在这里，它变成了一个突破回调做空建仓形态。交易者会预期它失败，激进的空头会在这根多头趋势K线的收盘价处做空，也会在它高点的略下方和略上方做空。更保守的交易者会等待确认：确认这根空头趋势K线只是熊旗突破之后的一次回调。他们会在该空头K线低点下方挂止损做空；如果这次回调持续得更久一些，就在接下来的一两根K线下方挂止损做空。


> This same behavior happens on a one-or two-bar pullback from the breakout of a flag. For example, if there is a low 2 bear flag at the moving average in a strong bear trend and it triggers a short, the entry bar might be followed by a bull trend bar. This represents a failed breakout and could be the start of a bull trend or a larger bear rally. However, it usually fails, and when a failure fails, it becomes a pullback in the larger trend. Here, it becomes a breakout pullback short setup. Traders will expect it to fail, and aggressive bears will short on its close and just below and above its high. More conservative traders will wait for confirmation that this bear trend bar is just a pullback from the breakout of the bear flag. They will short on a stop below the low of the bear bar, or the next bar or two, if the pullback continues a little longer.


由于回调只是趋势中的一次停顿、而不是反转，所以你一旦认定某段行情是自己所认为的回调，你就相信趋势会恢复，并且趋势的极值会被测试。举例来说，如果有一段多头趋势，随后市场抛售了好几根K线，而你把这次抛售看作是买入机会，那么你就相信它只是多头趋势中的一次回调。你预期多头趋势的高点会被测试。有一点很重要：这次测试并不一定要创出新高。是的，它常常是一个更高的高点，但它也可以是一个双顶或一个更低的高点。测试之后，你再来判断多头趋势是仍然完好，还是已经转变为交易区间、甚至空头趋势。


> Since a pullback is only a pause in a trend and not a reversal, once you identify what you believe is a pullback, you believe that the trend will resume and there will be a test of the trend's extreme. For example, if there is a bull trend and then the market sells off for several bars and if you see that sell-off as a buying opportunity, then you believe that it is just a pullback in the bull trend. You are expecting a test of the bull trend's high. It is important to note that the test does not have to reach a new high. Yes, it is often a higher high, but it can be a double top or a lower high. After the test, you will then decide whether the bull trend is intact or has transitioned into a trading range or even a bear trend.


回调常常是一段强劲的急速行情，让交易者怀疑趋势是否已经反转。举例来说，一段多头趋势中可能出现一根或两根大的空头趋势K线，跌破均线，甚至跌破交易区间好几个最小报价单位。交易者这时会怀疑：始终入场方向是否正在翻转向下。他们需要看到的，是卖盘出现后续行情，也许只要再来一根空头趋势K线就够了。所有人都会紧紧盯着下一根K线。如果它是一根大的空头趋势K线，大多数交易者就会相信反转已被确认，并开始以市价、以及在回调中做空。如果这根K线反而是多头收盘，他们就会怀疑这次反转尝试已经失败，而这波抛售只是价格一次短暂但猛烈的下挫，因而是一个买入机会。新手交易者看到那根强劲的空头急速行情，却忽略了它所处的强多头趋势。他们会在空头趋势K线的收盘价处、在它的低点下方、在接下来几根K线中任何一次小幅反弹处、以及在任何一个低1或低2做空形态下方卖出。聪明的多头正在做这些交易的反方向，因为他们明白正在发生什么。


> Pullbacks are often strong spikes that make traders wonder if the trend has reversed. For example, in a bull trend, there might be a large bear trend bar or two that break below the moving average and maybe several ticks below a trading range. Traders will then wonder if the always-in direction is in the process of flipping to down. What they need to see is follow-through selling in the form of maybe just one more bear trend bar. Everyone will watch that next bar closely. If it is a large bear trend bar, most traders will believe that the reversal has been confirmed and will start shorting at the market and on pullbacks. If the bar instead has a bull close, they will suspect that the reversal attempt has failed and that the sell-off is just a brief, but sharp, markdown in price and therefore a buying opportunity. Beginning traders see the strong bear spike and ignore the strong bull trend in which it is occurring. They sell the close of the bear trend bar, below its low, any small bounce over the next few bars, and below any low 1 or low 2 sell setup. Smart bulls are taking the opposite side of those trades because they understand what is happening.


市场一直在试图反转，但这些反转尝试中有80% 会失败，变成牛旗。反转尝试发生时，那两三根空头K线可能非常有说服力；但如果没有卖出方向的后续行情，多头就会把这波抛售看成绝佳机会，在短暂卖出高潮的低点附近重新做多。有经验的多头和空头会等待这类强趋势K线出现，有时干脆退到一边，直到它形成。然后他们进场买入，因为他们把这看作卖出的高潮式终结。空头买回自己的空头仓位，多头重建自己的多头仓位。这与趋势末端发生的情形正好相反：在趋势末端，强势交易者在等待一根巨大的趋势K线。举例来说，在一段靠近支撑区的强空头趋势中，常常会出现一次迟到的突破，表现为一根异常巨大的空头趋势K线。多头和空头此前都停止买入，直到看见它形成。到了那一刻，双方都买入这个卖出高潮：空头把它看作对空头仓位止盈的绝佳价格，多头把它看作以极低价格买入的短暂机会。


> The market is always trying to reverse, but 80 percent of those reversal attempts fail and become bull flags. At the time the reversal attempt is occurring, the two or three bear bars can be very persuasive, but without follow-through selling, the bulls see the sell-off as a great opportunity to get long again near the low of a brief sell climax. Experienced bulls and bears wait for these strong trend bars and sometimes step aside until one forms. Then they come into the market and buy because they view it as the climactic end of the selling. The bears buy back their shorts and the bulls reestablish their longs. This is the opposite of what happens at the end of a trend when the strong traders are waiting for one large trend bar. For example, in a strong bear trend near a support area, there will often be a late breakout in the form of an unusually large bear trend bar. Both the bulls and the bears stopped buying until they saw it form. At that point, both buy the sell climax, because the bears see it as a great price to take profits on their shorts and the bulls see it as a brief opportunity to buy at a very low price.


如果交易者认为自己看到的只是一次回调，那他们就会相信趋势仍然完好。在评估交易者等式时，概率从来都不是确定已知的；但由于他们做的是顺势交易，他们可以假定一次上下等幅运动的方向概率是60%。它可能更高，但不太可能低很多。否则，他们就会得出结论：这次回调持续得太久，已经失去预测价值，变成了一个普通交易区间——而后者的最终突破向上或向下的概率大致相同。一旦确定了风险，他们就可以设定一个至少与风险等大的止盈目标，并合理地假定自己有大约60% 或更高的成功率。举例来说，如果他们买入高盛（GS）牛旗的突破，保护性止损放在该牛旗下方、大约低于入场价50美分处，那么他们就可以假定自己有至少60% 的概率在这笔多头上赚到至少50美分。他们的止盈目标可能是回测多头趋势的高点。如果确实如此，而那个高点位于入场价上方 $2.00，他们很可能仍有大约60% 的成功率，但此时潜在回报是风险的四倍，这就让交易者等式得出一个非常有利的结果。


> If traders see what they believe is just a pullback, then they believe that the trend is still intact. When they are evaluating the trader's equation, the probability is never known with certainty, but since they are making a trade in the direction of the trend, they can assume that the directional probability of an equidistant move is 60 percent. It might be higher but it is unlikely to be much lower. Otherwise, they would have concluded that the pullback had lasted so long that it had lost its predictive value and had become an ordinary trading range, which has about an equal probability of the eventual breakout being up or down. Once they determine their risk, they can then set a profit target that is at least as large as the risk and reasonably assume that they have about a 60 percent chance or better of being successful. For example, if they are buying a breakout of a bull flag in Goldman Sachs (GS) and their protective stop is below the bull flag, about 50 cents below their entry, they can assume that they have at least a 60 percent chance of making at least a 50 cent profit on their long. Their profit target might be a test of the bull high. If it is and that high is $2.00 above their entry, they likely still have about a 60 percent chance of success, but now their potential reward is four times their risk, and this creates a very favorable result from the trader's equation.


一旦你相信市场已经反转，那么在新趋势展开之前，市场通常都会回调去测试旧趋势的极值。举例来说，假设有一段空头趋势，而此前那次回调强到向上突破了空头趋势线，现在市场正从一个测试空头趋势底部的更低的低点处反转向上。这可能是一次转折为多头趋势的趋势反转。如果上涨的第一段是一段强劲的急速行情，那么你就会相信，反转的概率现在更大了。这第一段强劲上涨之后的回调，通常会导致一个更高的低点，但它也可能造成一个与空头低点形成的双底，甚至一个更低的低点。你怎么会一边相信趋势已经反转向上、进入多头趋势，一边又看到市场跌到一个更低的低点？更低的低点是空头趋势的标志之一，它永远不可能成为多头趋势的一部分。是的，这是传统看法；但如果你采用更宽泛的定义，作为交易者你会赚到更多钱。如果市场跌破先前的空头低点，你可能会被自己的止损扫出多头仓位，但你可能仍然相信多头才真正掌控着市场。那根向上的急速行情是对旧空头趋势的突破，把市场转换成了一轮多头趋势。突破之后的回调是否跌破空头的低点，这并不重要。假设市场正好停在旧低点处、而没有再低1个最小报价单位，你真的认为那有很大关系吗？有时确实有关系，但通常够接近就算数。如果两件事很相似，它们的行为就会相同。同样不重要的是：你把多头急速行情的底部、还是把回调到更低低点的那次回调视为多头趋势的起点。严格来说，那根急速行情是反转的第一次尝试，而当市场跌破它的底部时，它就失败了。然而，它仍然是一次表明多头夺取了市场控制权的突破；至于回调是否跌到一个更低的低点、空头是否短暂地重新夺回控制权，真的并不重要。重要的是多头掌握着控制权，而且很可能在接下来许多根K线里都是如此；所以你需要寻找的是可以买入的回调，哪怕是这第一次回调到更低低点的回调。


> Once you believe that the market has reversed, it usually will pull back to test the prior trend's extreme before the new trend unfolds. For example, assume that there is a bear trend and that the prior pullback was strong enough to break above the bear trend line and now the market is reversing up from a lower low test of the bear trend's bottom. This is a possible trend reversal into a bull trend. If that first leg up is in the form of a strong spike, you then believe that the odds of a reversal are now even greater. The pullback from that first strong leg up will usually result in a higher low, but it can also result in a double bottom with the bear's low or even a lower low. How can it be that you believe that the trend has reversed up into a bull trend, yet the market has now fallen to a lower low? A lower low is one of the hallmarks of a bear trend, and it can never be a part of a bull trend. Yes, that is the conventional wisdom, but you stand to make more money as a trader if you use broader definitions. You might stop yourself out of your long if the market falls below the old bear low, but you might still believe that the bulls really control the market. That spike up was a breakout of the old bear trend and converted the market into a bull trend. It does not matter if the pullback from the breakout falls below the bear low. Suppose the market stopped exactly at the old low instead of going one tick lower. Do you really think that is of major importance? Sometimes it is but usually close is close enough. If two things are similar, they will behave the same. It also does not matter if you consider the bottom of the bull spike or the pullback to the lower low as the start of the bull trend. Strictly speaking, the spike was the first attempt at a reversal and it failed once the market fell below the bottom of the spike. However, it was still the breakout that showed that the bulls took control over the market, and it really does not matter that the pullback fell to a lower low and that the bears briefly regained control. All that matters is that the bulls are in control and will likely be so for many bars, so you need to be looking to buy pullbacks, even that first pullback to the lower low.


在多头趋势中回调到更低的低点、或在空头趋势中回调到更高的高点，这在每张图上发生的小段行情中都很常见。举例来说，假设有一段空头趋势，随后出现一段紧凑的通道式上涨行情、涨向均线，持续大约八根K线。由于这段通道很紧凑，它很强，这意味着第一次空头突破很可能失败，尽管它是顺着趋势方向的。交易者通常要等一次向上的回调出现，才去考虑做空。不过，这次回调往往表现为一个更高的高点，从而在空头趋势中形成一个 ABC 回调。他们会在前一根K线的低点下方做空，确信在强空头趋势中、均线处的低2做空是一笔绝佳交易。很多交易者不会把这种 ABC 想成一次空头突破（B 段是跌破构成 A 段的那条通道之后形成的突破）、随后再突破回调到一个更高的高点（C 段），但如果你仔细想想，它实际上就是这样。


> Pullbacks to lower lows in bull trends or higher highs in bear trends are common in the small legs that take place on every chart. For example, assume that there is a bear trend and then there is a tight channel rally to the moving average that lasts about eight bars. Since the channel is tight, it is strong and this means that the first bear breakout will likely fail, even though it is in the direction of the trend. Traders usually wait for a pullback back up before looking to short. However, that pullback will often be in the form of a higher high, creating an ABC pullback in the bear trend. They will short below the low of the prior bar, confident that a low 2 short at the moving average is a great trade in a strong bear trend. Many traders do not think of this ABC as a bear breakout (the B leg is the breakout below the channel that constitutes the A leg) and then a breakout pullback to a higher high (the C leg), but that is what it actually is, if you think about it.


有一种特殊的更高的高点或更低低点回调，在主要趋势反转中很常见，主要趋势反转在第3册中讨论。举例来说，如果一段多头趋势出现一波强劲下跌、跌破多头趋势线，随后又出现一轮弱势上涨行情（比如一个楔形）创出新高，这个更高的高点有时就是一段新空头趋势的起点。如果趋势随后反转向下、进入空头趋势，那么这轮走向更高的高点的弱势上涨行情，就只是那根跌破多头趋势线的空头急速行情之后的回调。那根空头急速行情才是空头趋势真正的起点，尽管它之后的回调一路涨到那根空头急速行情的顶部之上、在多头趋势中创出了新高。当空头趋势已经走了20根或更多K线之后，大多数交易者回头看时，会把那个更高的高点看作空头趋势的起点，这是一个合理的结论。不过，在趋势形成的当时，敏锐的交易者一直在想市场是否已经反转成空头趋势，而他们并不在乎那根空头急速行情之后的上涨行情是以一个更低的高点、一个双顶，还是一个更高的高点去测试多头的高点。从严格的技术角度看，趋势是在空头于那根急速行情中夺取市场控制权时开始的，而不是在测试多头高点时开始的。这次趋势反转的确认，出现在市场从那个更高的高点强劲抛售之后。尽管那个更高的高点实际上只是那根空头急速行情之后的回调，你把这两个高点中的哪一个看作空头趋势的起点都无所谓，因为你会用同样的方式交易市场，并且会在那个更高的高点下方寻找做空机会。空头趋势在一轮强劲的上涨行情突破空头趋势线之后从一个更低的低点反转为多头趋势时，情况也是如此。多头是在那根向上突破多头趋势线的急速行情中夺取市场控制权的〔译注：此处原文写作“多头趋势线”，但按本段上一句与走势逻辑，应为“空头趋势线”；译文照原文直译，未作改动。〕，但大多数交易者会说，新的多头趋势是从那个更低的低点开始的。然而，那个更低的低点只是那根强劲多头急速行情之后的回调。


> There is a special type of higher high or lower low pullback that is common in major trend reversals, which are discussed in book 3. For example, if there is a bull trend that has a strong move down below the bull trend line, and then a weak rally (for example, a wedge) to a new high, this higher high is sometimes the start of a new bear trend. If the trend then reverses down into a bear trend, this weak rally to the higher high is simply a pullback from the bear spike that broke the bull trend line. That bear spike was the actual start of the bear trend, even though the pullback from the spike rallied to above the top of the bear spike and created a new high in the bull trend. After the bear trend has gone on for 20 or more bars, most traders will look back at the higher high and see it as the start of the bear trend, and that is a reasonable conclusion. However, as the trend was forming, astute traders were wondering if the market had reversed into a bear trend, and they did not care if the rally up from the bear spike tested the bull high as a lower high, a double top, or a higher high. From a strictly technical perspective, the trend began once the bears took control of the market during the bear spike and not with the test of the bull high. The confirmation of the trend reversal came once the market sold off strongly from the higher high. Although the higher high is actually simply a pullback from the bear spike, it does not matter which of the two highs you think is the start of the bear trend, because you would trade the market the same way and look to short below the higher high. The same is true when a bear trend reverses into a bull trend from a lower low after a strong rally breaks above the bear trend line. The bulls took control of the market on the spike that broke above the bull trend line, but most traders would say that the new bull began with the lower low. However, that lower low was simply a pullback from the strong bull spike.


任何在极少数几根K线里就走完很多点数的趋势——也就是说，它由一些大K线、以及彼此重叠极少的K线组合而成——最终都会有回调。这类趋势动能极强，因此概率偏向回调之后趋势恢复，随后去测试趋势的极值。通常这个极值还会被越过，只要这次回调没有变成一轮方向相反的新趋势、并且没有延伸到原趋势起点之外。一般来说，如果回调回撤了75% 或更多，那么回调能够回到此前趋势极值的概率会大幅下降。对空头趋势中的回调而言，到了那个时候，交易者最好把这个回调看作一轮新的多头趋势，而不是旧空头趋势中的一次回调。


> Any trend that covers a lot of points in very few bars, meaning that there is some combination of large bars and bars that overlap each other only minimally, will eventually have a pullback. These trends have such strong momentum that the odds favor resumption of the trend after the pullback and then a test of the trend's extreme. Usually the extreme will be exceeded, as long as the pullback does not turn into a new trend in the opposite direction and extend beyond the start of the original trend. In general, the odds that a pullback will get back to the prior trend's extreme fall substantially if the pullback retraces 75 percent or more. For a pullback in a bear trend, at that point, a trader is better off thinking of the pullback as a new bull trend rather than a pullback in an old bear trend.


等回调最让人沮丧的一点是：有时它好像永远都不会来。举例来说，在一轮上涨行情中，你现在确信聪明做法是买入一次回调，可市场却一根K线接着一根K线地上涨，直到涨得太远、以至于你现在觉得它可能干脆反转、而不是回调。这是为什么？每一轮多头趋势都是由使用各种你能想到的算法的买入程序制造出来的；当许多公司都在朝同一方向运行程序时，强趋势就会出现。一旦你确信多头趋势很强，别人也一样确信。有经验的交易者明白正在发生什么，他们意识到任何回调几乎肯定都会被买入，而且后面还会跟着一个新的高点。正因如此，他们不去等回调，而是做着和机构完全一样的事。他们以市价买入，也在面前这张图上根本看不出来的微小回调中买入。也许他们是在一两个最小报价单位的回调处买入。程序会继续买入，因为概率表明趋势会一直延续到某个技术位才停。到了那里，数学期望就会偏向反转。换句话说，数学期望已经越过了中性点，现在偏向反转；正因如此，这些机构就会激进地朝反方向交易，而这轮新趋势会一直持续，直到它再次越过中性点、概率再次偏向反方向的运动。


> The most frustrating thing about waiting for a pullback is that sometimes it never seems to come. For example, when there is a rally and you are now confident that it would be smart to buy a pullback, the market goes up bar after bar and does not pull back until it has gone so far that now you think it might reverse instead of pulling back. Why is that? Every bull trend is created by buy programs that use every imaginable algorithm, and strong trends occur when many firms are running programs in the same direction. Once you are confident that the bull trend is strong, so is everyone else. Experienced traders understand what is going on, and they realize that any pullback will almost certainly be bought and it will be followed by a new high. Because of that, instead of waiting for a pullback, they are doing just what the institutions are doing. They are buying at the market and on tiny pullbacks that are not evident on the chart in front of them. Maybe they are buying on a one-or two-tick pullback. The programs will keep buying because the probability is that a trend will continue until it reaches some technical level. At that point, the math will favor a reversal. In other words, the math overshot neutrality and now favors a reversal, and because it does, the firms will aggressively trade in the opposite direction and the new trend will continue until once again it overshoots neutrality and the odds again favor a move in the opposite direction.


举例来说，如果苹果（AAPL）上涨了 $4.00、报 $280，并且在5分钟图上已经连续上涨了七根K线，那么它很可能会继续涨第8根K线，甚至更多。交易者愿意在 $280买入，是因为他们理解等距运动方向概率背后的逻辑。由于他们确信市场不久之后某个时点会比现在更高，而且他们没有把握市场不久之后会更低，所以他们以市价买入，也在小幅下跌时买入。尽管他们可能不会用方向概率来思考，但所有趋势交易都建立在它之上。当苹果强势上涨时，他们宁愿在 $280买入，因为他们相信市场会先涨到 $281，然后才回落到 $279。他们很可能还相信，市场会先涨到 $282，也许还有 $283，然后才回落1美元。他们可能不会用数学来思考这件事，而且精确的概率从来不是确定的；但在这种情况下，苹果很可能有大约70% 的概率先再涨两到三美元，然后才回调1美元。这意味着，如果你把这笔交易做10次，你会在7次里赚到2美元、合计盈利 $14，在3次里亏掉1美元。你的净利润是 $11，也就是每笔交易超过1美元。


> For example, if AAPL is up $4.00 at $280 and it has gone up for seven straight bars on the 5 minute chart, it will probably go up for the eighth bar and even more. Traders are willing to buy at $280 because they understand the logic of the directional probability of an equidistant move. Since they are confident that at some point soon the market will be higher than it is right now and they are not confident that it will be lower soon, they buy at the market and on small dips. Although they may not think in terms of directional probability, all trend trading is based on it. When AAPL is trending up strongly, they would rather buy at $280 because they believe that the market will reach $281 before it falls back to $279. They also likely believe that it will reach $282 and maybe $283 before it falls back one dollar. They may not think of this in terms of math and the exact probability is never certain, but in this situation, there is probably about a 70 percent chance that AAPL will go two or three dollars higher before it pulls back one dollar. That means that if you take this trade 10 times, you will make two dollars in seven cases for $14 profit and you will lose one dollar three times. Your net profit is $11, or more than a dollar per trade.


相反，如果他们等着那 $1.00的回落，这个回落可能要等到苹果涨到 $283才出现。那时他们可以在 $282买入，但这比他们早点直接以市价买入所能拿到的价格差了2美元。


> If instead they wait for the $1.00 pullback, it might not come until AAPL is at $283. They then could buy it at $282, but that is two dollars worse than what they could have paid earlier if they just bought at the market.


如果他们在 $280买入之后，苹果跌到了 $279，很多交易者会加仓买入，因为他们相信：市场上涨创出新高、让他们能把第一笔多头仓位保本平掉、并从更低的那笔入场中赚到1美元的概率，很可能高于70%。


> If after they bought at $280, AAPL fell to $279, many traders would buy more because they believe that the odds are probably better than 70 percent that it would rally to a new high and they could get out of their first long at breakeven and have a dollar profit on their lower entry.


这对那些等着在回调中入场的交易者很重要。当趋势很强时，以市价入场往往比等一次回调更好。


> This is important for traders who are waiting to enter on pullbacks. When the trend is strong, it is often better to enter at the market than to wait for a pullback.


![图 PIII.1](figures/fig-PIII-1.jpg)


**图 PIII.1　回调始于反转**


所有回调都始于一次反转，而这次反转往往强到让交易者在顺势信号终于出现时却不敢进场。在图 PIII.1中，左边那张图显示了均线处第10根K线低2做空建仓形态形成时5分钟图的样子，右边那张图显示的是整整一天。第7根K线是一根强势多头反转K线，它后面跟着一次强势的两根K线反转，并在第9根K线处形成一个更高的低点。不过，市场已经20多根K线没有触及均线，所以空头趋势很强，空头很可能会在涨到均线的两段式上涨行情中寻找做空机会，尤其是在出现一根空头信号K线时。当这个完美的建仓形态终于形成时，很多新手太专注于第7根和第9根K线，以至于忽略了它们之前的那段空头趋势，也忽略了这样一个事实：在均线处、并且有空头信号K线的情况下，低2做空是一个可靠的做空建仓形态。这轮上涨行情是多头止盈和做多剥头皮交易者共同制造的，而双方都打算在这次涨向均线附近的两段式回调中、趁强势卖出。多头止盈，空头重新建立自己的空头仓位。任何事都不会有100% 的确定性；但在空头趋势中、均线处、且带有空头信号K线时的低2，通常至少有60% 的概率能让那些在第10根K线下方1个最小报价单位处挂止损的空头做成一笔成功的做空。在这个具体案例中，信号K线只有三个最小报价单位高，所以空头为回测空头低点所承担的风险是五个最小报价单位，而那个空头低点大约低两个点。很多空头在均线下方1个最小报价单位处挂限价单，做空了这第一次回撤到均线的行情。另一些空头把它看作第一轮两段式空头上涨行情，因而预期它会失败。当他们看到第9根K线的多头反转时，就把做空的限价单挂在第8根K线高点处及其上方，并在涨到第10根K线的这段上涨行情中成交。他们预期任何反转都只是熊旗的起点，并认为任何向上突破都是在更高价格重新建立空头仓位的短暂机会；他们激进地抓住了这个机会，压倒了那些买入第8根K线上方突破的多头。


> All pullbacks begin with a reversal, and it is often strong enough so that traders are too afraid to take the with-trend signal when it finally develops. In Figure PIII.1, the chart on the left shows what the 5 minute chart looked like at the time of the bar 10 low 2 sell setup at the moving average, and the chart on the right shows the entire day. Bar 7 was a strong bull reversal bar, and it was followed by a strong two-bar reversal and higher low at bar 9. However, the market had not touched the moving average in more than 20 bars, so the bear trend was strong and the bears were likely going to look to short a two-legged rally to the moving average, especially if there was a bear signal bar. When the perfect setup finally formed, many beginners were so focused on bars 7 and 9 that they ignored the bear trend that preceded them, and the reality that a low 2 short at the moving average where there is a bear signal bar is a reliable sell setup. The rally was created by profit-taking bears and scalping longs, and both planned to sell into strength on a two-legged pullback to around the moving average. The longs took profits and the bears reestablished their shorts. Nothing is ever going to be 100 percent certain, but a low 2 at the moving average in a bear trend where there is a bear signal bar is usually at least 60 percent likely to be a successful short for bears who shorted on a stop at one tick below bar 10. In this particular case, the signal bar was only three ticks tall, so a bear would have been risking five ticks for a test of the bear low, which was about two points lower. Many bears shorted this first pullback to the moving average with a limit order located one tick below the moving average. Other bears saw this as the first two-legged bear rally, and therefore expected it to fail. When they saw the bar 9 bull reversal, they placed limit orders to short at or above the bar 8 high and were filled on the rally to bar 10. They expected any reversal to be the start of a bear flag and thought that any breakout to the upside would be a brief opportunity to reestablish shorts at a higher price; they aggressively seized that opportunity, overwhelming bulls who bought the breakout above bar 8.


第10根K线的低2熊旗以一根强劲的空头趋势K线完成突破，但后面跟着一根带多头实体的K线。这是想让这次突破失败的一次尝试。多头希望市场形成一个失败的低2、随后出现一波上涨行情，并把始终入场方向翻转为做多。不过，交易者知道大多数反转尝试都会失败，于是很多人在这根K线多头收盘时做空，并把做空的限价单挂在其高点上方。由于空头并不知道市场是否会走到这根多头K线的高点之上，如果他们既希望在这根K线处或上方做空，又想保证即使上方那些限价单没有成交也能做上空，那么很多人还会在它低点下方1个最小报价单位处挂止损单。如果他们在该K线高点处的限价单成交了，很多人就会撤销自己的止损入场单。如果限价单没成交，这根K线下方的止损单就能确保他们做上空。大多数人早已在低2突破时做空，但有些人会在市场朝自己方向走时加仓。在计算机程序化交易中尤其如此：市场持续下跌时，许多程序会继续做空。


> The bar 10 low 2 bear flag broke out with a strong bear trend bar, but was followed by a bar with a bull body. This was an attempt to have the breakout fail. The bulls wanted the market to form a failed low 2 and then a rally, and flip to always-in long. However, traders know that most reversal attempts fail, and many shorted the bull close and had limit orders to short above its high. Because the bears did not know whether the market would trade above the high of this bull bar, if they were hoping to short at or above the bar but wanted to guarantee getting short even if their limit orders up there did not get filled, many also placed stop orders at one tick below its low. If their limit orders at the high of the bar were filled, many would have canceled their stop entry orders. If their limit orders were not filled, the stop below the bar would have ensured that they got short. Most would have already shorted the low 2 breakout, but some would have added on as the market went their way. This is particularly true of computerized program trading where many programs continue to short as the market continues to fall.


顺便说一句，交易反转时有一条最重要的规则：在市场第二次尝试恢复趋势时离场。在这个案例中，指望第7根K线是一个持久底部为时过早。一旦市场在均线处形成低2，尤其是在第10根信号K线带空头实体的情况下，所有多头都必须离场。很少有人有能力反手做空；那些没有这个能力的人，平掉了自己小小的多头剥头皮仓位，错过了一笔大空头交易。在空头趋势中，耐心等待一次涨到均线的上涨行情再做空，要远好过做一笔多头剥头皮。


> Incidentally, one of the cardinal rules about trading reversals is to exit on the market's second attempt to resume the trend. In this case, it was premature to expect bar 7 to be a lasting bottom. Once the market formed a low 2 at the moving average, and especially with the bar 10 signal bar having a bear body, all the longs must exit. Very few had the ability to reverse to short, and those who did not have that ability exited their small long scalps and missed a big short trade. It is far better to wait patiently to short a rally to the moving average in a bear trend than it is to scalp a long.


一旦多头趋势明确，交易者就预期第一次两段式回调会失败。当他们看到第21根K线之后那根多头趋势K线时，就把买入限价单挂在第21根K线的低点处，因为他们预期跌破第21根K线的突破会失败。那将是强多头趋势中的第一次两段式下跌，而强趋势中大多数“第一次”都会失败。他们还相信均线会成为支撑、那里会有激进的买盘。随着市场跌到均线，他们的买入限价单成交了。另一些多头在第23根K线高点上方挂买入止损单入场，因为那是一个多头趋势中的高2买入建仓形态、并在均线处有一根多头信号K线，这是非常强的买入建仓形态。


> Once the bull trend was clear, traders expected the first two-legged pullback to fail. When they saw the bull trend bar after bar 21, they placed buy limit orders at the bar 21 low, since they expected that the breakout below bar 21 would fail. It would have been the first two-legged move down in a strong bull trend, and most firsts against a strong trend fail. They also believed that the moving average would be support and that there would be aggressive buyers there. Their buy limit orders were filled as the market fell to the moving average. Other bulls entered on a buy stop above the bar 23 high, since it was a high 2 buy setup in a bull trend with a bull signal bar at the moving average, which is a very strong buy setup.


第24根空头反转K线带有一条下影线，强度略弱于从第20根K线到第23根K线之前那根K线这段空头微型通道的多头突破。那根突破K线是一根大多头趋势K线，并且前面跟着两根多头K线。有些交易者在第24根K线下方做空，预期多头突破会失败。另一些人则等着看接下来一两根K线长什么样。那根做空入场K线是一根强的空头K线，但守在多头突破K线的低点之上，所以市场还没有翻转为始终做空。下一根K线带多头实体，因此没有确认卖盘。多头在其高点上方买入，认为这是一个合理的突破回调买入建仓形态——它出现在多头趋势中的均线处，或者说出现在一个正在形成的交易区间中的多头行情段里。


> The bar 24 bear reversal bar had a tail on the bottom and was slightly less strong than the bull breakout of the bear micro channel from bar 20 to the bar before bar 23. The breakout bar was a large bull trend bar, and it followed two bull bars. Some traders shorted below bar 24, expecting the bull breakout to fail. Others waited to see what the next couple of bars would look like. The short entry bar was a strong bear bar but held above the low of the bull breakout bar, so the market did not yet flip to always in short. The next bar had a bull body, and therefore did not confirm the selling. Bulls bought above its high, believing that it was a reasonable breakout pullback buy setup at the moving average in a bull trend, or in a bull leg in a developing trading range.


![图 PIII.2](figures/fig-PIII-2.jpg)


**图 PIII.2　每一次回调都始于一次反转**
