This gives them a casino advantage. If a casino has only one customer, and he bets a billion dollars on a single bet, the casino has a 47 percent chance of going out of business on that bet. However, with a huge number of bets of ordinary sizes, the math greatly favors that their edge will result in a consistent profit. The same is true for a HFT firm. Since many are trying to make just a tick or two on each trade, their reward is tiny and their risk is relatively large on each trade, but the reliability of their success is high. Most of them probably have a 90 percent chance or better of making a profit every day, which means that their probability of success is high. The edge that day traders can have is an exceptional ability to read charts, resulting in a high winning percentage, which can be 70 percent or more. When combined with a profit target that is at least as large as the risk, they can make a very high return on their equity. Most of the very best traders in the world are discretionary traders, using subjective evaluations to make their decisions. Why would a superstar continue to work at Goldman Sachs, sharing his rewards, when he can go out on his own and open a hedge fund or trade for himself? Very few would, and that is why the world's greatest traders go out on their own, and it is also the great lure for all of us. There are countless examples on Wall Street of well-known traders earning billions of dollars a year from discretionary trading. Some hold positions for months or years at a time, like Warren Buffett, whereas others are day traders, like Paul Rotter, the “Eurex flipper.” Day traders have many options in the trade-offs among risk, reward, and probability, and some are willing to accept a lower probability of success, say 40 percent, in exchange for a reward that is three or more times the risk.


下面是一些交易者拥有优势的情形示例：成功概率70%或更好（仅仅为了打平，回报也必须至少是风险的一半）：


> Here are some examples of situations where a trader has an edge: Probability of success of 70 percent or better (reward has to be at least half as big as risk just to break even):


- 剥头皮，但既然大多数交易者无法持续挑出成功概率70%的交易，他们只在回报至少与风险一样大时才应该做剥头皮。举例来说，如果你认为在 Emini 中需要两个点的止损，那就只有在至少两个点的回报是合理的时候才做这笔交易。


> • Scalps, but since most traders cannot consistently pick trades with a 70 percent chance of success, they should trade a scalp only if the reward is at least as large as the risk. For example, if you believe that a two-point stop is needed in the Emini, take the trade only if at least a two-point reward is reasonable.


成功概率60%或更好（为了打平，回报至少要与风险一样大）：


> Probability of success of 60 percent or better (reward has to be at least as big as risk to break even):


- 在多头趋势中买入回调到移动平均线的高2。
- 在空头趋势中卖出回调到移动平均线的低2。
- 在多头趋势中买入楔形牛旗的回调。
- 在空头趋势中卖出楔形熊旗的回调。
- 在多头趋势中，买入牛旗突破之后的突破回调。
- 在空头趋势中，卖出熊旗突破之后的突破回调。
- 在多头趋势中买入强劲多头急速行情中的高1回调，但不要在买入高潮之后买入。
- 在空头趋势中卖出强劲空头急速行情中的低1回调，但不要在卖出高潮之后卖出。
- 在交易区间顶部做空，尤其是二次入场时。
- 在交易区间底部做多，尤其是二次入场时。
- 趋势反转：


> • Buying a high 2 pullback to the moving average in a bull trend. • Selling a low 2 pullback to the moving average in a bear trend. • Buying a wedge bull flag pullback in a bull trend. • Selling a wedge bear flag pullback in a bear trend. • Buying a breakout pullback from a breakout of a bull flag in a bull trend. • Selling a breakout pullback from a breakout of a bear flag in a bear trend. • Buying a high 1 pullback in a strong bull spike in a bull trend, but not after a buy climax. • Selling a low 1 pullback in a strong bear spike in a bear trend, but not after a sell climax. • Shorting at the top of a trading range, especially if it is a second entry. • Buying at the bottom of a trading range, especially if it is a second entry. • Trend reversals:


- 趋势线被强势突破之后，在趋势极值被测试之后、且出现一根好的反转信号K线时，寻找反转。交易者在底部想买更高的低点或更低的低点，在顶部想做空更高的高点或更低的高点。
- 强势的末端旗形反转。
- 在空头楼梯形态中买入第三次或第四次向下推进，去测试前一次向下推进的低点。
- 在多头楼梯形态中卖出第三次或第四次向上推进，去测试前一次向上推进的高点。
- 用限价单入场；这需要更多的读图经验，因为交易者是在一个正朝交易反方向运行的市场里入场。不过，经验丰富的交易者可以在下列这些建仓形态上可靠地使用限价单或市价单：


> • After a strong break of the trend line, look for a reversal after a test of the trend's extreme where there is a good reversal signal bar. Traders are looking to buy a higher low or a lower low at a bottom, or to short a higher high or a lower high at a top. • Strong final flag reversal. • Buying a third or fourth push down in a bear stairs pattern for a test of the low of the prior push down. • Selling a third or fourth push up in a bull stairs pattern for a test of the high of the prior push up. • Entering using limit orders; this requires more experience reading charts, because the trader is entering in a market that is going in the opposite direction to the trade. However, experienced traders can reliably use limit or market orders with these setups:


- 在强劲多头突破中买入多头急速行情，用市价单或在K线收盘时买，或用限价单在前一根K线低点处或下方买（在急速行情中入场需要更宽的止损，而急速行情发生得很快，所以这个组合对许多交易者来说很难）。
- 在强劲空头突破中卖出空头急速行情，用市价单或在K线收盘时卖，或用限价单在前一根K线高点处或上方卖（在急速行情中入场需要更宽的止损，而急速行情发生得很快，所以这个组合对许多交易者来说很难）。
- 在等距运动附近买入空头突破，前提是这次突破不太强——例如，如果 Emini 中的区间大约有四个点高，就在区间下方四个点处用限价单买入，冒四个点的风险，预期市场会去测试突破点。只有经验非常丰富的交易者才应该考虑这样做。
- 在等距运动附近卖出多头突破，前提是这次突破不太强——例如，如果 Emini 中的区间大约有四个点高，就在区间上方四个点处用限价单卖出，冒四个点的风险，预期市场会去测试突破点。只有经验非常丰富的交易者才应该考虑这样做。


> • Buying a bull spike in a strong bull breakout at the market or at the close of the bar, or on a limit order at or below the low of the prior bar (entering in spikes requires a wider stop and the spike happens quickly, so this combination is difficult for many traders). • Selling a bear spike in a strong bear breakout at the market or at the close of the bar, or on a limit order at or above the high of the prior bar (entering in spikes requires a wider stop and the spike happens quickly, so this combination is difficult for many traders). • Buying a bear breakout at around a measured move, if the breakout is not too strong—for example, if the range is about four points tall in the Emini, buying on a limit order at four points below the range, risking four points, and expecting a test of the breakout point. Only very experienced traders should consider this. • Selling a bull breakout at around a measured move, if the breakout is not too strong—for example, if the range is about four points tall in the Emini, selling on a limit order at four points above the range, risking four points, and expecting a test of the breakout point. Only very experienced traders should consider this.


- 在可能出现的、紧随强势反转之后的新多头趋势中，或在交易区间的底部，用限价单在低1或低2弱势信号K线处或下方买入。
- 在可能出现的、紧随强势反转之后的新空头趋势中，或在交易区间的顶部，用限价单在高1或高2弱势信号K线处或上方做空。
- 在移动平均线处一个平静的牛旗中，用限价单在前一根K线处或下方买入。
- 在移动平均线处一个平静的熊旗中，用限价单在前一根K线处或上方做空。
- 在一根向上突破牛旗的多头K线下方买入，预期出现突破回调。
- 在一根向下跌破熊旗的空头K线上方卖出，预期出现突破回调。成功概率约50%（为了打平，回报至少要比风险大50%）：


> • Buying at or below a low 1 or 2 weak signal bar on a limit order in a possible new bull trend after a strong reversal or at the bottom of a trading range. • Shorting at or above a high 1 or 2 weak signal bar on a limit order in a possible new bear trend after a strong reversal or at the top of a trading range. • Buying at or below the prior bar on a limit order in a quiet bull flag at the moving average. • Shorting at or above the prior bar on a limit order in a quiet bear flag at the moving average. • Buying below a bull bar that breaks above a bull flag, anticipating a breakout pullback. • Selling above a bear bar that breaks below a bear flag, anticipating a breakout pullback. Probability of success of about 50 percent (reward has to be at least 50 percent greater than risk to break even):


- 在交易区间中分批建仓时的第一次入场。


> • The initial entry when scaling into a position in a trading range.


- 在窄幅交易区间中买入或卖出，预期一次突破能带来几倍于风险的利润。
- 当趋势可能反转向下时在交易区间中做空一个更低的高点，或者当趋势可能反转向上时买入一个更高的低点。由于入场点在交易区间的中部，概率是50%，但回报通常是风险的两倍。成功概率40%或更低（回报至少要是风险的两倍）：


> • Buying or selling in a tight trading range, expecting a breakout that would result in a profit that is several times greater than your risk. • Shorting a lower high in a trading range when the trend might be reversing down, or buying a higher low when the trend might be reversing up. Since the entry is in the middle of the trading range, the probability is 50 percent, but the reward is usually twice the risk. Probability of success of 40 percent or less (reward has to be at least twice the size of risk):


- 在空头趋势的底部买入，或在多头趋势的顶部做空，此时反转交易允许很小的风险和非常大的回报——例如，在上涨行情涨到明确的阻力位时做空，用限价单在阻力位下方一个最小报价单位处入场，把保护性止损放在阻力位上方一个或两个最小报价单位处。在讲限价单入场的那一章里就有好几个例子。成功概率40%到60%，视情况而定（当概率只有40%时，为了打平，回报至少要是风险的两倍）：


> • Buying at the bottom of a bear trend or shorting at the top of bull trend where the reversal trade allows for a small risk and a very large reward—for example, shorting a rally to a clear resistance level, entering on a limit order at one tick below the resistance, and having a protective stop at one or two ticks above it. There are several examples in the chapter on entering on limit orders. Probability of success of 40 percent to 60 percent, depending on circumstances (reward has to be at least twice the size of risk to break even when the probability is only 40 percent):


- 在多头趋势中，当市场下跌时用限价单买入一次突破回测；或在空头趋势中，当市场上涨时用限价单做空一次突破回测。
- 在一个新的多头趋势中，或在交易区间的底部，用限价单在低1或低2信号K线下方买入，即使那根信号K线并不弱势（这是一个潜在的更高的低点）；或者在一个新的空头趋势中，或在交易区间的顶部，用限价单在高1或高2信号K线上方做空，即使那根信号K线并不弱势（这是一个潜在的更低的高点）。举例来说，如果市场可能在多头趋势中正在完成一个楔形反转顶部，然后回调了一根K线或几根K线，那么在高1和高2信号K线上方做空，就是在你希望是新空头波段行情的地方做空。
- 对磁力位做反向操作，比如在多头趋势中一个等距运动上涨处做空，或在空头趋势中一个等距运动下跌处买入。
- 在一个已经走得过头的空头趋势中，在支撑区域，在一根异常大的空头趋势K线收盘前后买入一个卖出高潮（高潮在第三册中讨论）。
- 在一个已经走得过头的多头趋势中，在阻力区域，在一根异常大的多头趋势K线收盘前后卖出一个买入高潮。


> • Buying a breakout test in a bull trend on a limit order as the market is falling, or shorting a breakout test in a bear trend on a limit order as the market is rising. • Buying below a low 1 or 2 signal bar, even if it is not weak, on a limit order (a potential higher low) in a new bull trend or at the bottom of a trading range, or shorting above a high 1 or 2 signal bar, even if it is not weak, on a limit order (a potential lower high) in a new bear trend or at the top of a trading range. For example, if the market might be completing a wedge reversal top in a bull trend and pulls back for a bar or a few bars, shorting above the high 1 and high 2 signal bars is shorting in what you hope is a new bear swing. • Fading magnets, like shorting at a measured move up in a bull trend or buying at a measured move down in a bear trend. • Buying a sell climax around the close of an unusually large bear trend bar in an area of support in an overdone bear trend (climaxes are discussed in book 3). • Selling a buy climax around the close of an unusually large bull trend bar in an area of resistance in an overdone bull trend.


初学交易者很快就会明白，趋势看起来是极好的赚钱方式。然而，他们很快就会发现，趋势交易其实和其他任何类型的交易一样难。他们想赚钱，就得有人亏钱。市场是一个零和游戏，两边都有数不清的聪明人在玩。这就保证了交易者等式里的三个变量总会把优势压得很小、而且很难评估。一个交易者想赚钱，就必须持续比外面一半以上的交易者做得更好。既然大多数竞争对手是盈利的机构，那么交易者必须非常优秀才行。在趋势中，概率往往比初学者希望的要小，而风险更大。在交易区间中，风险不大，但概率和回报也都不大。在反转中，虽然回报可能很大，但风险往往也很大，而概率很小。在剥头皮中，概率很高，但回报相比风险很小。


> Beginning traders quickly learn that trading trends appears to be an excellent way to make money. However, they soon discover that trading trends is actually just as difficult as any other type of trading. For them to make money, someone else has to lose it. The market is a zero-sum game being played by countless smart people on both sides. This guarantees that the three variables in the trader's equation will always keep the edge small and difficult to assess. For a trader to make money, he has to be consistently better than half of the other traders out there. Since most of the competitors are profitable institutions, a trader has to be very good. In a trend, the probability is often smaller than a beginner would like, and the risk is larger. In a trading range, the risk is not great, but neither is the probability or the reward. In a reversal, although the reward can be large, the risk is often big as well and the probability is small. In a scalp, the probability is high, but the reward is small compared to the risk.


## 交易者的等式


> ### TRADER'S EQUATION


大多数交易者不会用数学的方式去想一笔交易，所有成功的交易者都在运用交易者等式，至少是下意识地在用。你常常会听到电视上的评论员在决定是否做一笔交易时谈论风险回报比。这很可惜，因为它忽略了一个同样重要的变量：概率。要做一笔交易，你必须相信交易者等式是有利的：成功概率乘以回报，必须大于失败概率乘以风险。当一个评论员说某笔交易的风险回报比不错时，他其实只是说，如果你正确地管理这笔交易，它有一种优势、也就是一种数学上的有利条件。他的推荐里隐含的意思是这笔交易“大概率”会成，也就是他相信你有超过50%的机会赚到钱。虽然他们不会这样评价自己的说法，但如果他们是成功的交易者，他们就一定是这样想的，因为不考虑全部三个变量，就不可能成功。


> THE TRADER'S EQUATION Even though most traders don't think about a trade in mathematical terms, all successful traders use the trader's equation, at least subconsciously. You will often hear pundits on television talk about the risk/reward ratio when they are deciding whether to take a trade. This is unfortunate because it overlooks an equally important variable, probability. To take a trade, you must believe that the trader's equation is favorable: the probability of success times the reward has to be greater than the probability of failure times the risk. When a pundit says that a trade has a good risk/reward ratio, he simply means that it has an edge or a mathematical advantage, if you manage your trade correctly. Implicit in his recommendation is that the trade will “probably” work, meaning that he believes that there is better than a 50 percent chance that you will make a profit. Although they don't think of their comments this way, this is what they must believe if they are successful traders, because there is no way to be successful without considering all three variables.


任何一笔交易，回报和风险都是由你自己设定的，因为潜在回报就是到你的止盈目标的距离，风险就是到你的止损的距离。这个等式难就难在给概率赋值，而概率永远无法被确定地知道。


> With any trade, you set the reward and risk because the potential reward is the distance to your profit target and the risk is the distance to your stop. The difficulty in solving the equation is assigning a value to the probability, which can never be known with certainty.


一般来说，如果你拿不准，就假设你赢或输的概率是50%；如果你有信心信号看起来不错，就假设你赢的概率是60%、输的概率是40%。根本不用去担心行情可能走多远。只评估这个建仓形态看起来好不好，如果好，就假设任何幅度的上涨相比同样幅度的下跌，概率都有60%或更好。这就是等距运动的概率，也可以称为方向概率（directional probability）；本章后面会讨论。如果潜在回报是风险的许多倍，许多交易者也会考虑做一笔不太可能成功的交易。在这种时候，他们应该假设概率是40%。如果成功概率比这还低得多，那么无论潜在回报有多大，愿意考虑这笔交易的交易者都会极少。


> In general, if you are uncertain, assume that you have a 50 percent of winning or losing, and if you are confident that the signal looks good, assume that you have a 60 percent chance of winning and a 40 percent chance of losing. Don't even worry about how far the move might go. Simply evaluate whether the setup looks good, and if it does, assume that the probability of a move up of any size has a 60 percent chance or better compared to a move down of the same size. This is the probability (or directional probability) of an equidistant move and is discussed later in this chapter. If the potential reward is many times larger than the risk, many traders will also consider taking a trade that is unlikely to be successful. When that is the case, they should assume that the probability is 40 percent. If the probability of success is much less than that, very few traders would ever consider taking the trade, no matter how great the potential reward is.


理解这些概率的含义很重要。否则，初学者很容易在市场做出他以为不可能、甚至绝不会发生的事情时变得心烦意乱。不管你多有信心，市场经常会做出与你坚信的应该发生的事恰好相反的事。如果你有60%的把握市场会上涨，那就意味着在40%的情况下它反而会下跌，而你做了这笔交易就会亏钱。你不应该忽略那40%，就像你不会忽略30码外一个朝你开枪、但有40%的概率打中你的人一样。40%是非常真实、非常危险的，所以要永远尊重那些与你看法相反的交易者。


> It is important to understand the implications of these probabilities. Otherwise, it is easy for a beginning trader to become upset when the market does something that he thinks is improbable, or even impossible. No matter how confident you feel, the market will often do the exact opposite of what you believe that it should. If you are 60 percent confident that the market will go up, that means that in 40 percent of the cases it will instead go down, and you will lose if you take the trade. You should not ignore that 40 percent any more than you would dismiss someone 30 yards away who is shooting at you, but who has only a 40 percent chance of hitting you. Forty percent is very real and dangerous, so always respect the traders who believe the opposite of you.


如果你因为觉得概率只有50%而不做一笔交易，只在认为概率有60%时才做交易，那么在一半的情况下你会错过一笔好交易。这只是交易的一部分，是在一个有着海量聪明人、其中一半人坚信另一半人恰好相反想法的零和游戏中，优势必然很小所带来的结果。永远不要因为市场做出任何事而心烦或困惑。只要接受任何事都有可能发生，即使你不明白为什么会发生。从来没有人真正明白为什么，而原因从不重要。你靠数学赚钱，不靠原因，所以如果一个交易者只在交易者等式明显有利时才做交易，这个交易者就处在可以持续赚钱的有利位置。


> If you don't take a trade because you think that the probability is only 50 percent and you only take trades where you think the probability is 60 percent, then in half of the cases you will miss a good trade. This is just part of trading and a consequence of the edges being as small as they have to be in a zero-sum game with a huge number of very smart people, where half of them believe the exact opposite of the other half. Never get upset or confused by the market doing anything. Simply accept that anything is possible, even if you do not understand why it is happening. No one ever really understands why, and the reason is never important. You make money from math, not from reasons, so if someone takes trades only when the trader's equation is strongly favorable, that trader is in a good position to consistently make money.


如果你想多年来一直盈利地交易，就必须待在自己的舒适区里。有些交易者喜欢回报是风险好几倍的交易，他们愿意只在30%到40%的交易上获胜。这种做法的交易者等式是有利的，但大多数交易的回报只与风险差不多大。这意味着这些交易者会选择错过每天出现的大多数交易，因为他们认为回报不够大、不足以支撑那么低的成功概率。另一些交易者只做高概率的建仓形态，愿意接受只与风险一样大的回报。然而，市场处于趋势中时，回调常常很小，而这些建仓形态的概率常常不到50%。举例来说，如果有一个带明显影线的弱势空头通道，通道底部也许会出现一个卖出信号。市场看起来更倾向于形成一个交易区间，但愿意在底部做空、寻求一段两倍或三倍于风险的波段行情的空头，会做得非常好。只想要高概率交易的交易者会坐在一旁，看着空头趋势再延续10根或20根K线，等一个高概率的反转建仓形态来做多，或者等一次回调来做空。这也是一种可以接受的交易方式。有些交易者在所有环境中都自在，会根据市场调整自己的风格。这让他们能够整天都盈利地交易，而这是每个交易者的目标。现实是，大多数优秀交易者都有一种特定的风格，然后等待与这种风格一致的建仓形态。


> You have to remain in your comfort zone if you expect to trade profitably for many years. Some traders like trades where the reward is several times greater than the risk, and they are willing to win on only 30 to 40 percent of their trades. This approach has a favorable trader's equation, but most trades have a reward that is only about as large as the risk. This means that these traders will choose to miss most trades that take place every day because they don't believe that the reward is large enough to justify the low probability of success. Other traders will only trade high probability setups, and are willing to accept a reward that is only as large as the risk. However, very often when the market is trending, the pullbacks are small and the probability of the setups is often less than 50 percent. For example, if there is a weak bear channel with prominent tails, there might be a sell signal at the bottom of the channel. The market looks like the odds favor the formation of a trading range, but bears who are willing to short at the bottom, looking for a swing that is two or three times as large as their risk, will do very well. The traders who only want high probability trades will sit and watch the bear continue for 10 or 20 bars as they wait for a high probability reversal setup to buy or pullback to short. This is also an acceptable approach to trading. Some traders are comfortable in all environments and adjust their style to the market. This allows them to trade profitably all day long, which is the goal of every trader. The reality is that most good traders have a particular style and wait for setups consistent with that style.


剥头皮交易者追求相对其承担的风险来说比较小的利润（他们应该争取至少与风险一样大的回报），并且需要很高的成功概率才能让交易者等式为正。不要以为这意味着他们只做旗形，因为许多人也会做强突破。在强突破中，止损理论上在急速行情之外，这可能非常远（例如，在由四根多头趋势K线构成的突破中，最初的止损理论上在第一根K线低点之下，尽管大多数交易者不会冒那么大的风险）。然而，由于突破很强，等距运动有60%或更好的概率。这意味着他们可以做一笔风险很高的交易，因为回报同样高，概率也高。为了让每笔交易上承担的风险金额与其他交易保持一致，他们必须交易更小的仓位。


> Scalpers seek relatively small profits compared to the risk that they incur (they should go for a reward that is at least as large as the risk), and need a high probability of success to create a positive trader's equation. Don't assume that this means that they will only trade flags, because many will also trade strong breakouts. With a strong breakout, the stop theoretically is beyond the spike, which can be far away (for example, in a four bull trend bar breakout, the initial stop is theoretically below the low of the first bar, although most traders would not risk that much). However, since the breakout is strong, there is a 60 percent chance or better of an equidistant move. This means that they can take a trade with high risk, because the reward is equally high and the probability is also high. To keep their dollars at risk the same as it is for their other trades, they have to trade smaller volume.


交易者整天做出的最重要的决定之一，就是在上一根K线的高点或低点处，多头还是空头会赢。举例来说，如果出现一根强劲的多头趋势K线，那么会不会有更多空头卖出以开立空头、更多多头卖出手中的多头并止盈，主要使用市价单和限价单，大致是在这根K线的高点和收盘价附近？还是会有更多多头开立新的多头、更多空头买回他们的空头，主要使用止损单？同样，在低点处，买入更多还是卖出更多？交易者试图评估：赚到足够多的利润、以抵消自己在交易中必须承担的风险，这件事的概率有多大。他们的目标是长期赚钱，他们知道自己会经常亏钱。然而，要在长期里盈利，他们就需要做那些交易者等式有利（为正）的交易。


> One of the most important decisions that traders make all day long is whether the bulls or the bears will win at the high or low of the prior bar. For example, if there is a strong bull trend bar, will there be more bears selling to initiate shorts, and bulls selling out of their longs and taking profits around the high and close of the bar, mostly using market and limit orders, or will there be more bulls initiating new longs and bears buying back their shorts, mostly using stop orders? Similarly, at the low, will there be more buying or more selling? Traders try to assess the probability of making enough of a profit to offset the risk that they need to assume in a trade. Their goal is to make money over time, and they know that they will often lose. However, for them to be profitable in the long run, they need to be taking trades that have favorable (positive) trader's equations.


一旦你看到一个可能的建仓形态，你要做的第一件事就是确定保护性止损必须放在多远。一旦知道了风险，你就能决定可以做多少股或多少张合约，把总风险控制在你的正常限度之内。举例来说，如果你买股票时通常冒500美元的风险，而你认为这笔交易的保护性止损需要放在入场价下方大约1.00美元处，那你可以做500股。然后你要判断这笔交易的概率是多少。如果你判断不出来，就假设它是50%。如果是50%，那么你的潜在回报至少要达到风险的两倍，这笔交易才值得做。如果你没有理由指望这笔多头能赚到2.00美元，就别做这笔交易。如果成功概率是60%，那么你的回报至少要等于风险，如果那个1.00美元的止盈目标不合理，就别做这笔交易。如果你做了这笔交易，一定要使用至少1.00美元的止盈目标，因为当风险是1.00美元、概率是60%时，这是让交易者等式为正所需要的最低值。每一笔交易都需要一个数学基础。假设在 Emini 中你必须冒两个点的风险，而你正在考虑一个做空形态。在亏掉两个点之前赚到两个点，这件事有60%的把握吗？赚到一个点的概率有70%、或者赚到四个点的概率有40%吗？如果其中任何一个的答案是肯定的，那就至少有一个最低限度的数学理由去做这笔交易。如果对所有这些答案都是否定的，那就把同样的三种可能放到做多上考虑一遍。如果三个选项里任何一个答案是肯定的，就考虑做这笔交易。如果对多头和空头来说答案都是否定的，那么用止损单入场在目前不是一个好办法，市场是不清晰的。这意味着市场处于交易区间中，经验丰富的交易者可以寻找在K线上方做空、在K线下方用限价单买入的机会。


> Once you see a possible setup, the first thing you have to do is determine how far away your protective stop has to be. Once you know your risk, you can decide on the number of shares or contracts that you can trade, keeping your total risk to within your normal limits. For example, if you normally risk $500 when you buy a stock, and you think that you would need to have your protective stop on the trade in question at about $1.00 below your entry price, then you can trade 500 shares. You then decide on what the probability of the trade is. If you cannot tell, then you assume that it is 50 percent. If it is 50 percent, then your potential reward should to be at least twice the size of your risk to make the trade worth taking. If you cannot reasonably expect to make $2.00 on that long, don't take the trade. If the chance of success is 60 percent, then your reward has to be at least equal to your risk, and if that $1.00 profit target is unreasonable, don't take the trade. If you do take the trade, make sure to use at least a $1.00 profit target, since that is the minimum that you need to have a positive trader's equation when the risk is $1.00 and the probability is 60 percent. Every trade needs a mathematical basis. Assume that you have to risk two points in the Emini and you are considering a short setup. Is it 60 percent certain that you can make two points before losing two points? Is there a 70 percent chance of making one point, or a 40 percent chance of making four points? If the answer to any of these is yes, then there is at least a minimum mathematical reason to take the trade. If the answer to all of them is no, then consider the same three possibilities for a long. If the answer is yes for any of the three choices, then consider taking the trade. If the answer is no for both the bulls and the bears, then entering on a stop is not a good approach at the moment, and the market is unclear. This means that it is in a trading range, and experienced traders can look to short above bars and buy below bars with limit orders.


交易者等式有三个变量，交易者可能因为自己的性格而更偏重其中某一个。举例来说，一个需要高胜率才能整天保持专注的交易者，会倾向于寻找这种可能的交易，因此必须愿意接受相对更小的回报和更大的风险。当概率很高时，这种不平衡很显眼，市场会很快把它中和掉。结果就是这波行情通常只持续几根K线，因此回报一般也必须很小。因为一个好的剥头皮建仓形态往往概率高、风险小，交易者在做强势剥头皮时常常会用他们最大的仓位规模。另一个极端是那些想要回报远大于风险的交易者，而为了实现这个目标，他们必须能够坦然接受只在大约40%的交易上获胜。当概率低时，交易者常常交易得更小，有些人一边等着市场朝自己方向走一边考虑加仓。因此，波段交易者的初始仓位常常比剥头皮交易者更小。还有些人可能厌恶风险，想要每笔交易的风险都最小。要做到这一点，交易者就必须接受回报更低和成功概率更低这两者的某种组合。还有另一些交易者，不论当下有什么交易机会都接受，并根据市场背景恰当地去做。当概率相对较高时，他们会更早止盈。当这笔交易最重要的特征看起来是它提供的回报时，他们接受概率会更低，也接受必须愿意把更多仓位做波段持有，才能让这个策略长期奏效。许多交易处于这些极端之间，成功概率大约50%。无论交易者做的是哪一种，他都应该总是争取回报大约为风险的两倍，以保持交易者等式为正。


> There are three variables to the trader's equation, and traders might focus on one over the other three because of their personalities. For example, a trader who needs a high winning percentage to be able to stay focused for the entire day will tend to look for trades where that is possible and would therefore have to be willing to accept relatively less reward and more risk. When the probability is high, the imbalance is conspicuous and the market will neutralize it quickly. The result is that the move usually lasts for only a few bars, and therefore the reward generally has to be small. Because the probability is often high and risk is small for a good scalp setup, traders will often trade their largest position size when taking a strong scalp. At the other extreme are traders who want their reward to be much larger than their risk, and to achieve that goal, they will have to be comfortable winning on only about 40 percent of their trades. When the probability is low, traders often trade smaller and some look to add on as the market goes their way. It is therefore common for a swing trader to take a smaller initial position than a scalp trader. Someone else might be risk averse and want a minimal risk on each trade. To get that, the trader has to accept some combination of lower reward and lower probability of success. There are other traders who take whatever trade is present and trade it appropriately, based on the context. When the probability is relatively high, they will take profits sooner. When the most important feature of the trade appears to be the reward that it offers, they accept that the probability will be less and that they have to be willing to swing more of their position to make the strategy work over time. Many trades are in between these extremes and have about a 50 percent chance of success. Whenever a trader takes one, he should always try for a reward that is about twice the size of his risk, to keep the trader's equation positive.


尽管一笔低概率交易可以拥有远大于风险的潜在回报，因而是一笔极好的交易，但对大多数交易者来说这里有一个固有的问题。因为波段交易按定义就有很大的回报，所以它们也必须要么概率相对较低、要么风险很大。一笔交易不可能既拥有很高的成功概率、又能赚到相对于风险来说很大的回报。为什么不可能？记住，必须有某个人愿意做你交易的对手方，而既然机构控制着市场，那你就必须相信有机构交易者愿意跟你对着做。如果你的成功概率是80%，那他就是20%。如果你的回报是六个点，他的风险就是六个点。如果你的风险是两个点，他的回报就是两个点。所以，如果你认为自己有80%的概率冒两个点的风险赚到六个点，那你就是在相信：有机构交易者愿意接下你交易的对面，而他们只有20%的概率冒六个点的风险只赚两个点。既然在一个巨大的市场里这几乎不可能，你就必须假设是你对这些变量的评估错了，这笔交易远没有你想的那么好。没有任何机构必须愿意做与你所做的恰好相反的事，但市场愿意——市场由所有机构组成，基本上就是一家大机构。所以必须有若干机构愿意做你所做的每一件事的反面，如果你的交易那么棒，那他们的就糟透了，而市场绝不会允许这种局面发展起来。没错，的确有许多天真的人因为误读市场而愿意做你交易的对手方，但市场被机构非常高效地控制着，它们绝不会让优势变得那么大。你应该假设，几乎每一笔成交的交易，两边下的单子都来自机构，或者来自一个在下机构本来会下的单子的个体。个体下了大量的单子，但他们无法推动市场，不管他们下单时多么无知。他们的单子只有在机构愿意下同样的单子时才能成交。举例来说，如果 Emini 在1264，而你有多头仓位、保护性卖出止损在1262，那么除非有一家机构也愿意在1262卖出，你的止损不会被打到。对几乎所有的交易来说都是如此。如果市场正在强劲上涨，为什么会有机构愿意在市场价下方卖出？因为许多机构在低得多的地方买入了，正在找理由止盈。如果它们认为市场跌到1262是部分止盈的理由，它们就会在那里卖出。如果市场打到了你的止损，那不是因为它在收割散户的止损。那是因为有机构认为在1262卖出是一个在数学上稳妥的决定。


> Even though a low-probability trade can have a potential reward that is much larger than the risk and therefore be a great trade, there is an inherent problem for most traders. Because swing trades have a large reward, by definition, they must also have either relatively low probabilities or large risks. A trade cannot exist with a high probability of making a large reward relative to the risk. Why not? Remember, there has to be someone who will take the other side of your trade, and since institutions control the market, then you have to believe that an institutional trader is willing to trade against you. If your probability of success is 80 percent, his is 20 percent. If your reward is six points, his risk is six points. If your risk is two points, his reward is two points. So if you think that you have an 80 percent chance of making six points while risking two points, then you believe that there are institutional traders willing to take the opposite side of your trade, where they have a 20 percent chance of making only two points while risking six points. Since that is virtually impossible in a huge market, you have to assume that your assessment of the variables is wrong and the trade is not nearly as good as you think. No institution has to be willing to do the exact opposite of what you are doing, but the market, which is composed of all institutions and is basically a single big institution, does. So some combination of institutions has to be willing to do the opposite of everything that you do, and if your trade is so great, then theirs is horrible, and the market would never allow it to develop. Yes, there are many naïve people who would be willing to take the other side of your trade because of their misread of the market, but the market is very efficiently controlled by institutions, and they would never let an edge get that large. You should assume that both sides of virtually every trade that takes place is being placed by an institution, or by an individual placing a trade that an institution would take if that individual did not place the trade. Individuals place lots of trades, but they cannot move the market, no matter how ignorant they are willing to be with their orders. Their orders can only get filled if an institution is willing to place the same order. For example, if the Emini is at 1264 and you are long with a protective sell stop at 1262, your stop cannot get hit unless there is an institution who is also willing to sell at 1262. This is true for virtually all trades. If the market is going up strongly, why would any institution ever be willing to sell below the market? Because many bought much lower and are looking for reasons to take profits. If they believe that the market falling to 1262 is a reason to take partial profits, they will sell there. If the market hits your stop, it is not because it was running stops on the little guys. It is because there were institutions who believed that selling at 1262 was a mathematically sound decision.


随着任何一笔交易开始朝高概率、高回报、低风险的方向发展，机构会迅速行动去利用它，使优势永远无法变得很大。同时，处在这个优势亏损一方的机构会迅速行动去加强自己的优势。市场会以一根或多根大型趋势K线的形式，朝着那个止盈目标的方向快速而大幅地运动（也就是一段急速行情），在建仓形态变强之前就大大提高了风险（所需要的止损幅度）。弱势的信号、或者低概率，使大多数波段交易难以出手。没有人会把钱送给你，交易永远都会很难。如果你看到了轻松的钱，那就是你读错了市场，很快就会发现自己把钱送给了别人。


> As any trade starts to move in the direction of having high probability, high reward, and low risk, institutions would act quickly to take advantage of it, preventing the edge from ever becoming very big. Also, the firms on the losing side of the edge would act fast to increase their edge. The market would move fast and far in the form of one or more large trend bars (a spike) in the direction of that profit target, greatly increasing the risk (the size of the required stop) before the setup became strong. The weak signal or the low probability makes most swing trades difficult to take. No one is going to give you money, and trading is always going to be difficult. If you see easy money, you are reading the market wrong and will soon find yourself giving your money to someone else.


大型市场里90%或更多的交易都是由机构完成的，这意味着市场实际上就是众多机构的集合体。几乎所有机构长期都是盈利的，少数不盈利的很快就会倒闭。既然机构是盈利的，而它们就是市场，那么你做的每一笔交易，都有一个盈利的交易者（机构集合体的一部分）在做你的对手方。除非有一家机构愿意站一边、另一家愿意站另一边，否则任何交易都无法成交。全部交易量中有70%由计算机算法产生，而个体交易者的那点小成交量不足以让程序化交易偏离它的路径。个体做的小单子，只有在一家机构愿意做同样的交易时才能成交。如果你想在某个价格买入，那么除非有一家或多家机构也想在那个价格买入，市场就不会走到那个价格。除非有一家或多家机构愿意在那里卖出，否则你无法在任何价格卖出，因为市场只能走到一个有机构愿意买、另一些机构愿意卖的价格。如果你交易200张 Emini 合约，那你就是在交易机构级别的成交量，实际上就是一家机构，你有时能够把市场推动一两个最小报价单位。然而，大多数个体交易者完全没有推动市场的能力，不管他们下单时多么无知。市场不会去收割你的止损。市场也许会测试你保护性止损所在的那个价格，但这与你的止损无关。只有当一家或多家机构认为在那个价格卖出在财务上是稳妥的、而另一些机构认为在那里买入是有利可图的，市场才会测试那个价格。在每一个最小报价单位上，都有机构在买入、另一些机构在卖出，而它们全都拥有被证明能靠下这些单子赚钱的系统。


> Ninety percent or more of all trading in large markets is done by institutions, which means that the market is effectively a collection of institutions. Almost all are profitable over time, and the few that are not soon go out of business. Since institutions are profitable and they are the market, every trade that you take has a profitable trader (a part of the collection of institutions) taking the other side of your trade. No trade can take place without one institution willing to take one side and another willing to take the other. Seventy percent of all volume is generated by computer algorithms, and the small volume from individual traders is not enough to deter the program trading from its path. The small volume trades made by individuals can only take place if an institution would be willing to take the same trade. If you want to buy at a certain price, the market will not get to that price unless one or more institutions also want to buy at that price. You cannot sell at any price unless one or more institutions are willing to sell there, because the market can only go to a price where there are institutions willing to buy and others willing to sell. If you trade 200 Emini contracts, then you are trading institutional volume and are effectively an institution, and you will sometimes be able to move the market a tick or two. Most individual traders, however, have no ability to move the market, no matter how ignorantly they are willing to trade. The market will not run your stops. The market might test the price where your protective stop is, but it has nothing to do with your stop. It will only test that price if one or more institutions believe that it is financially sound to sell there and other institutions believe that it is profitable to buy there. At every tick, there are institutions buying and other institutions selling, and all have proven systems that will make money by placing those trades.


每当一个交易者在做剥头皮，他对面的交易者很可能是个波段交易者。然而，许多波段交易者也会与别的波段交易者做对手盘。好的剥头皮交易者做不了其他好的剥头皮交易者所下交易的对手方，因为两个方向的风险和回报都差不多，而只能有一方拥有高成功概率。剥头皮交易者有很高的成功概率，所以对面的交易者成功概率就低。既然他是机构交易者，你就必须相信他的方法在长期里是稳妥、盈利的。在一个零和游戏里，如果你靠做他的反面来赚钱，这怎么可能成立？因为事情不是这样。你的入场点是反的，但你的管理方式不是。假设你在 Emini 中使用两个点的止盈目标和两个点的止损，在一个交易区间顶部一根弱势的高1买入信号K线上方做空，并且正确地相信自己有超过60%的成功概率。机构交易者在你的卖出价买入，他的风险也许也是两个点，而这正是你回报的反面（你止盈的地方就是他止损的地方），但他的回报远大于你的风险。你的保护性止损是两个点。那是你亏损买回空头的地方。然而，那不是他卖出手中的多头的地方。他的目标大概要远好几倍，所以他尽管成功概率低，也能拥有正的交易者等式。他也可能正在使用非常宽的止损并分批建仓，这两者都可能把他的概率提高到60%或更多，即使他最初入场的成功概率也许只有40%。想一想就会明白：低概率交易如果没有任何办法管理成正的交易者等式，就不可能存在，因为没有机构会做它们，它们也就永远不会被触发。它们只有在机构愿意做的时候才能被触发，而机构除非有办法盈利地交易它们，否则不会去做。机构有许多管理交易以确保交易者等式为正的方式，包括分批建仓或分批止盈、使用宽止损、对冲，以及把这笔交易做波段以取得远大于风险的回报，从而抵消低概率。


> Whenever a trader is taking a scalp, the trader on the other side is probably a swing trader. However, many swing traders will also take the opposite side from other swing traders. Good scalpers cannot not take the other side of trades placed by other good scalpers because the risk and reward are about the same for both directions, and only one can have a high probability of success. The scalper has a high probability of success, so the trader on the opposite side has a low probability of success. Since he is an institutional trader, you have to believe that his methodology is sound and profitable over time. How can that be if you are making money doing the opposite of him in a zero sum game? Because you are not. Your entry is the opposite, but your management is not. Let's say that you are using a two-point profit target and a two-point stop in the Emini and you are shorting above a weak high 1 buy signal bar at the top of a trading range, correctly believing that you have better than a 60 percent chance of success. The institutional trader is buying as you are selling and his risk might also be two points, which is the opposite of your reward (he gets stopped out where you take your profits), but his reward is far greater than your risk. Your protective stop is two points. That is where you will buy back your short for a loss. However, that is not where he will sell out of his long. His target is probably several times greater, so he can have a positive trader's equation, despite a low probability of success. He might also be using a very wide stop and scaling into his trade, both of which could increase his probability to 60 percent or more, even though the probability of success on his initial entry might be only 40 percent. If you think about it, low probability trades could not exist if there was no way to manage them to get a positive trader's equation, because no institution would ever take them and they would never trigger. They can only trigger if an institution is willing to take them, and an institution would not take them unless there was a way to trade them profitably. Institutions have many ways to manage their trades to ensure a positive trader's equation, including scaling in or out, using a wide stop, hedging, and swinging the trade for a reward that is sufficiently larger than the risk, so that they can offset the low probability.


市场活动的谱系，从极度单边，比如强趋势的急速行情阶段，到极度双边，比如一个极窄的交易区间。大多数时候它处于两者之间，单边成交较多的时期与双边成交更占主导的时期交替出现。这在交易区间中很容易看到：趋势K线代表单边成交，反转和影线代表双边成交。当市场处于多头趋势并涨到前一根K线高点之上时，它就是在突破；当它跌到前一根K线低点之下时，它就是在回调。空头趋势中则相反，突破是跌到前一根K线低点之下，回调是涨到前一根K线高点之上。当市场极度单边时，比如强趋势的急速行情阶段，回调大多是止盈造成的。举例来说，如果市场处于由五根多头趋势K线构成的强劲多头急速行情中，随后价格跌破第五根K线的低点，发生这种情况是因为在更低价位买入的多头正在卖出一部分持仓来止盈。记住，每一笔交易都必须有机构接手另一边，而只有在这是某个盈利策略的一部分时他才会接手。还有一个下跌真空，把市场吸到那根K线下方。这是所有急于开始做多或者加仓多头的多头造成的，他们一直在前几根K线的低点处及更低处挂限价单，希望以小幅折扣做多。这些多头渴望做多，但只想在更好的价格买入。如果前一根K线有六个最小报价单位高，许多这样的多头只有在比该K线高点低六个最小报价单位或更低的位置才开始买入（换句话说，在该K线的低点处或更低处）。这意味着从下方一个到五个最小报价单位之间存在相对的买方缺失，价格可以被快速吸下去寻找买家，而它会在该K线的低点附近成功找到买家。记住，正在止盈的多头卖出一部分多头持仓，他们需要买家接下他们交易的对面。一旦止盈者决定部分止盈，他们就需要愿意在一个有足够多交易者愿意买入的价格卖出。一旦市场涨得足够高，唯一愿意买的交易者就是那些等待市场跌到前一根K线下方的人。如果足够多的多头想要止盈，市场就必须跌到前一根K线下方，他们才能卖出一部分多头持仓。其他多头只有在市场跌到前一根K线下方时才会开始止盈他们的多头，所以他们会在一根K线下方一个最小报价单位处用止损单卖出。急于买入的多头会接下止盈多头的交易的对面。在那根K线低点下方做空的空头会非常少，所以这波下跌并不是想做波段空头的空头造成的。虽然有些公司也许正在通过在前一根K线下方用止损单做空来分批建仓空头，但说它会成为强劲急速行情中第一次回调里的重要因素，并不合乎逻辑。当市场极度单边时，想要做空的公司知道，它们很快就能在更高处做空，这个概率可能有80%或更高，所以现在在这里做空对它们来说并不合理。


> The spectrum of market activity is from intensely one-sided, like during the spike phase of a strong trend, to extremely two-sided, like in an extremely tight trading range. Most of the time, it is in between, with periods of more one-sided trading alternating with periods when two-sided trading is more dominant. This can easily be seen in a trading range, where trend bars represent one-side trading, and reversals and tails represent two-sided trading. When the market is in a bull trend and moves above the high of the prior bar, it is breaking out, and when it moves below the low of the prior bar, it is pulling back. The opposite is true in a bear trend, where a breakout is a move below the low of the prior bar and a pullback is a move above the high of the prior bar. When the market is extremely one-sided, like during the spike phase of a strong trend, pullbacks are mostly due to profit taking. For example, if the market is in a strong bull spike made of five bull trend bars and it then trades below the low of the fifth bar, it does so because bulls who bought lower are selling out of part of their positions to take some profits. Remember, there has to be an institution taking the other side of every trade, and he will only do so if it is part of a profitable strategy. There also is a sell vacuum that sucks the market below that bar. It is due to all of the bulls who are eager to either initiate longs or add to their longs, and they have been placing limit orders at and below the lows of the prior bars, hoping to get long at a small discount. These bulls are eager to get long, but only at a better price. If the prior bar is six ticks tall, many of these bulls will only begin buying at six ticks below the high of the bar or lower (in other words, at the low or below the bar). This means that there is a relative absence of buyers from one to five ticks down, and the price can get sucked down quickly to find buyers, which it will succeed in doing around the low of the bar. Remember, the bulls who are taking profits are selling out of part of their longs and they need buyers to take the other side of their trade. Once the profit takers decide to take partial profits, they need to be willing to sell at a price where there will be enough traders willing to buy. Once the market gets high enough, the only traders willing to buy will be those waiting for the market to fall below the prior bar. If enough bulls want to take profits, the market will have to drop below the prior bar for them to be able to exit part of their longs. Other bulls will only begin to take profits on their longs if the market moves below the prior bar, so they will sell out on a stop at one tick below the bar. The bulls who are eager to buy will take the other side of the profit taking bulls. There will be very few bears shorting below the low of that bar, so the move down is not due to bears who are looking to swing a short. Although some firms might be scaling into shorts by shorting on a stop below the prior bar, it is not logical that this would be a significant factor in the first pullback in a strong spike. When the market is extremely one-sided, firms looking to short know that the probability may be 80 percent or higher that they can soon short higher, so it does not make sense for them to short here.


因为强趋势中的小幅回调大多是止盈造成的，所以在多头趋势中第一次回调正在形成时，空头通常没有好办法通过在前一根K线低点下方做空来获利；在空头趋势中，多头也无法通过在前一根K线高点上方买入来赚钱。然而，当市场在多头趋势中突破前一根K线的高点、或者在空头趋势中跌破前一根K线的低点时，做多和做空两种交易都有一种可行的管理方式可以赚钱。如果在强劲多头趋势中，买家和卖家都无法在前一根K线高点上方赚到钱，市场就不会在那里交易，因为只有当一家机构能靠在那里买入获利、另一家能靠在那里卖出获利时，市场才能到达那里。在那里的卖出，是多头止盈与空头做空的组合，而随着市场变得越来越双边，空头做空在成交量中占的比重越来越大。如果在强劲空头趋势中，市场跌破前一根K线时买家和卖家都无法赚钱，市场就不会在那根K线下方交易。机构为什么会做一笔属于亏损策略的交易呢？它们永远不会。买入的公司和卖出的公司都不必在每一笔交易上赚钱，但每一笔交易都必须是某个盈利策略的一部分，否则它们就不会做。


> Since small pullbacks in strong trends are mostly due to profit taking, there is usually no good way for the bears to make profits by shorting below the low of the prior bar as the first pullback is forming in a strong bull trend, or for a bull to make money by buying above the high of the prior bar as the first pullback is forming in a strong bear trend. However, when the market breaks above the high of the prior bar in a bull trend or below the low of the prior bar in a bear trend, there is a profitable way to manage both a long and a short trade. If there is no way for both the buyers and the sellers to make money above the high of the prior bar in a strong bull trend, the market would not trade there, because it can only get there if one institution can make a profit by buying up there and another can make a profit by selling. The selling up there is a combination of profit taking by bulls and shorting by bears, and as the market becomes increasingly two-sided, the shorting by bears becomes a bigger part of the volume. If there is no way for both the buyers and sellers to make money when the market moves below the prior bar in a strong bear trend, the market will not trade below the bar. Why would an institution ever take a trade that is a losing strategy? They never would. Neither the buying firm nor the selling firm has to make money on every trade, but every trade has to be part of a winning strategy or else they would not take them.


如果机构是聪明的、盈利的、并且对每一个最小报价单位负责，那它们为什么会在多头趋势中买入最高的那个最小报价单位（或者在空头趋势中卖出最低的那个最小报价单位）？因为它们的算法一路涨上来都是这样做的、并且一直盈利，其中一些算法被设计成继续这样做，直到明确牛市趋势不再有效。它们在最后那笔买入上亏了，但之前在所有的交易上赚得足够多，足以抵消那笔损失。记住，它们的所有系统都有30%到70%的时候会亏，而这只是其中一次。还有一些高频交易公司会为了哪怕一个最小报价单位剥头皮，一直剥到多头趋势的最高那个最小报价单位。最高点总是位于一个阻力位，许多高频交易公司会在阻力位下方一两个最小报价单位处买入，试图抓住最后那个最小报价单位，前提是它们的系统显示这是一个盈利策略。另一些机构买入是为了在另一个市场（股票、期权、债券、外汇等）中建立对冲，因为它们认为通过建立这个对冲能改善自己的风险回报比。成交量不是来自个体小交易者，因为在主要转折点处，他们贡献的交易量不到5%。


> If institutions are smart, profitable, and responsible for every tick, why would they ever buy the highest tick in a bull trend (or sell the lowest tick in a bear trend)? It is because that is what their algorithms have been doing profitably all of the way up, and some are designed to continue to do it until it is clear that the bull trend is no longer in effect. They lose on that final buy, but make enough on all of their earlier trades to offset that loss. Remember, all of their systems lose between 30 and 70 percent of the time, and this is one of those times. There are also HFT firms that will scalp for even a single tick right up to the high tick of a bull trend. The high is always at a resistance level, and many HFT firms will buy a tick or two below resistance to try to capture that final tick, if their systems show that this is a profitable strategy. Other institutions are buying as part of a hedge in another market (stocks, options, bonds, currencies, etc.) because they perceive that their risk/reward ratio is better by placing the hedge. The volume is not from small individual traders, because they are responsible for less than 5 percent of the volume at major turning points.


市场越双边，每一次突破和回调就越可能同时有机构空头和机构多头在建仓（而不是像强劲急速行情中的第一次回调那样只有一方在止盈）。它们这样做是基于经过测试、并被证明长期盈利的策略。涉及的资金有数亿美元之巨，所以每一处都被严格审视、都必须有效。这些资金的所有者会要求交易有稳妥的数学基础，否则他们就会把资金转给一家交易有数学基础的公司。当市场大多是双边成交时——大多数时候都是如此——每一次突破和每一次回调都有买方和卖方在入场，而既然机构是盈利的，它们就都在使用盈利的策略，即使其中许多策略的成功概率只有40%或更低。


> The more two-sided the market is, the more likely every breakout and pullback has both institutional bears and bulls initiating trades (rather than one side simply taking profits, like in the first pullback in a strong spike). They are doing so based on strategies that they have tested and shown to be profitable over time. Hundreds of millions of dollars are at stake, so everything is closely scrutinized and has to be effective. The people who own that money will demand that the trading have a sound mathematical basis, or else they will move it to a firm whose trading does. When there is mostly two-sided trading going on, which is most of the time, there are buyers and sellers entering on every breakout and every pullback, and since institutions are profitable, all of them are using profitable strategies, even though many have probabilities of success of 40 percent or less.


在强劲多头急速行情中那次单根K线回调的例子里，如果价格突破那根K线的高点，那主要是急于加大赌注的多头在加仓多头或新建多头造成的。他们从愿意卖出的人手里买入，而那些卖方是多头止盈者（他们买得更低）和开始做空的激进空头这两者的组合。起初，空头只会是剥头皮交易者，他们只预期小幅回调。一些高频交易公司会为了仅仅一两个最小报价单位的利润剥头皮，而且往往存在一个高概率的建仓形态让它们这样做，即使是在强趋势中一根强势的高1买入信号K线上方。许多公司使用的是基于最小报价单位图的算法，那些图能显示5分钟图上不可见的微小形态。随着市场变得更加双边、交易区间开始形成，空头会开始卖出上涨行情（有些会在市场走高时分批建仓），比如在区间或通道顶部的弱势高1或高2买入信号K线上方卖出，并打算持有一段下跌行情。市场越双边，越多的空头开始做波段，越多的多头停止做波段、开始剥头皮。最终大多数做波段的多头都会已经止盈，那时大多数多头就都是剥头皮交易者了。当买入信号K线变得更弱时，剥头皮交易者对买入失去兴趣，因为概率下降了，他们只做高概率的交易。一旦多头剥头皮交易者和大多数做波段的多头停止买入，而做空更多是由做波段的空头而不是空头剥头皮交易者进行时，趋势就反转了。


> In the example of that one-bar pullback in the strong bull spike, if there is a breakout above the high of that bar, it will be mostly due to eager bulls who are pressing their bets as they add to their longs or initiate new longs. They are buying from someone willing to sell, and those sellers are a combination of profit taking bulls who bought lower and aggressive bears who are beginning to short. Initially, the bears will only be scalpers, expecting only small pullbacks. Some HFT firms will scalp for a profit of only a tick or two, and there is often a high probability setup that will allow them to do so, even above a strong high 1 buy signal bar in a strong trend. Many are using algorithms based on tick charts, which can show tiny patterns that are invisible on the 5 minute chart. As the market becomes more two-sided and a trading range begins to develop, bears will begin to sell rallies (some will scale in as the market goes higher), like above weak high 1 or high 2 buy signal bars at the top of the range or channel, and look to hold for a swing down. The more two-sided the market becomes, the more bears begin to swing and the more bulls stop swinging and begin to scalp. Eventually most of the swing trading bulls will have taken their profits, at which point most of bulls will be scalpers. When the buy signal bars become weaker, scalpers lose interest in buying because the probability drops, and they will only take high probability trades. Once the bull scalpers and most of the swing bulls stop buying, and the shorting is being done more by swing trading bears than bear scalpers, the trend reverses.


即使市场正在进入交易区间，仍然有一些多头在买入那些低概率（大约40%）的买入建仓形态，比如区间顶部的弱势高1和高2信号K线。他们是运行算法的波段交易者，那些算法已被证明在长期里做这类低概率波段交易是能盈利的。他们知道，随着市场越来越成为一个交易区间，成功概率正在下降。但他们也知道自己的系统是盈利的，即使成功概率只有40%或更低。他们的一部分赢家会比自己的止损大好几倍，足以远超他们在60%的时候经历的那些亏损。他们的程序还能在更低的位置分批建仓，而且更低位置的那些入场可以更大。这样，如果他们认为自己最初的判断不再成立、想要退出这笔交易，他们就能以保本、甚至带着一点小利出场。在大多数日子里，你靠在交易区间或弱势多头通道顶部的那个糟糕的高1买入信号K线的高点做空来赚钱。然而，每个月总有几天，市场会强劲上涨并形成一连串低概率的买入信号K线（比如用十字星或空头趋势K线当信号K线），而每一根之后都跟着一波巨大的上涨行情，回报是风险的许多倍。在这些日子里，那些买入这些低概率建仓形态的波段交易程序能赚到一笔财富，足以弥补所有那些小损失。另一方面，剥头皮交易者往往错过这些趋势的很大一部分，因为他们不愿意交易低概率的建仓形态。当市场强劲上涨时，大多数剥头皮交易者会看到这种强势，避免在弱势买入信号K线上方做空。他们知道在多头趋势的顶部卖出是有风险的。“有风险”只是说交易者等式很糟糕，而逆着趋势交易的风险在于：任何一个低概率的顺势建仓形态都可能带来一波巨大的行情。低概率通常是高回报的另一面，正如高概率通常意味着回报很小（一次剥头皮）。因为他们看到了多头趋势，所以他们想做多。然而，由于买入信号看起来弱，因此这些是概率相对较低的建仓形态。结果剥头皮交易者最终没有买入，错过了一段可能持续几小时、覆盖许多点的趋势。剥头皮交易者会等待更深的回调来买入，偶尔会买入一次他认为会有一两根K线后续行情的强突破，但在这种趋势日里，他赚到的钱会远少于波段交易者。而在大多数其他日子里，一个好的剥头皮交易者会比一个波段交易者赚到更多的钱。记住，既然剥头皮交易者做的是高概率交易，而且因为他的利润目标更小、有远多于波段交易者的建仓形态可选，那么理论上他就拥有远多于波段交易者的盈利交易，这意味着更平滑的资金曲线和更多赚钱的日子。


> Even when the market is entering a trading range, there are still some bulls buying those low probability (around 40 percent) buy setups like the weak high 1 and high 2 signal bars at the top of the range. They are swing traders running algorithms that have been proven to be profitable over time when taking these low probability swing trades. They know that the probability of success is falling as the market becomes more of a trading range. However, they also know that their systems are profitable, even if the probability of success is 40 percent or less. Some of their winners will be many times larger than their stops, more than making up for the losers that they experience 60 percent of the time. Their programs can also scale in lower, and their lower entries can be larger. This enables them to get out at breakeven or even with a small profit, if they consider their initial premise to be no longer valid and they want to get out of the trade. On most days, you win by shorting the high of that bad high 1 buy signal bar at the top of a trading range or weak bull channel. However, there are a few days a month when the market will trend up strongly and create a series of low probability buy signal bars (like dojis or bear trend bars for signal bars), and each one will be followed by a huge rally where the reward is many times greater than the risk. On these days, those swing trading programs that buy these low probability setups can make a fortune that is great enough to more than make up for all of those little losses. The scalpers, on the other hand, often miss much of these trends, because they are unwilling to trade the low probability setups. When the market is trending up strongly, most scalpers will see the strength and avoid shorting above weak buy signal bars. They know that selling at the top of a bull trend is risky. “Risky” simply means that the trader's equation is bad, and the risk from trading against a trend is that any low probability with trend setup can result in a huge move. Low probability is usually the flip side of high reward, just as high probability usually means that the reward is small (a scalp). Because they see the bull trend, they want to buy. However, since the buy signals look weak, they therefore are relatively low probability setups. The scalper then ends up not buying, and missing a trend that can last for hours and cover many points. The scalper will wait for deeper pullbacks to buy, and will occasionally buy a strong breakout that he thinks will have follow-through for a bar or so, but he will make far less money on this type of trend day than will a swing trader. A good scalper will make more money than a swing trader on most other days. Remember, since the scalper is taking high probability trades and has far more setups to choose from because his profit goal is smaller, he theoretically has far more profitable trades than the swing trader, which means a smoother equity curve and more profitable days.


每当你交易一个低概率系统，这个系统的交易者等式为正，但在任何单笔交易上获胜的机会都很小。每一笔单独的交易成功机会都小，但如果你把所有建仓形态都做了，这一组的交易者等式就是正的。这意味着你不能在那些成功概率低的交易里挑挑拣拣，不管回报比风险大多少。人们有一种离奇的本事，能把所有的坏樱桃都挑出来、一个好樱桃都挑不到，还常常错过那笔用来弥补此前亏损所必需的关键交易。他们最终说服自己不去做那些能带来巨额利润的低概率交易，却把所有的输家都做了，因为那些看起来总是更容易下手。结果是他们亏钱。要交易一个低概率系统，你必须做每一个强信号，因为如果你挑挑拣拣，你几乎必然会挑错，而且常常会错过那笔你用来弥补此前亏损所必需的关键交易。大多数交易者通常无法做到每笔交易都做。这让他们暴露在这个风险之下，也使低概率交易很难做到盈利。


> Whenever you trade a low probability system, the system has a positive trader's equation, but the chances of winning on any one trade are small. Each individual trade has a small chance of success, but if you take all of the setups, the trader's equation for the group is positive. This means that you cannot cherry pick among trades that have a low probability of success, no matter how much larger the reward is than the risk. People have an uncanny ability to pick all of the bad cherries and none of the good ones, and often miss that one great trade that is needed to overcome their earlier losses. They end up talking themselves out of taking the low probability trades that result in huge profits, and into taking all of the losers, which always look easier to take. The result is that they lose money. To trade a low probability system, you have to take every strong signal, because if you cherry pick, you will invariably pick the wrong cherries, and will often miss that one great trade that you need to overcome your earlier losses. Most traders are usually unable to take every trade. This exposes them to this risk, and makes low probability trading so difficult to trade profitably.


另一个极端是高概率交易，交易者牺牲回报的大小，去换取每一笔交易都高得多的获胜机会。如果一个系统的概率是60%或更高，而且回报至少与风险一样大，那么每一笔单独的交易都有正的交易者等式。交易者不需要用一大堆其他交易来平均，才能盈利。每一笔交易的交易者等式都是正的，所以交易者想怎么挑都行，仍然能赚钱，即使连续错过10笔好交易也没关系。如果一个交易者错过了许多交易，但成功做上了几笔高概率交易，他盈利的机会仍然不错。正因为这种不做每一笔交易的自然倾向，如果交易者发现自己在波段交易中挑挑拣拣，他们应该考虑：大多数交易者应当把重点放在做更多高概率交易上。事实上，我有一个朋友交易十年期美国国债期货，他想要每笔交易的风险尽可能小。为了做到这一点，他在一张50个最小报价单位的图上交易，图上许多K线只有两个最小报价单位高，并且每笔交易只打算冒三四个最小报价单位的风险。他争取每笔交易赚到八个或更多最小报价单位，而且由于他读图非常厉害，他有90%的胜率——至少他是这么告诉我的。我猜想这意味着他并不是每笔交易都能达到八个最小报价单位的目标，而且他的许多赢家只赚一两个最小报价单位。如果他觉得亏10%和赢90%是一回事，他甚至可能把保本的交易也算进赢的那一栏。不管怎样，他的重点是风险，他假设只要自己仔细挑选交易，胜率和回报会自己照顾自己。


> At the other extreme is high probability trading, where a trader sacrifices the size of his reward for a much higher chance of winning on every trade. If a system has a probability of 60 percent or higher and a reward that is at least as large as its risk, then every individual trade has a positive trader's equation. Traders don't need to average every trade with a bunch of other trades to be profitable. Each trade has a positive trader's equation, so traders can cherry pick all they want and still make money, and it does not matter if they miss 10 good trades in a row. If a trader misses many trades, but manages to take a few high probability trades, his chance of being profitable is still good. Because of this natural tendency to not take every trade, if traders find themselves cherry picking among swing trades, they should consider that most traders should focus on taking more high probability trades. I, in fact, have a friend who trades the 10-Year U.S. Treasury Note Futures, and he wants the smallest possible risk on each trade. To achieve that, he trades a 50 tick chart where many of the bars are only two ticks tall, and looks to risk just three or four ticks on each trade. He tries to make eight or more ticks on his trades and, since he is a very good chart reader, he wins on 90 percent of his trades, or so he told me. I assume that means he does not necessarily reach his eight-tick target on all of his trades, and that many of his winners have just a tick or two of profit. He might even count his breakeven trades in his win column if he thinks that losing on 10 percent is the same as winning on 90 percent. In any case, his emphasis is on risk and he assumes that his winning percentage and his reward will take care of themselves if he picks his trades carefully.


一家高频交易公司也许每天在几千只股票构成的篮子上做几十万笔交易，而这些交易基于统计，而不是基本面。举例来说，如果一家公司发现，当一只股票连续六个最小报价单位下跌时，卖出一波一个最小报价单位的上涨行情、赚一个最小报价单位、冒三个最小报价单位的风险是有利可图的，它也许就会把这当成自己的程序之一。你觉得它们的策略到底有多有效？它们有最聪明的数学家在设计和测试这些策略，所以你大概会以为，它们肯定得有70%或更高的胜率。但我严重怀疑事实并非如此，因为它们的程序要和其它公司的算法竞争，那么大的优势极不可能持续很长时间而不被其它公司发现并中和掉。一切都是权衡，它们的目标是拥有一个极其可靠的系统，几乎每天都靠它赚钱。如果一家公司每天做50万笔交易、每笔都只追求一到两个最小报价单位的利润，我怀疑它做不到在70%的交易上获胜。我怀疑的原因是：优势是短暂而微小的，每天要找到50万笔成功概率70%的交易，可能性极其之低。我猜它们的胜率是55%或更低。记住，一家赌场的优势只有大约3%，可赌场每天都在赚钱。这怎么可能？如果你有99%的把握认为你的优势是真的，而游戏会被玩上几千次，数学就会以压倒性的优势倾向于你会赢。高频交易公司也是这样。它接受一个很小的优势和相对较大的风险，来换取稳定的利润。如果那家高频交易公司去交易70%确定的建仓形态，它赚的钱不是更多吗？如果它能用数学证明那些建仓形态真的有70%的把握，那显然会更多。这意味着它做不到，但这并不代表这些建仓形态不存在。它们存在，但它们带有主观性，而且显然极难编成程序。这种主观性给了个体交易者一种优势。如果他们培养出做出主观判断的能力、以及不犯很多错误的能力，他们就有了优势。在这么多聪明人参与交易的情况下，优势永远都会很小、很主观，也永远会很难持续从中获利；但它是可以做到的，而这是每个交易者的目标。


> A high-frequency trading firm might place hundreds of thousands of trades every day on a basket of several thousand stocks, and the trades are based on statistics rather than fundamentals. For example, if a firm found that it is profitable to sell a one-tick rally for a one-tick profit and a three-tick risk when a stock falls on six consecutive ticks, they might use that as one of their programs. Just how effective do you think their strategies are? They have the smartest mathematicians designing and testing them, so you'd think that they surely have to win 70 percent of the time or more. I seriously doubt that is the case, though, because their programs are competing against algorithms at other firms, and it is highly unlikely that an edge that large could last more than a very short time before other firms spot it and neutralize it. Everything is a trade-off, and their goal is to have an extremely reliable system with which they will make money almost every day. If a firm is making 500,000 trades a day, trying for a one-or two-tick profit on each trade, I doubt it is winning on 70 percent of its trades. I doubt it because edges are fleeting and small and it is extremely unlikely that they could find 500,000 trades every day where the chance of success is 70 percent. I suspect that their winning percentage is 55 percent or less. Remember, a casino's edge is about 3 percent, yet casinos make money every day. How can that be? If you are 99 percent certain that your edge is real, and the game is played thousands of times, the math overwhelmingly favors that you will win. The same is true for a high-frequency trading firm. It is accepting a small edge and a relatively large risk in exchange for consistent profits. Wouldn't the HFT firm make more money if it traded setups that are 70 percent certain? Obviously it would, if it could prove mathematically that the setups actually were 70 percent certain. This means that it cannot, but that does not mean that these setups don't exist. They do, but they are subjective and obviously very difficult to program. This subjectivity gives individual traders an edge. If they develop the ability to make subjective judgments and the ability to not make many mistakes, they have an edge. With so many smart people trading, edges are always going to be small and subjective, and it will always be very difficult to consistently capitalize on them; but it can be done and it is the goal of every trader.


你入场越早，能赚到的利润就越多，但你的成功概率就更低。有些交易者更喜欢高胜率，如果能更确定自己的交易会盈利，他们愿意稍微晚一点入场。举例来说，如果市场有可能正在反转向上，一个交易者也许会买入。另一个交易者也许会等两根强劲的多头趋势K线和明确的始终做多买入信号出现之后再买入。这笔交易更确定，但由于错过了一部分行情，这个交易者能赚到的钱更少。他用一部分潜在利润为更好的概率付了钱，因为他相信这是一个划算的权衡。有些交易者对非常高的胜率感觉更踏实，即使这意味着他们在这笔交易上赚得更少。另一些交易者更喜欢远大于风险的潜在回报，即使这意味着他们可能只在40%的时候获胜。成功概率越高，建仓形态就越明显。当一个建仓形态特别明显时，许多聪明的交易者都会做它，而这种不平衡只会持续一两根K线。市场会很快到达预期目标，然后要么反转，要么进入交易区间。这就是为什么最好的剥头皮机会利润潜力有限、但成功概率很高。然而，既然大多数交易者无法持续只挑出高概率的剥头皮机会，他们就应该坚持做潜在回报至少与风险一样大、概率大约60%的交易。


> The earlier you enter, the more profit you stand to make, but your probability of success is less. Some traders prefer a higher winning percentage, and they are willing to enter a little later if they can be more certain that their trade will be profitable. For example, if the market might be reversing up, a trader might buy. Another trader might wait for a couple of strong bull trend bars and a clear always-in long buy signal before buying. The trade is more certain, but the trader, having missed part of the move, stands to make less. The trader paid for the better odds with some of the potential profit, in the belief that it was a good trade-off. Some traders feel more comfortable with a very high winning percentage, even if that means that they make less on the trade. Other traders prefer a potential reward that is many times greater than the risk, even if that means that they might win only 40 percent of the time. The higher the probability of success, the more obvious the setup is. When a setup is particularly obvious, a lot of smart traders will take it, and the imbalance will last for only a bar or two. The market will quickly reach the expected target and then either reverse or enter a trading range. That is why the best scalps have limited profit potential but a high probability of success. However, since most traders are unable to consistently pick only the high-probability scalps, they should stick to trades where the potential reward is at least as great as the risk and the probability is about 60 percent.


在任何一个给定时刻，回报、风险和概率都有数不清的可能组合，而交易者需要有一个清晰的计划。如果他们实际上打算赚一个点就出场，他们就不能把“冒两个点风险赚两个点”的概率拿来用。要让一笔交易在数学上稳妥，所需要的最低概率，对这两笔交易来说是不同的，而交易者在过于急切地想入场时，有时会把两种情形搞混。这是初学者常犯的问题，但这也是通往爆仓的一条确定的路。你需要从一笔好交易里赚到尽可能多的钱，因为在一笔糟糕的交易上你总是会亏掉可能的最大值，而你需要那些大利润来弥补这些亏损。


> At any given moment, there are countless possible combinations of reward, risk, and probability, and traders need to have a clear plan. They cannot use the probability of making two points while risking two points if they really are planning on exiting with a one-point profit. The minimum probability needed to make a trade mathematically sound is different for the two trades, and traders sometimes will mix the two scenarios up if they are overly eager to take a trade. This is a common problem for traders starting out, but it is a sure path to a blown account. You need to get the most you can out of a good trade, because you will always lose the most possible on a bad one, and you need the big profits to make up for those losses.


有没有成功概率达到90%或更高的情形？有一种情形出现在每一笔交易上，而且是某个盈利策略的一部分。举例来说，如果你持有多头，市场触及了你止盈的限价单但没有成交，你至少会短暂地继续持有多头，因为你觉得你的单子很可能很快就会被成交。你的止损也许在前一根K线低点下方，大约六个最小报价单位之外。你要继续持有多头去多赚那一个最小报价单位的利润，同时冒着六个最小报价单位的风险，这意味着你至少在那个瞬间认为自己有90%的成功概率。如果你继续持有仓位，那你就是相信“很可能”你的单子会在止损被打到之前成交。虽然大多数交易者从不思考实际的数学，但如果成功概率不是大约90%，他们就无法继续认为这笔交易是好的。而在那一刻，他们是对的。如果市场迅速回调三个最小报价单位，那么你此时是在试图朝着限价单赚三个最小报价单位的同时，朝着止损冒三个最小报价单位的风险，你就不再是90%那么确定了。


> Is there ever a situation where the probability of success is 90 percent or higher? One occurs on every trade and is a part of a profitable strategy. For example, if you are long and the market touches your profit taking limit order but does not fill it, you will still hold long, at least briefly, because you think that the chances are good that your order will be filled very soon. Your stop might be below the low of the prior bar, about six ticks away. For you to continue to hold long for that one extra tick of profit while risking six ticks means that you believe, at least at that moment, that you have a 90 percent chance of success. If you hold onto your position, then you believe that “chances are” that your order will be filled before your stop is hit. Although most traders never think about the actual math, they cannot continue to think that the trade is good unless the probability of success is about 90 percent. They are right, at least at that instant. If the market quickly pulls back three ticks, you are then risking three ticks to your stop as you try to make three ticks to your limit order, and you are no longer 90 percent certain.


还有另一种情形，交易者可以对一波行情有90%或更高的把握，但它不是一笔明智的交易。举例来说，在一天中的任何时候，市场很可能有95%的确定性会先上涨一个最小报价单位、再下跌200个最小报价单位；同样有95%的确定性会先下跌一个最小报价单位、再上涨200个最小报价单位。然而，无论成功概率有多高，你都不会为了赚一个最小报价单位而去冒200个最小报价单位的风险。一次亏损就会抹掉200次的赢，这意味着仅仅为了打平，你就需要99.5%的成功概率，而且你还得连续200次做到完美执行。


> There is another situation where a trader can be 90 percent or more certain of a move, but it is not a sensible trade. For example, at any time in the day, there is likely a 95 percent certainty that the market will go up one tick before it goes down 200 ticks and a 95 percent certainty that it will go down one tick before it goes up 200 ticks. However, you would never risk 200 ticks to make one tick, no matter what the odds of success were. One loss would wipe out 200 winners, which means that you need a 99.5 percent chance of success just to break even, and you would have to execute flawlessly 200 times in a row.


同样，有没有成功概率只有10%、却仍然稳妥的数学策略呢？有。举例来说，如果市场处于强劲的空头趋势中，从更高的低点向上走出了一波上涨行情，但现在又跌下来了，交易者可以在比前一个低点高一个最小报价单位处挂限价单买入，保护性止损设低一个最小报价单位。成功概率也许只有10%，但如果市场强劲反转向上，他们冒半个点的风险可能赚到10个点。这意味着，如果他们把这样的交易做上10次，9次亏损可能亏掉18个最小报价单位，1次获胜赚到40个最小报价单位，平均每笔交易赚2.2个最小报价单位。


> Likewise, is there ever a sound mathematical strategy where the chance of success is only 10 percent? Yes, for example, if the market is in a strong bear trend and has a rally up from a higher low but is now falling again, traders might place limit orders to buy at one tick above the earlier low and protective stops one tick lower. The chance of success might be only 10 percent, but if the market has a strong reversal up, they might make 10 points on their half-point risk. This means that if they took the trade 10 times, they might lose 18 ticks on their nine losers and make 40 ticks on their one win, and have an average profit per trade of 2.2 ticks.


记住，你关于是否做一笔交易的决定，需要把概率、风险和回报都考虑进去，而不只是其中一个或两个变量。一般来说，每当一笔交易的概率非常高时，你就应该把其中大部分或全部作为剥头皮来做。这是因为极端高概率的情形不会持续超过一两根K线，市场就会把它们纠正过来。如果某件事看起来非常确定，你基本可以肯定它不会持续得足够久、让你能做一笔波段交易。成功的机会越低，回报相对于风险就必须越大。最佳交易是成功机会在60%或以上、而回报至少与风险一样大、最好是大约两倍的交易。这类交易在大多数市场里每天都会出现，但你必须在建仓形态形成之前就预判到位，在它一旦形成后立刻做进去，并且管理好它。


> Remember, your decision about whether to take a trade needs to incorporate probability, risk, and reward, and not just one or two of the variables. In general, whenever the probability of a trade is very high, you should trade most or all of it as a scalp. This is because extremely high-probability situations will not last more than a bar or two before the market corrects them. If something seems very certain, you can be fairly sure that it won't last long enough for a swing trade. The lower the chance of success, the greater the reward has to be relative to the risk. The best trades are trades where the chance of success is 60 percent or more, and the reward is at least as large as the risk and preferably about twice as big. These trades occur every day in most markets, but you have to anticipate them before they set up, and you have to take them once they do set up, and manage them well.


一旦你找到一个建仓形态，接下来你就必须判断这笔交易该不该做。这个决定建立在一个需要三项输入的数学计算上：风险、回报和概率。可惜，人们有一种只考虑概率的自然倾向。


> Once you find a setup, you next must decide whether you should take the trade. The decision is based on a mathematical calculation that requires three inputs: risk, reward, and probability. Unfortunately, there is a natural tendency to consider only the probability.


许多初学交易者会看到一个他们认为有60%机会成为一次成功剥头皮的建仓形态，他们也许是对的，但他们仍然亏钱。这怎么可能？因为决定不能只建立在概率上。你必须考虑你能赚到多少，以及为了赚到这些你必须冒多少风险。记住，你需要成功概率乘以回报大于失败概率乘以风险。举例来说，如果你今天在看 Emini 图，在一个强劲空头市场里看到一个位于下跌的移动平均线正下方的低2，并且你根据自己的经验判断：做空它，有大约70%的概率在两个点的止损被打到之前先让两个点的止盈限价单成交，那么你就有70%的概率赚两个点、30%的概率亏两个点。如果你把这样的交易做上10次，你会赚到7 × 2 = 14个点，亏掉3 × 2 = 6个点。这10笔交易的净利润是14 – 6 = 8个点，所以每笔交易平均赚0.8个点，也就是40美元。如果你的佣金很低，往返大约5.00美元，那么实际每笔交易平均利润大约是35美元。这听起来也许不多，但如果你每天能做两次这样的交易、并且交易25张合约，那就是每天大约1,700美元、一年大约350,000美元。


> Many beginning traders will see a setup that they feel has a 60 percent chance of being a successful scalp, and they may be right, but they still lose money. How can that be? It is because the decision has to be based on more than just probability. You have to consider how much you stand to gain and how much you have to risk to achieve that gain. Remember, you need the probability of success times the reward to be greater than the probability of failure times the risk. For example, if you are watching the Emini today and see a low 2 just below the falling moving average in a strong bear market, and you decide from your experience that shorting it has about a 70 percent chance of leading to a two-point profit target limit order being filled before a two-point stop is hit, then you have a 70 percent chance of making two points and a 30 percent chance of losing two points. If you take this type of trade 10 times, you will make 7 × 2 = 14 points and you will lose 3 × 2 = 6 points. Your net profit for the 10 trades is 14 – 6 = 8 points, so your average profit is 0.8 point, or $40, per trade. If you have low commissions of about $5.00 round turn, then your actual average profit is about $35 per trade. That might not sound like much, but if you can do that twice a day and trade 25 contracts, that is about $1,700 a day and about $350,000 a year.


如果你改用两个点的止损和四个点的止盈目标，做一笔你认为好过50–50的赌注的交易，我们还是只用50%的概率来算一遍。如果你做10笔交易，你会在其中5笔上赚四个点，共20个点的利润。你会在另外5笔上亏两个点，共亏损10个点。那么净利润就是10笔交易10个点，每笔交易平均利润大约一个点。如果扣掉0.1个点的佣金，你每笔交易平均大约45美元。显然，会有很多交易在触及你的止损或止盈目标之前就退出了，但可以合理地假设这些交易大致会互相抵消，所以这个公式在指导你选择交易上是有用的。如果你对建仓形态非常挑剔，只做有70%成功机会的交易，那么做10笔你会赚到7 × 4 = 28个点，亏掉3 × 2 = 6个点。扣掉佣金后，每笔交易平均利润大约2.1个点。


> If instead you use a two-point stop and a four-point profit target and take a trade that you think is better than a 50–50 bet, let's still do the math using only a 50 percent probability. If you take 10 trades, you will win four points on five of those trades for 20 points of profit. You will lose two points on the other five trades for a 10-point loss. Your net profit then is 10 points in 10 trades and your average profit is about one point per trade. If you subtract out 0.1 point for your commission, you will average about $45 per trade. Obviously, there will be lots of trades that you will exit before your stop or profit target is hit, but it is reasonable to assume that those will approximately offset each other and therefore this formula is useful in guiding you in your trade selection. If you are very selective in your setups and take only trades that have a 70 percent chance of success, if you take 10 trades you will make 7 × 4 = 28 points and lose 3 × 2 = 6 points. Your profit after commissions will average about 2.1 points per trade.


虽然你可以尝试用市价单出场，但大多数使用止盈目标的交易者都用限价单出场，而且会在他们精确的价格上成交。你可以通过选择保护性止损和止盈目标来控制风险和回报。如果你选择使用10个最小报价单位的止损，在大多数情况下这就是你的风险。你有时会遇到明显的滑点，尤其是在流动性更稀薄的市场里，你也必须把它算进去。举例来说，如果你在交易一只小盘股，而这只股票的止损单通常有大约10美分的滑点，并且你使用50美分的保护性止损，那么你的风险大约是60美分加上你的佣金。如果你交易 Emini，而且你不是在一份报告发布之前刚刚入场，你通常不会有滑点，但你仍然会有大约0.1个点的佣金。


> Although you could try to exit using a market order, most traders who use profit targets exit on limit orders and will be filled at their exact price. You can control the risk and reward by your selection of a protective stop and a profit target. If you choose to use a 10-tick stop, that is your risk in most cases. You will sometimes encounter significant slippage, especially in thinner markets, and you have to factor that in as well. For example, if you are trading a small-cap stock and usually have about 10 cents of slippage on stop orders in that stock, and you are using a 50 cent protective stop, then your risk is about 60 cents plus your commission. If you trade the Emini and you are not entering just before a report, you usually will not have slippage but you will still have a commission that will be about 0.1 point.


这个等式里最困难的部分，是评估你的止盈限价单在保护性止损被打到之前成交的概率。虽然风险和潜在回报你都清楚，因为那是你自己选的，但概率永远不可能被精确地知道。不过，你往往能做出一个有根据的估计。如果你对自己的估计没有信心，就用50%，因为不确定意味着市场处于交易区间中，上涨的概率与下跌的概率大致相同。


> The most difficult part of the equation is assessing the probability that your profit-taking limit order will be filled before your protective stop is hit. Although you know the risk and potential reward because you chose them, it is impossible to ever know the probability precisely. However, you can often make an educated guess. If you don't have any confidence in your guess, just use 50 percent since uncertainty means that the market is in a trading range and the probability of a move up is about the same as for a move down.


然而，如果你是在强劲多头趋势中买入一次两段式回调到移动平均线的顶部，成功概率也许是70%。如果你反而是在一个强劲空头市场中，买入一个刚好处在移动平均线下方的交易区间的顶部，你的成功概率也许只有30%。这意味着如果你做10笔交易，你会亏掉7 × 2 = 14个点。既然你只有三个赢家，那这些赢家必须平均每笔赚五个点才能打平！由于这极不可能，你几乎不应该考虑这笔交易。


> However, if you are buying at the top of a two-legged pullback to the moving average in a strong bull trend, the probability of success might be 70 percent. If instead you are buying in a strong bear market at the top of a trading range that is just below the moving average, your probability of success might only be 30 percent. That means that if you take 10 trades, you will lose 7 × 2 = 14 points. Since you have only three winners, those winners have to average five points each just to break even! As that is extremely unlikely, you should rarely consider this trade.


如果你做一笔交易，是因为相信自己有60%的概率在亏掉10个最小报价单位之前先赚到10个最小报价单位，但随后几根K线里市场进入了一个窄幅交易区间，那么你的成功概率现在已经降到大约50%。既然在成功概率只有50%的时候，冒10个最小报价单位去赚10个最小报价单位已经是一个亏损策略，你就应该尽可能接近保本地退出这笔交易。如果你运气好，也许还能赚一两个最小报价单位。这是交易管理的一部分。市场随着每一个最小报价单位而变化，如果一个成功的策略突然变成了亏损策略，就出场，不要指望靠希望。一旦你的原始判断不再成立，就出场，然后去寻找另一笔交易。你必须交易你当下拥有的市场，而不是几分钟之前的市场，也不是你希望接下来几分钟会出现的那一个。交易里没有希望的位置。你是在与没有情绪、冷冰冰地客观的计算机对抗，你也必须那样。


> If you take a trade because you believe that you have a 60 percent probability of making 10 ticks before losing 10 ticks but then over the next few bars the market enters a tight trading range, your probability of success has now fallen to about 50 percent. Since it is now a losing strategy to risk 10 ticks to make 10 ticks if the chance of success is only 50 percent, you should exit the trade as close to breakeven as possible. If you are lucky, you might even be able to make a tick or two. This is part of trade management. The market changes with each tick, and if a successful strategy suddenly becomes a losing strategy, get out and don't rely on hope. Once your premise is no longer workable, just exit and look for another trade. You have to trade the market that you now have and not the one that you had a few minutes ago and not the one you hope will develop over the next few minutes. Hope has no part in trading. You are trading against computers that have no emotion and are coldly objective, and that is how you have to be as well.


那么，在 Emini 中用止损单入场、做赚一个点的剥头皮，怎么样？如果你冒两个点的风险去赚一个点，那么仅仅为了打平，你就必须赢的次数是输的两倍。如果你把佣金也算进去，那就需要70%的时候判断正确才能打平。想要盈利，你必须有80%或更多的时候判断正确；即使是大多数经验丰富、能盈利的交易者，长期也做不到这一点。那么你就必须得出这样的结论：这根本不是一个盈利策略。如果你这样做，长期下来你几乎必然会亏钱，而既然你交易时压倒一切的目标是持续赚钱，你就不能这样交易。没错，每天也许有几笔交易，在亏掉两个点之前赚到一个点的概率超过80%，如果你读图非常厉害、非常自律、能在下单前及时看准最好的建仓形态，并且把你赚一个点的剥头皮限制在这几笔建仓形态上，那么理论上你可以赚到很多钱。这可以是一个盈利策略，但所有这些“如果”构成的壁垒，对大多数交易者来说是无法逾越的。好得多的做法是寻找数量更少的交易，但那些交易只需要你判断正确50%到60%就能盈利。问题之一在于：在赚一个点的剥头皮上做到60%的胜率相当容易，而这个高胜率会强化你的行为，让你相信自己离成功已经非常近了。然而，那80%的要求对大多数交易者来说根本无法达到，不管他们靠得多近。


> So what about one-point scalps in the Emini where you are entering on stops? If you are risking two points to make one point, then you have to win twice as often as you lose just to break even. If you add in commissions, then you need to win 70 percent of the time to break even. To make a profit, you have to be right 80 percent or more of the time; even most experienced, profitable traders could not do that long-term. You then have to conclude that it is simply not a profitable strategy. If you do it, you will almost certainly lose over time, and since you have to be trading with the overriding goal of consistently making money, you cannot trade this way. Yes, there are probably a few trades a day where the probability of making one point before losing two points is more than 80 percent, and you could theoretically make a lot of money if you are a very good chart reader, if you are very disciplined, if you can spot the best setups in time to place the trades, and if you restrict your one-point scalps to those few setups. This can be a profitable strategy, but the barrier posed by all of those ifs is insurmountable for most traders. It is far better to look for fewer trades but those where you have to be right only 50 to 60 percent of the time to make a profit. One of the problems is that it is fairly easy to win on 60 percent of one-point scalps, and this high winning percentage reinforces your behavior and makes you believe that you are so close to being able to be successful. However, that 80 percent requirement is simply impossible to reach for most traders, no matter how close they get.


概率、风险和回报，随每一个时间级别上的每一笔交易、随着每一个最小报价单位而变化。举例来说，如果交易者们在 Emini 中买入一个高2牛旗，并认为它有60%的概率在亏两个点之前先赚两个点，那么三个变量都会随着每一个最小报价单位而变化。如果市场飞快上涨了六个最小报价单位，所有回调都只有一两个最小报价单位，那么他们最初判断成立的概率此时也许已有80%。既然他们只需要再涨四个最小报价单位就能剥到两个点的利润出场，他们的回报此时就是四个最小报价单位。他们也许会把保护性止损提高到当前K线低点下方一个最小报价单位处，甚至在这根K线收盘之前就这样做，而这也许只比他们的入场价低三个最小报价单位。这把原来那笔交易的风险降到了三个最小报价单位。他们现在也许有80%的概率在冒三个最小报价单位风险的同时赚到剩下的两个最小报价单位，这是一个极好的交易者等式。然而，如果他们此时是空仓、并且看到了这一切发生，他们不应该按市价买入去冒三个最小报价单位赚两个最小报价单位。一家做动量交易、支付极小佣金的机构可以盈利地做这笔交易，但个体交易者几乎必然会亏钱，因为他们无法足够快、足够准确地执行这笔交易，让它奏效。而且，在几乎所有回报不到一个点的交易上，佣金都会大大削弱盈利能力。每一刻都有交易者持有多头与空头仓位，带着你能想象到的各种风险、回报和概率组合。虽然日内交易者关心每一个最小报价单位，但一个根据日线图或周线图做交易的交易者会忽略小波动，因为它们太小，对交易者等式不会有什么明显影响。如果市场在入场之后没有立即上涨、反而下跌了四个最小报价单位，那么剥头皮交易者还剩四个最小报价单位的风险、而有12个最小报价单位的回报，这是一个极好的风险回报比，但概率会大幅下降，也许只有35%。这仍然是一个稳妥的策略，但长期盈利性远远不如从前。既然交易者等式仍然有利，交易者就不应该提前出场，除非原始判断已经改变、概率降到也许30%或更低。


> The probability, risk, and reward change for every trade on every time frame with each tick. For example, if traders bought a high 2 bull flag in the Emini and thought that it had a 60 percent chance of making two points before losing two points, all three variables change with every tick. If the market races up for six ticks with all of the pullbacks being only one or two ticks, the probability of their original premise being correct might now be 80 percent. Since they need only four more ticks to scalp out with two points of profit, their reward is now four ticks. They might raise their protective stops to one tick below the low of the current bar, even before the bar closes, and this might be only three ticks below their entry price. This reduces the risk of the original trade to three ticks. They now might have an 80 percent chance of making the remaining two ticks while risking three ticks, which is a great trader's equation. If they were flat and saw this happening, however, they should not buy at the market and risk three ticks to make two ticks. An institution that is trading momentum and paying minuscule commissions can profitably take that trade, but individual traders would almost certainly lose money because they could not execute the trade fast enough and correctly often enough to make it work. Also, commissions greatly reduce the profitability on almost all trades where the reward is less than one point. At every moment, there are traders holding long and short trades with every imaginable combination of risk, reward, and probability. Although a day trader is concerned with every tick, a trader trading off of the daily or weekly charts would ignore small movements, because they would be too small to have any significant impact on the trader's equation.
